comments.author: ntm-pane-17
comments.text:
2026-08-20 ntm:%17 current-byte static/type-structure audit. NO EDIT: all three diagnosed defects are already repaired at these bytes, so no bounded correction was necessary and no Agent Mail registration or reservation was taken. 1m load 14.03, so per instruction NO typecheck, Bun, Biome, or UBS was run. No stage/commit/close.

FROZEN CURRENT BYTES:
  apps/wire/src/krater/krater.test.ts  86e3ba1858459d4d0142b1b8fcb2eb6e0176bd431cf61d586cbbc4ec63bd4756
  apps/wire/src/krater/s2-client.ts    ad0472911ea93a5e0393b70afb2fb704b784aec5e13b564e43df104e28f29f75

THE THREE DIAGNOSED DEFECTS, RE-CHECKED INDEPENDENTLY:
  1. "krater.test.ts references an undefined chain_digest identifier instead of its chainDigest state" - REPAIRED. Every occurrence is now a property key or string content, never a bare identifier: :172 and :182 bind `chain_digest: chainDigest` from the real state, :97/:98 are the SQL substring and a null-head fixture, :300 is `chain_digest: eventBindings[4]`, :335 is `root_chain_digest: chainDigest`. No unresolved reference remains.
  2. "s2-client parser helpers return unknown or widened string values without exact runtime narrowing" - COMPILES, with a caveat recorded below. numberAt (:518-522), ownStringAt (:557-561) and stringAt (:583-587) each guard with a typeof/isFinite check and then return `value as <T>`. Casting from `unknown` is always legal, so these are not type errors.
  3. "the oldest-pending result uses possibly-null arithmetic" - REPAIRED. parseS2OutboxStatus narrows explicitly at :1343-1347: `const measuredAgeMs = result.oldest_pending_age_ms;` then `if (result.pending === 0 || measuredAgeMs === null) fail(...)` then `const exactMeasuredAgeMs = measuredAgeMs as number;` before the threshold comparison. The `number | null` value never reaches arithmetic unnarrowed.

STRUCTURAL FINDING THAT EXPLAINS ALL NINE CASTS (diagnostic, not a defect). s2-client.ts declares its refusal helper as `const fail = (code: string): never => { throw new Error(code); };` (:501-503). TypeScript applies control-flow narrowing to a never-returning call only when the called entity is a function declaration or a const with an EXPLICIT TYPE ANNOTATION ON THE VARIABLE. Here the annotation sits in the arrow's return position, not on `fail` itself. That is why nine `as number`/`as string`/`as boolean` casts exist in this file: they silence the compiler in place of narrowing it cannot perform.

CONSEQUENCE WORTH RECORDING: the casts, not the guards, are what satisfy the compiler. Invert or delete any `if (...) fail(...)` and `value as number` still compiles, emitting a mistyped value with no diagnostic. Type safety on this parser therefore rests entirely on the runtime plants, not on tsc.

SMALLEST FOLLOW-UP (deliberately NOT applied here, because it is an improvement rather than a fix for a red gate, and this bead's scope is "fix only the diagnosed names/narrowings"): annotate the variable - `const fail: (code: string) => never = (code) => { throw new Error(code); };` - after which all nine casts can be dropped and the guards become compiler-verified. That should be its own bead so the cast removal is reviewed as a deliberate change rather than smuggled into a typecheck repair.

PENDING GATE - THE ONLY THING BLOCKING CLOSURE. The acceptance criteria require the exact files to pass typecheck, Biome, focused tests, diff-check and scoped UBS. At 1m load 14.03 I was instructed not to run any of them, and I did not. This audit therefore establishes that the three diagnosed source defects are absent from these bytes; it does NOT establish that `bun run typecheck` is green, because a fourth, undiagnosed error elsewhere in the Wire project would still red the canonical gate. To close, re-run at load < 10 and record the result against exactly the two hashes above:
  bun run typecheck; bun run lint; cd apps/wire && bun run test; ubs --diff

BOUNDARY. Source-level and type-structural reading only (shasum, sed, grep) plus this bead comment. NO compiler was invoked and NO test was executed, so every statement about what does or does not typecheck is inference from the TypeScript narrowing rules and the declarations at the cited lines, not an observed tsc result. No local and no deployed evidence. Assignment moved to ntm:%17 per instruction; status unchanged; bead NOT closed.

title: W12.2 SP4D flagship + rung 6/7 frontier slate (famous-problem guardrail)
description:
WHY: Day-one visitors must also see a frontier worth joining — honest even if quiet for months. The flagship is also where R-21 ("AI solved a famous problem" virality outrunning verification) is most dangerous, so the guardrail ships with the problem from day one, not after the first scare. WHAT: sharpen the SP4D flagship (smooth 4-dimensional Poincare conjecture) with famous-problem guardrail framing: canonical formulation + explicit distinction from commonly conflated variants; authoritative references; a standing banner that no resolution will be displayed without extraordinary evidence; under-result-review status + external-expert review REQUIRED before any resolution-shaped status language appears anywhere including share cards (share honesty is a hard rule: cards always carry exact status — open / under result review / strongly supported / resolved with scope — never resolution-shaped language for unresolved work). Rich in bounded sub-goals (Gluck twists, trisection invariants) so arriving Fellows have real moves. Prepare the rung-6 frontier slate behind it: Kaplansky zero-divisor (live post-Gardam), union-closed sets (the post-Gilmer constant race — exactly review-shaped), Erdos-Straus, sums of three cubes for outstanding n, Sendov remaining degrees, lonely runner small-k, BB(6) lower-bound coordination (every result a verifiable artifact), quantum channel additivity counterexample hunting, and a strictly-bounded Navier-Stokes sub-question as the statement-gate stress test. Rung 7 (new-theory workshops) rules enforced by schema: explicit predictions, consistency checks, stated distinction from established theory — "explore vibes" is not a problem. Famous-problem guardrail applies from rung 6 up. DONE: flagship public with guardrail banner and sharpened statement (non-proposer statement-clear review recorded); frontier slate drafted with statements ready for post-launch publication. SCHEDULING NOTE: flagship statement drafting, reference gathering, and sub-goal decomposition may begin immediately in docs/seed/ (long-lead intellectual work); the bead is blocked only on the live guardrail + sharpening machinery.

AUTHORSHIP PATH: the operator may prepare the SP4D/frontier governance briefs and source dossiers, but an explicitly onboarded Fellow/session must deliberately adopt each exact scientific statement before the sponsor/steward publication gate. Platform screening or seed-import code never impersonates a Fellow.

QUALITY-SURFACE PREREQUISITE: source drafting remains parallel and ungated in W12.P2, but this live-publication bead waits for the full W9 screening, moves, roster, review-matchmaking, calibration and honors behavior. Frontier publication must not create a famous problem whose promised reviewer routing, safe moderation or bounded sub-goal moves are placeholders.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Source and external-expert review gates verify the SP4D formulation, variant distinctions, references, falsifier, extraordinary-evidence requirement, no-resolution phrasing, and each rung-6/7 dossier before publication. Unit/golden tests cover famous-problem status/share-card guardrails and seed schema; scripts/e2e-seed-frontier.sh publishes into staging, attempts premature resolution-shaped events, and verifies agent/human/share faces remain exact and scoped. The structured launch report records seed/source/render digests, reviewer role and independence, gate outcomes, rejected transitions, and residual no-claim boundary; never states that a famous problem is solved absent the full external gate.

title: W10.4 Auth race matrix on the real implementation
description:
WHY: S-1 proved the auth races on a prototype; the REAL Propylon implementation must hold the same guarantees, because one-time-exchange semantics and the two-plane seam are where quiet security bugs live. The invariant: exactly one credential outcome may ever commit, no matter how requests interleave. WHAT: race matrix against the real stack (local D1/miniflare bindings, no mocks): two simultaneous exchanges of one join code (secret is single-use, SHA-256 at rest); enrollment expiry racing approval; sponsor revocation racing an in-flight Fellow write (the write must lose); approval-page refresh double-POST (CSRF-protected, account-bound, idempotent outcome); device poll faster than interval (RFC 8628 slow_down semantics); loopback callback and server-poll both returning in asimp login (exactly one wins cleanly). Adjacent invariants proven here: pending proposals expire after 24h unapproved (independent of the 30-min join-secret TTL, which only gates STARTING a proposal); regenerating an unused join URL invalidates the predecessor; token revocation takes effect immediately (revocation-not-taking-effect is a named operator alert); WRONG_PRINCIPAL in both directions (bearer on a sponsor route, cookie on a.); flow-handle polling never accepts the bare proposal ID and the handle never appears in a query string; fragment secret provably absent from server logs (grep the log pipeline in the test). DONE: matrix green in CI with interleaving traces logged per race; exactly-one-commit assertions on every credential path.

ONE-TIME RESPONSE-LOSS GATE: include approval/poll response loss immediately before and after commit. The database may retain only the bearer hash plus a nonsecret issuance receipt/state; it must never retain or reconstruct a replayable secret. First authenticated use proves delivery. A repeated exchange after an ambiguous response returns the same nonsecret receipt with CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN, never the token and never a silently reminted replacement. Recovery is an explicit recent-auth sponsor revoke/rebind flow whose new credential outcome is independently audited. Race tests include simultaneous poll/retry/first-use/rebind and assert one active intended credential, immediate old-hash revocation, no unauthorized write window, and no secret in artifacts or logs.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: A table-driven harness enumerates enroll mint/propose/approve/reduce, token mint/revoke/write, service-envelope nonce, session open/resume/close and step-up races with deterministic barriers and repeatable seeds; unit tests validate scenario scheduling and oracle assertions. Mock-free staging executes every interleaving against real D1/DO/Auth boundaries, including disconnect-before/after-commit, and scripts/e2e-auth-races.sh reruns minimal failing schedules from artifact seeds. OPS.2a JSONL records scenario/seed/interleaving, revision/bindings, pseudonymous principals, request/event IDs, transaction and cursor states, status/code, retry, duration and assertion diff; never secrets, pairing codes, fragments, cookies, OAuth data, bearer tokens, signatures, bodies, or raw browser traces. The matrix explicitly includes lost credential responses, CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN, first-use delivery proof and sponsor revoke/rebind. Assertions inspect persistent state to prove hash-only storage, no plaintext/reversible credential capsule, no replay/remint, and exactly one intended active credential after every schedule.

description: WHY: content requiring a blocking safety decision must NEVER be briefly public while legitimate weird math must sail through, and refusals must not become an attacker iteration oracle. OWNERSHIP: this bead owns L0 structural validation, L1 ingest classifiers, quarantine-before-public mechanics, SSRF-safe enrichment, and the versioned screening record. W9.3b alone owns the higher-order analysis-versus-operational dual-use boundary, bounded cross-post aggregation, L2/L3 human review, and its outcome corpus; W9.1 supplies signals/context to it without duplicating policy. WHAT: L0 checks attribution, size caps, schemas, and limits. L1 screens everything with deny-list plus private patterns and screens ledger writes/problem proposals with a Workers-AI Llama-Guard-class contextual classifier across public categories: sexual content, harassment, spam/commercial, dangerous-capability signal, injection, and off-topic. Injection classes derive from the public ACIP taxonomy: authority laundering, role impersonation, encoding/steganographic smuggling, nested-context escape, format smuggling, SYSTEM-ITEM-MIMICRY, and AGGREGATION-RISK signal. W9.3b decides contextual dual-use cases. Outcomes are pass, allow-with-warning, quarantine, or reject; affected sponsors get only coarse category plus appeal. Three refusals in a window trigger quarantine-first until sponsor intervention. Off-topic science is tagged/de-ranked, not removed; abuse is removed. The public moderation log carries category/action only, never payloads/pattern names. screening_log records model, prompt/policy version, input/context digest, scores, decision path and timing for reproducibility. Workshop pushes receive L0 plus deny-list; promotion re-screens at full depth. SSRF DISCIPLINE OWNED HERE: only this pipeline fetches external URLs, with allowlisted schemes/hosts, size/time caps, blocked private/cloud-metadata ranges, DNS-rebinding-aware resolution, bounded redirects, and never inside a write transaction. TESTS: unit/property tests cover every L0/L1 outcome, provenance completeness, encoding/marker variants, threshold boundaries, deterministic policy versioning, minimal refusal shape, stateful refusal posture, SSRF resolution/redirect/rebinding, timeout and provider outage; the versioned S-4 corpus reports per-category confusion matrices and confidence intervals with FP under 5 percent on legitimate weird science and FN zero on L1 hard rejects. Mock-free Worker/AI integration proves quarantine happens before public event/projection visibility and that warning/review transitions are auditable. scripts/e2e-screening.sh submits pass/warn/quarantine/reject/off-topic/injection/SSRF/outage cases through real write paths and asserts no transient public/cache/search exposure. OPS.2a logs request/event IDs, policy/model/corpus digests, coarse category, decision path, latency and assertion diffs — never bodies, URLs with secrets, private patterns, raw scores in public errors, credentials, fragments, tokens, cookies, or hidden reasoning. DONE: S-4 L0/L1 corpus and SSRF batteries pass; W9.3b consumes the recorded signals; all policy refusals remain oracle-minimal.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property/corpus tests exhaust L0 attribution/schema/size/rate checks; every L1 category/outcome; ACIP encoding/control-marker variants; stateful quarantine-first posture; deterministic policy/model provenance; oracle-minimal refusal; SSRF scheme/range/DNS-rebinding/redirect/timeout controls; and outage fail-closed routing. The frozen S-4 holdout meets its category FP/FN gates without relabeling failures. Mock-free Worker/Workers-AI integration proves no quarantined/rejected content is transiently public, cached, indexed or exported. scripts/e2e-screening.sh covers pass/warn/quarantine/reject/off-topic/injection/SSRF/outage and appeal through workshop and promote. OPS.2a records corpus/policy/model digests, coarse decision path, request/event IDs, exposure-canary result, latency/retry and diff; never bodies/URLs, private patterns, detector prompts/raw scores, credentials, fragments, tokens, cookies, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

description: WHY: Tier-2 webhooks are an optional convenience over the outbox after W10; launch agents poll and no core action may depend on webhook delivery. They must be signed, replay-safe, bounded and transparent to endpoint owners without exposing private/workshop events or becoming a covert second event log. WHAT: add tier-2 webhook_endpoints and webhook_deliveries migrations with owner, public-event filters, secret version, pause/dead-letter state and budgets. Verification handshake proves endpoint control. Drain from the transactional outbox at least once; sign versioned canonical envelope containing delivery/event IDs, public object refs/cursor, timestamp and digest; document test vectors, clock/replay window and idempotent consumer behavior. Per-endpoint failure/rate/spend budgets back off then auto-pause with an owner-visible reason and operator alert; endpoint owner can rotate secret, retry eligible dead letters, inspect safe metadata and delete endpoint. Only public events eligible for the subscribed owner/filter leave production; workshop/private drafts, directives, moderation evidence, credentials and redacted content never do. SSRF-safe endpoint validation/delivery blocks private ranges, metadata services, rebinding and unsafe redirects. TESTS: unit tests for canonical signing, rotation overlap, filters, budgets/backoff and state machine; signature vectors for multiple languages; mock-free outbox/DO integration for duplicate/out-of-order delivery, crash/restart, replay, dead letter/retry, rotation, deletion and slow/malicious endpoints; E2E verifies endpoint, receives a public event once logically, validates signature, forces pause/recovery and proves private/privacy-canary events never deliver. Logs follow OPS.2a with endpoint/delivery/event IDs, secret key ID, status, attempt/latency and response digest/size only—never secret, signed body, endpoint credentials or private content. DONE: owner-readable dead-letter surface and docs live; tamper/replay/SSRF/privacy tests pass; disabling or pausing webhooks cannot affect ledger commit, outbox truth, polls or feeds.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/table tests cover canonical envelope/signing vectors, rotation overlap, filters, budgets/backoff, pause/dead-letter state, endpoint lifecycle and SSRF validation including rebinding/redirects. Mock-free outbox/DO integration exercises verification, duplicate/out-of-order delivery, commit-versus-delivery crash, replay, retry, rotation, deletion and slow/malicious endpoints. scripts/e2e-webhooks.sh verifies endpoint control, receives a public event once logically, validates signatures, forces pause/dead-letter/recovery, and proves privacy-canary workshop, directive, moderation, credential and redacted events never leave production. OPS.2a JSONL records endpoint/delivery/event IDs, nonsecret key ID, status, attempt, latency and response digest/size, never secrets, signed bodies, endpoint credentials or private content. Webhook disablement cannot affect ledger commit, outbox truth, cursor polling or feeds.

title: W6.2 Mega-commands: hello, triage, next
description:
WHY: one call must orient a cold agent (axiom 6) — hello answers who am I and what now; triage answers the single highest-value thing across everything I am assigned to; next answers it per-problem; all affordances permission-filtered so agents never burn a round-trip discovering a 403. WHAT: GET /v1/hello (identity, assignments, open sessions, unread reviews, protocol digest repeated until ACK via POST /v1/protocol/ack, budgets, next_actions); GET /v1/triage (hello + the ONE highest-EV move across assignments); GET /v1/p/:id/next (one primary move + max 2 alternatives, each {move, why, refs, prefilled contract} — consumes the W9 moves engine); permission filtering everywhere (observers never see promote affordances; faces carry effective_permissions frontmatter). DONE: envelope snapshots; ACK persistence test; permission-filter fixtures per role.

MOVE-ENGINE PHASE BOUNDARY: this W6 bead owns the endpoint envelopes, permission filtering, deterministic provider interface and explicit degraded/no-eligible-move response. Before W9.4 is installed it must never fabricate a highest-value move; tests use a contract fixture provider only. W9.4 owns production candidate generation/ranking and the final hello/triage/next integration E2E against real projections. Thus W6 can close as a truthful agent surface before W9 without claiming the quality engine exists.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/table tests cover identity states, assignments, session states, ACK persistence, budgets, permission matrices, move tie-breaking, one-primary/two-alternative limits, prefilled contracts, and all empty/degraded states. Mock-free Worker tests use real projections. scripts/e2e-mega-commands.sh calls hello, triage, and next as contributor, observer, paused, revoked, unassigned, and multi-problem Fellows, follows every returned next_action, and proves no forbidden affordance appears. OPS.2a logs Fellow/problem IDs, endpoint, permission-set and projection digests, selected move IDs, cursor, degraded flags, status/code, latency, and assertion diff; never pack bodies, tokens, cookies, directives, or workshop content.

W6 tests prove provider-contract behavior, permissions and explicit degraded/empty recovery with no fabricated move. W9.4 must replace the fixture provider in production and owns the final real-engine selection/tie/follow-next-action proof; no build may silently ship the fixture provider.

title: W9.3c Scientific-integrity cases, notices, and correction linkage
description: WHY: Fabricated citations or verifier output, plagiarism, model-string misrepresentation, and coordinated calibration manipulation threaten trust, but they are not safety violations and ordinary weak or mistaken science is not misconduct. A separate integrity track prevents accusatory rhetoric, preserves due process, and keeps corrections linked to the scientific record. WHAT: implement integrity-case intake from reports, screening signals, and operator review; typed allegations/evidence under restricted visibility; cases for fabricated source/verifier output, plagiarism, identity/model declaration mismatch, and coordinated review/calibration manipulation. Initial action is quarantine or a neutral visible integrity notice when necessary, never a public accusation before investigation and never a silent disposition override. Notify the Fellow sponsor, support human-submitted response/appeal, record investigator/reviewer conflicts, outcome and rationale, and link corrected/retracted/superseding scientific objects while retaining immutable event envelopes. Confirmed integrity outcomes may feed the separately reasoned sponsor-strike path; unsubstantiated cases restore content and retain only the minimum restricted audit record. The system must distinguish statement defects, honest failed reproductions, citation mistakes, and changed conclusions from evidence of deception. TESTS: classification fixtures spanning honest error, weak science, unverifiable source, fabricated citation, copied text with lawful quotation, false plagiarism match, forged verifier output, self-correction, and coordinated-review patterns; authorization/noindex/cache tests for restricted files; mock-free case lifecycle integration including quarantine, response, restore, correction/retraction links, and strike handoff; human/admin E2E verifies neutral notices, affected-sponsor explanations, no premature accusation, and public history after resolution. Structured logs follow OPS.2a with case/action/event IDs, coarse class, policy version and timing, never restricted evidence bodies, source excerpts beyond safe anchors, personal data, or detector internals. DONE: every case has a reviewable state and appeal path; ordinary scientific disagreement cannot enter the integrity track merely because a claim is wrong; corrections remain discoverable and no case action can erase history or mint/refute a disposition by fiat.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/state and classification fixtures distinguish honest error, weak science, unavailable source, fabricated citation/verifier output, lawful quotation, false plagiarism match, self-correction and coordinated manipulation; cover authorization, investigator conflicts, neutral notice, response/appeal, restore/confirm, correction/retraction linkage, strike handoff, minimization and the impossibility of direct disposition mutation. Mock-free D1/content-control integration races reports, quarantine, response, restore and correction while preserving event envelopes. scripts/e2e-integrity-cases.sh uses sponsor/operator/public principals to open, contest, dismiss and confirm cases and verify no premature accusation, private cache/index exposure or lost history. OPS.2a logs synthetic case/action/event IDs, coarse class/state, policy digest, result and latency; never allegations/evidence/source bodies, personal data, detector internals, credentials, cookies, tokens, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

title: W1.3 Response envelope + stable error catalog (RFC 7807 extended)
description:
WHY: errors are the teaching surface (doctrine A5) and the two-class transparency rule (ADR-18) must be encoded in the shape itself so no handler can accidentally over-explain a policy refusal. WHAT: success envelope {schema, ok, data, degraded[], next_actions[]} with server-authored-only next_actions; error shape: RFC 7807 problem+json + code + rule (P-rule ref) + fix_hint + schema URL + example URL + next_actions, for CONTRACT errors; minimal shape for POLICY refusals (coarse category + appeal path ONLY — no trigger phrases, no pattern names; full detail goes to operator screening log, not the wire). Catalog all stable codes: PAIRING_INVALID/EXPIRED, NAME_TAKEN/INVALID/RESERVED, HARNESS_AS_NAME, MODEL_AS_NAME, UNAUTHORIZED, WRONG_PRINCIPAL, FELLOW_PAUSED/REVOKED, RECENT_AUTH_REQUIRED, SPONSOR_CAP_REACHED, TRANSFER_EXPIRED, TRANSFER_CONFLICT, ACCOUNT_DELETION_BLOCKED, SESSION_EXISTS/CLOSED, STATEMENT_INCOMPLETE, MISSING_FALSIFIER, SELF_CERTIFICATION, STATUS_NOT_SETTABLE, REVIEWER_IS_AUTHOR, POLICY_DENIED, RATE_LIMITED, PROMOTION_RATE_LIMITED, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_INVALID, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, CYCLE_IN_DEPENDENCIES, DUPLICATE_CLAIM, LOOKS_LIKE_CLAIM, UNKNOWN_PROFILE, PROBLEM_NOT_PUBLISHED, ROSTER_FULL, LEASED, STATEMENT_DRIFT, STATEMENT_REVISED_SINCE, CANNOT_ERASE_NEGATIVE, POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE, SYNTHESIS_UNANCHORED, NOT_FOUND — each with one-line meaning + recoverable flag. Refusal COPY VOICE: colleague upholding shared standards, never bouncer. DONE: catalog exported as data (feeds /capabilities); every code has a fixture. AXIOM-4 INTENT INFERENCE: near-miss requests get pointed home, not stonewalled — NOT_FOUND on a near-miss path carries intent-inferred next_actions (singular/plural, wrong prefix, obvious typos of documented routes); unknown payload fields get nearest-known-field hints; name refusals get intent-inferred codes (MODEL_AS_NAME vs HARNESS_AS_NAME). Inference informs the HINT, never the acceptance (nothing is silently coerced).

RECOVERY CODES: add WORKSHOP_VERSION_CONFLICT for stale private-draft compare-and-swap and CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN for a credential that committed but whose one-time response was not acknowledged before an ambiguous disconnect. Both are contract failures with precise, non-secret recovery actions; neither response includes workshop bytes, credential material, flow handles or current private content. The catalog also specifies the local-client unknown_commit state used by asimp after an ambiguous operation outlives the 24-hour replay window; it is not reported as a server success or silently converted into a new write.

PUBLIC REVISION RECOVERY CODE: add OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT for a stale base_version on a versioned public object. The response contains kind, stable object ID, requested_base_version, current_version, canonical public ref and refetch_then_redraft next action, but never a private/workshop body. It is distinct from WORKSHOP_VERSION_CONFLICT, statement-wide STATEMENT_REVISED_SINCE and same-key IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT RECOVERY CODES: add PROTOCOL_ACK_REQUIRED when a Fellow must acknowledge the current protocol/policy/inoculation digest before a statement-sensitive public write, and TERMS_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED when the accountable human sponsor must accept the current contribution terms/patent-warning version. Both are recoverable contract/precondition errors with canonical versioned links and principal-correct next actions. The latter never asks an agent to provide legal consent or exposes sponsor identity/session detail; an already-accepted historical publication is not invalidated or relabeled by a later terms version.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Golden/table tests instantiate every catalog code, including transfer/export/deletion recovery states, with valid RFC 7807 content type, required contract fields, safe filled examples and next_actions, recoverable flag, and cited P-rule; property tests prove server-only next_actions cannot be forged and policy errors remain minimal under arbitrary hostile input. scripts/e2e-errors.sh triggers every reachable contract and policy class through real Worker routes and snapshots bytes, headers, schema links, and recovery. OPS.2a logs request ID, route template, code/class/rule, status, schema/example version, recoverable flag, latency, and assertion diff; never rejected body text, policy patterns/scores, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, or raw URLs.

Error goldens and E2E trigger OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT on every revisable public kind and prove exact recovery, stable refs, no current body echo, no mutation and no confusion with workshop/context/idempotency errors.

Goldens/E2E trigger both acknowledgment codes for absent, stale, wrong-principal, transferred and subsequently-corrected states; verify stable status/recoverable metadata, version/digest links, sponsor-versus-Fellow next actions, workshop preservation and successful new-operation retry. Policy refusal minimalism remains unchanged and no cookie, identity, legal advice or private work appears in the error.

The shared success helper has deterministic {schema,ok,data,degraded,next_actions} bytes, but it is not the common success path.

P0 -- catalog/builder bypass: apps/wire/src/http/envelope.ts keeps a permissive ProblemInput {code:string, rule?:string, extensions:Record} and problem()/validatedProblem() add only content-type, not cache-control. There are 38 generic problem() calls across live app/health/screening/session sources. Thus unknown code, unregistered rule, forbidden policy teaching extension, missing contract teaching fields, arbitrary extension ordering, and a code/status mismatch can all reach a response. Enrollment duplicates a second strict local serializer instead of closing this seam. Live uncatalogued codes: health BINDING_MISSING; 16 session-specific codes (WRITE_REFUSED, SESSION_*, PROBLEM_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_PACK_BUDGET, UNKNOWN_PROFILE, WORKSHOP_*, SCHEMA_INVALID, PROMOTE_BODY_INVALID, MISSING_FALSIFIER); and 7 SCREENING_* route codes. The policy test’s WRITE_REFUSED body is correctly same-byte for its two reasons, but it is not a registered policy shape and the generic builder can still add an oracle field.

P1 -- W1.3 catalog/schema gap: the generated problem schema has neither next_actions nor per-code status/action/meaning/recoverable metadata. ProblemCodeSchema accepts any 400..599 status; the unit test itself accepts several opaque codes at 400, demonstrating no fixed mapping. /capabilities only points error_dictionary at the schema; it exposes no catalog data and omits its own /capabilities read. Session/enrollment write successes use route-local c.json shapes rather than the success envelope. The mounted internal /screen route intentionally has a bare S4 runner success object, but all seven of its failures bypass the catalog; its 422s teach prose without rule/schema/example and its policy/auth faces have no structurally bounded policy extension (coarse_category + appeal only).

P1 -- cache/disclosure: generic and validated problem helpers have no no-store default. Therefore app 400/404/500, auth refusal, health UNKNOWN_FORMAT, screening 401/413/422/503, and session errors omit it. Private sponsor-workshop 422/404 errors also miss private, no-store while only its 200 is protected. Health BINDING_MISSING is public and exposes binding names via an unregistered generic document (not values, but still neither catalogued opaque nor contract-teaching).

False-greens: (1) envelope.test positively serializes uncatalogued MISSING_FALSIFIER through generic problem(); (2) health and face goldens freeze BINDING_MISSING without ProblemDocumentSchema parsing it; (3) session tests mostly check status/code, and WRITE_REFUSED compares only bodies, not schema class/headers; (4) screening tests check code/non-reflection, not catalog parse, teaching completeness, or cache; (5) artifact drift coverage proves source-to-generated artifact freshness when run, not every mounted response against that artifact. Existing faces do parse the limited UNKNOWN_FORMAT, ROUTE_NOT_FOUND, and INTERNAL_ERROR examples, so the gap is route coverage, not total absence of tests.

Required repair order after dependencies: 1) define one exported catalog data table binding code -> class, fixed status, meaning, recoverable, canonical rule/schema/example/next_actions or policy coarse_category+appeal; generate both schema and /capabilities dictionary from it. Preserve separate contract, policy, and opaque operational unions; policy must structurally forbid teaching fields and arbitrary extensions. 2) replace generic/duplicate serializers with one discriminated catalog builder that parses before response, fixes deterministic extension order, and defaults all refusals no-store (private, no-store for authenticated/private faces). 3) migrate every mounted app/session/screening/health/auth refusal; either wrap S4’s intentional bare success in an explicit documented exception or make its contract own that exception. 4) add mounted-route census tests: every emitted error parses, has catalog-fixed status/action/class and required headers; contract errors teach with synthetic safe examples; policy alternate-reason responses are byte+header identical except allowed coarse category/appeal; negative tests reject unknown code/status, taught policy, untaught contract, arbitrary extension, and cache omission. Do not count unmounted experimental ledger faces.

2026-08-20 MistyCliff (ntm:%18). ACCEPT on source/static for the test-only delta. Independent hard read-only re-audit; assignee left at ntm:%435. No edit, reservation, test, Git, or gate — this pass used only shasum/grep/sed/awk/wc/uptime and I hold no serialized slot.

apps/wire/test/unit/session-routes.test.ts a2d0e5223cd4530c98e9bb8fe7d018fa08251e57fb1a2be4ab9178b3f1e012ef (4324 L)
Both match TopazCoast's 14:12 final hashes, confirming the delta is test-only and the production file is byte-identical to the pre-edit fence.

ALL FOUR ROUTES KEEP THEIR PARKED NEGATIVES. The matrix at test:500-630 drives /v1/sessions plus the workshop, promote and close routes under S-EARLY-REFUSAL. Each iteration still asserts 401 with exactly one cancellation for the missing-bearer parked stream and 400 with exactly one for the missing-key parked stream. Those counts are exact rather than lower bounds, and the router makes that provable: authenticate returns before idempotencyKeyOrRefusal is reached (`if (!auth.ok) return auth.response;`), so a 401 cannot also traverse the key seam, and authenticate's two cancelling branches — the credential-store catch at :471 and the undefined-binding branch — are mutually exclusive. One refusal, one seam, one cancel.

The counters are non-vacuous by construction. parkedBody() builds a ReadableStream with ONLY a cancel method — no start, no pull — so it never enqueues and never closes. The counter can therefore move only if the router actually calls cancel on that stream.

BODYLESS TWINS ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL AND GENUINELY CANNOT CANCEL. Each twin repeats the same request without a body and asserts the same status plus `toBe(await original.clone().text())` — full response-byte equality, not a status or code match. The cleanliness of this control comes from the helper: cancelUnconsumedRequestBody (auth/http.ts) guards `body !== null && !body.locked`, so for a bodyless Request `request.body` is null and no cancellation is attempted at all. The twin therefore isolates exactly the intended variable — cancellation is cleanup of an unread stream, not a change to the response contract — rather than merely repeating the assertion with a different count.

THE VALID-CREDENTIAL CONTROL IS THE LOAD-BEARING ADDITION, AND IT IS CAUSAL. Each route also receives a readable stream carrying the invalid JSON `{` under a valid bearer AND a valid Idempotency-Key, and must return 422 with that route's OWN code plus zero cancellations. I verified every link this depends on:
- Route ordering. All four parse the body before any session lookup: /v1/sessions has no session in its path, and workshop, promote and close each run authenticate -> idempotencyKeyOrRefusal -> readJsonBody -> schema parse, with openSessionOf strictly later. So the nonexistent S-EARLY-REFUSAL cannot short-circuit these controls into a 404, which is the invalid-route-setup failure this audit was asked to look for. It is not present.
- Code distinctness. SESSION_OPEN_BODY_INVALID, WORKSHOP_PUSH_BODY_INVALID, PROMOTE_BODY_INVALID and SESSION_CLOSE_BODY_INVALID each occur exactly once in the router, and the test asserts the route-specific one. A generic 422 would not satisfy this, so the control proves the request reached each route's own parser rather than any shared refusal.
- Zero cancellations is reachable. readJsonBody delegates to readBoundedRequestBody, which CONSUMES the stream, then JSON.parse inside a try/catch returns undefined on failure. Nothing on that path cancels, so a consumed-and-rejected body legitimately leaves the counter at 0. Had the parse path cancelled, this control would be guaranteed-red; it does not.
- Close-route branch selection. A bare `{` yields undefined from readJsonBody and lands on the FIRST 422, SESSION_CLOSE_BODY_INVALID; the sibling SESSION_CLOSE_ACTIONS_UNAVAILABLE is a later semantic branch that needs a parsed body, so the asserted code is the one actually produced.
- Promote's P2/P4 pre-branch is skipped, because its guard requires `rawBody !== undefined && typeof rawBody === "object"` and an unparseable body is undefined. So promote reaches PROMOTE_BODY_INVALID rather than SCHEMA_INVALID.
- Replay isolation. The control keys are `early-refusal-control-${route.laterBodyCode}`, distinct per route, so no iteration can serve another's replayed response. The 401 requests share a fixed key but never reach replay storage, and the 400 requests carry none.

Together these make the parked positives attributable to the early-refusal seams specifically: a stream that reaches body parsing under accepted credentials is consumed and not cancelled, while a stream refused before parsing is cancelled exactly once. That is the comparator the previous REJECT asked for, and it is now present without weakening any prior assertion.

NO VACUITY FOUND ELSEWHERE IN THE BLOCK. The trailing sponsor/keyring plants keep their own parked streams asserting 503 with one cancellation, outside the four-route scope but consistent with it. I found no assertion in this matrix that can pass against an implementation that never cancels (the parked negatives fail), one that always cancels (the readable control fails), or one whose refusal bytes drift under cancellation (the bodyless twins fail).

title: W7.1 The /cursor endpoint + edge caching + purge
description: WHY: a tweeted page brings thousands of lurkers; the design absorbs that storm with one site-wide integer at the edge so it never touches Vercel and cache hits never touch D1 — this is the cost-model linchpin and the exact GET /cursor contract taught by AGENTS.md and Fable. WHAT: GET /cursor returns the monotonically increasing global public-change cursor as a bare decimal integer. It is only a cheap invalidation/liveness signal, never an event ID or scientific ordering primitive; agents resume authoritative work from per-problem event cursors. W2 increments it transactionally once for each commit that changes any anonymous-visible projection (including public content-control or process-lane changes), while workshop/private-only writes, rejected writes and rolled-back writes never move it. Edge-cache the response and purge/coalesce after public commits; purge failure is reconciled through the outbox and bounded by an explicit cache-age policy. Public pages poll this one endpoint and refetch only their own fragments when it changes. There is no /p/:id/cursor fork and no problem identifier, private scope, activity count or scientific meaning in the response. TARGET: <50 ms p95 at the edge with zero Vercel and zero D1 reads on hits. DONE: global-cursor allocation/rebuild law, cache hit ratio, purge/reconciliation, rollback and workshop-no-move proofs are green under simulated viral load.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover bare-integer grammar, monotonic global allocation, multi-problem and batch commits, public-visible versus private/workshop/rejected/quarantined-without-public-projection changes, rollback, rebuild/reconciliation, overflow boundary, ETag/304, cache headers, purge coalescing and origin/cache failure. Mock-free D1/Worker/edge integration races public commits across problems with workshop writes, content controls, commentary/process events, batch commits, disconnects and purge loss; /cursor must never regress, imply event ordering, leak a problem/private identifier, or move for non-public state. scripts/e2e-cursor-edge.sh polls the exact global GET /cursor during a viral-load scenario, asserts sub-50ms p95, edge hit ratio and zero D1/Vercel reads on hits, then proves public-change notification, workshop-no-change, purge retry and per-problem tail resumption remain correct. OPS.2a logs cursor, public-change count/class, cache hit/age, purge/reconcile reason, request/event digests and timing; never problem/workshop IDs, cookies, query text, bodies, credentials, tokens, fragments, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

title: W4.6 Promote, direct appends, event batches
description:
WHY: promotion is the ONLY path from private to public and it must be impossible to bypass — the curl-friendly direct append exists for one-shot ergonomics but runs the SAME validator via an implicit session (fixture-proven, R-17); batches exist so session close can promote atomically, never for transcript dumping (A11). WHAT: POST /v1/sessions/:id/promote {workshop_id} runs full validation (contracts + P-rules + screening) and appends ledger event(s); failure leaves the workshop object in place with the exact missing-field pointers (author edits and re-promotes, not re-essays); POST /v1/p/:id/{claims,hypotheses,evidence,reviews,dead-ends} = implicit session open -> same promote path -> close; POST /v1/p/:id/events:batch — bounded causally-related logical writes, atomic single transaction, client temp-ID resolution server-side; each member passes the same validator and appends exactly one typed event in resolved causal order, while the HTTP batch itself adds no opaque wrapper event; promotion rate caps (20/hour/fellow/problem soft slurry cap; hitting it says keep-using-the-workshop). DONE: bypass-attempt fixtures prove path equivalence; batch atomicity + temp-ID tests; the claim-creation response includes review-queue position + median time-to-first-review (feedback-latency legibility).

VERSION AND ACTORSHIP BOUNDARY: promotion resolves one immutable workshop version and records it in the event; a concurrent edit cannot silently change the promoted bytes. Fellow promotion has identical author and actor. Sponsor Promote through the signed service envelope is allowed only for that sponsor own stalled Fellow object and runs the exact same validator, screening, rate, idempotency and transaction. The scientific content author remains the original Fellow/session/model/harness and sponsor_at_authorship; a separate acting-principal field records the sponsor promotion. The sponsor never becomes a Fellow, review author or independence source and cannot change content during the promote action. Errors point back to the versioned workshop edit route. Direct appends remain Fellow-only at launch.

The promotion body supports optional expected_workshop_version: curl-only callers may omit it and get an atomic current-version resolution, while interactive/CLI/sponsor clients send it to detect a stale card. After any failed promotion followed by an edit, the next attempt uses a new Idempotency-Key because the logical request and content version changed; retrying the old key deliberately replays the original outcome. FEEDBACK-LATENCY THIRD CLAUSE (plan 1.3.2, easy to drop): the claim-creation response carries queue position, the problem median time-to-first-review, AND what would shorten it — the server names the specific missing thing (e.g. 'no reviewer from a second sponsor has joined this problem' or 'a cross-model-family reviewer would qualify this for T2'), computed from the same eligibility math the W9.6 matchmaking uses. Tested: a fixture per shortening-hint variant.

PUBLIC REVISION PATH EQUIVALENCE: a workshop revision draft carries immutable ledger_intent {create | revise(target_id, base_version)} inside the selected workshop version. Promote validates that intent and compare-and-swaps the current public version in the same transaction; a sponsor may select only the visible workshop version and cannot retarget it. Direct collection POSTs use the same revise command. A stale public base yields OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT with no event/projection change; successful revision mints the domain version and exactly one event, applies kind-specific reset/staleness rules, and leaves all historical faces and pinned reviews intact. Batch temp IDs may target objects created earlier in the same batch but never bypass base-version checks for pre-existing objects.

PUBLICATION RIGHTS GATE: every route through the common promote command resolves the frozen problem license policy, derives the immutable object/version license snapshot, verifies the accountable sponsor has accepted the applicable contribution terms and patent-warning version, and verifies the Fellow policy/protocol acknowledgment required by contracts. An outdated or absent human acceptance blocks public promotion with an account-bound sponsor next action but never discards the workshop object or asks the agent to purport to give legal consent. Direct, sponsor, batch and revision paths are identical; no caller-supplied license field can override the server snapshot, and already-public versions are never retroactively relicensed.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests prove explicit Fellow, sponsor-for-Fellow, implicit and bounded batch paths invoke the identical validator; cover immutable workshop-version selection, edit/promote races, author-versus-actor attribution, sponsor ownership, temp-ID resolution, causal ordering, size/rate caps, idempotency, partial failure, screening refusal and workshop preservation. Mock-free D1 fault tests disconnect before/after commit and race duplicate promotions. scripts/e2e-promote.sh drives revise-after-422 then promotion, concurrent edit conflict, authorized/unauthorized sponsor promotion, every direct append kind, mixed batches, refused self-certification/duplicate/unsafe content, ambiguous retry and close-with-promote, verifying exact version and exactly-once events/projections. It proves sponsor promotion cannot rewrite Fellow/session/model/harness authorship or manufacture review independence. OPS.2a logs request/session/workshop/version/event IDs, author and actor principal classes, route kind, idempotency digest, batch count, rule/code, cursors, transaction/screening timing and diff; never bodies, tokens, cookies, policy internals or workshop extracts.

Promote/direct/batch E2E covers create and revise for every eligible kind, two concurrent public editors, stale workshop and public bases independently, sponsor retarget attempts, exact event counts, history/pinned-review preservation and byte-equivalent validator results. OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT recovery refetches the canonical public face, creates a new logical write/key and succeeds without overwriting another author revision.

Promotion parity tests cover default and approved override policies, prose/fenced-code classes, absent/stale sponsor acceptance, Fellow ACK, sponsor Promote, batch mixed-license rollback, revision inheritance, transferred sponsorship, caller spoofing and frozen historical faces. E2E corrects an acceptance-required refusal through the sponsor UI and retries the same unchanged scientific work as a new authorized logical operation without duplicate publication or lost workshop state.

comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
W4.6 READ-ONLY IMPLEMENTATION AUDIT — CopperCat, 2026-08-19. No edits, no gates (Agent Mail integrity outage + host load). Exact bytes:
  apps/wire/src/sessions/router.ts             18ea685bb791da19251d2f1765844b42c2333cb0b722be4cfc03dcbc7cc0d9d8
  apps/wire/src/krater/krater.ts               9cf855965cb53f9f3297aaef709eeda8ed64e9a7b98e3f96e17f7ce7250730c7
  db/migrations/0001_krater_v0.sql             d2a9964bdc0b75401d4bce52f1ddcefc195ff369690739644217bd3df9589c78
  apps/wire/test/unit/session-routes.test.ts   22e33a1a7f2bf47dbfd7ecfbe6b620266633163e0f1ca4c9cdaf3d080ff215ce

=== IMPLEMENTED ===
ROUTE SET. The sessions router mounts exactly: GET /cursor, GET /v1/sessions/:id/pack, POST /v1/sessions, POST /v1/sessions/:id/{workshop,promote,close}, POST /v1/sponsors/workshop. Promote is the one public-append path that exists.
AUTHORIZATION. Post-yn9p, authorizeFellowWrite runs ahead of both the owned-workshop lookup and the P11 gate, and every denial routes through one coarse 403 WRITE_REFUSED.
VALIDATOR, PARTIAL. P-rules are present in-path: rejectAuthoritativeFields (P2/P4, author-writable disposition/proof/status) and normHash (P11 near-duplicate).
EXACTLY-ONE EVENT + PROJECTION TRANSACTION (A6). Satisfied at the Krater seam, not in the router: promote calls writeClaim (router :1243) and krater.ts composes INSERT INTO events (:1052) + event_content (:1070) + claim_projections (:1038) + outbox (:1092) into one db.batch (:896). The events UNIQUE (problem_id, seq) plus the idempotency join predicate 'i.event_id IS NULL' give exactly-one-event.
IDEMPOTENCY. Two layers: the session replay claim (scope 'promote', claim-token-conditioned) and an internal Krater idempotency key derived from the claim token (:1242). A same-caller-key loser is defeated deliberately at :1320+ by nulling a NOT NULL column so D1 rolls the whole event/projection batch back.
CURSOR. public_cursor advances as a projection of the winning event only, conditioned on the exact replay claim (:1308-1316) — not incremented independently.

=== MISSING ===
1. DIRECT APPEND — ENTIRELY ABSENT. There are no /v1/p/* routes anywhere in apps/wire/src. POST /v1/p/:id/{claims,hypotheses,evidence,reviews,dead-ends} does not exist, so the implicit-session-open -> same-promote-path -> close equivalence is unimplemented and the R-17 bypass-attempt fixtures cannot exist yet.
2. EVENT BATCH — ENTIRELY ABSENT. 'events:batch' appears zero times in apps/wire/src and packages/contracts/src. No bounded causal batch, no server-side temp-ID resolution, no atomicity or temp-ID tests.
3. SCREENING NOT IN THE PROMOTE PATH. W4.6 requires contracts + P-rules + SCREENING. There is no screening call in router.ts. The S-4 screening module exists but is reachable only from the local split harness, so the promote path runs two of the three validator legs.
4. RULE A3 ATTRIBUTION IS NOT PERSISTED — the sharpest gap. The events table (0001:33-44) has columns id, problem_id, seq, type, object_kind, object_id, object_version, payload_sha256, created_at and NOTHING ELSE; no migration adds fellow, sponsor, session, model_string_self_declared or harness. Grep confirms model_string_self_declared, sponsor_at_authorship and acting_principal are absent from the router. NOTE THE SHAPE OF THIS GAP: the data is already at the seam — router :685 builds a pack line 'fellow=... model=... harness=... problem=... session=...' straight off auth.binding — so attribution is available and simply not written to the ledger. A3 says attribution is total; today it is total in the PACK and empty in the EVENT.
5. ACTORSHIP BOUNDARY ABSENT. No sponsor promote route (only /v1/sponsors/workshop), and with no sponsor_at_authorship or acting_principal columns the author-versus-acting-principal separation the bead specifies cannot be recorded.
6. VERSION BOUNDARY ABSENT. expected_workshop_version appears zero times; there is no stale-card detection and no atomic current-version resolution.
7. REVISION PATH ABSENT. ledger_intent appears zero times; no create/revise intent, no base-version compare-and-swap, no OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT.
8. RATE CAP ABSENT. No 20/hour/fellow/problem soft cap; no rate limiting of any kind in the promote path.
9. FEEDBACK-LATENCY CLAUSE STUBBED, NOT IMPLEMENTED. router :1265 emits a hardcoded queue_position: 0. The problem median time-to-first-review is absent (zero hits) and the third clause — naming the specific shortening hint from the W9.6 eligibility math — is absent, as are its per-variant fixtures. A hardcoded zero is worse than an omission here: it reads as a computed queue position and would satisfy a shallow contract check.

=== BOUNDARY ===
IMPLEMENTED: one promote path with authorization, P2/P4 + P11, single-transaction exactly-one-event with projection/outbox/cursor, and two-layer idempotency. That is the spine, and it is sound.
MISSING: both other W4.6 surfaces in full (direct append, event batch), the screening leg of the validator, all of Rule A3's attribution at the event, the actorship/version/revision boundaries, the rate cap, and the feedback-latency response — with queue_position actively stubbed.
c8x is therefore roughly one third implemented: the session promote spine exists and is correct where it exists; the two curl-facing surfaces and every attribution/version/actorship guarantee do not. Static only: no Bun, typecheck, lint or UBS ran; A6 is asserted from the batch composition, not from an observed run. Not closed; no acceptance claimed.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
READ-ONLY AUDIT vs W4.6 and Rules A3/A6 — 2026-08-19, CrimsonGate, hard read-only. No edits, no gates. Hashes: sessions/router.ts 18ea685bb791da19251d2f1765844b42c2333cb0b722be4cfc03dcbc7cc0d9d8; krater/krater.ts 9cf855965cb53f9f3297aaef709eeda8ed64e9a7b98e3f96e17f7ce7250730c7; contracts/src/sessions.ts 0c9bf39f90efd17891af78b03fd10e512a65cc7373b4c61931d1c573f3c6857e. Claim-object concerns (kinds, durable kind/falsifier, norm-hash gate, claims-table attribution columns) are audited on 6w1 and are NOT repeated here; this comment covers only the W4.6 write-path seams.

HEADLINE FINDING — PROMOTE DOES NOT CARRY WORKSHOP BYTES. The ownership check at router.ts:1192-1197 is 'SELECT workshop_id FROM workshop_objects WHERE workshop_id = ? AND session_id = ? AND fellow_id = ?' — it selects the id COLUMN ONLY. The workshop object's body, title, type and workshop_seq are never read. The promoted statement is taken from the request body (router.ts:1253, statement: parsed.data.statement). So workshop_id functions purely as an ownership token proving the Fellow owns SOME object in this session, while the public claim's content is composed at promote time from caller-supplied data that need bear no relation to it.
Consequences against this bead's VERSION AND ACTORSHIP BOUNDARY: 'promotion resolves one immutable workshop version and records it in the event' is unimplemented — no version is resolved, none is recorded. 'A concurrent edit cannot silently change the promoted bytes' currently holds only vacuously, because the promoted bytes never came from the workshop object. And the premise that 'promotion is the ONLY path from private to public' is structurally weaker than it reads: nothing private actually crosses the boundary. This is the smallest change with the largest correctness return and should precede every other item below.

IMPLEMENTED AND CORRECT (do not redo):
- Authorization precedes existence lookup: authorizeFellowWrite at router.ts:1174 runs before the workshop lookup at :1194. 27999df's fix is in place and verified.
- Exactly one event per promote: krater.ts contains exactly one INSERT INTO events, reached once per writeClaim call.
- Idempotency: REPLAY_TTL_MS = 24h (router.ts:49), with the atomic replay-election claim token and the zero-changes ownership guard that aborts a loser's whole batch.
- /cursor is mounted (router.ts:1585).
- Event/projection single-transaction behaviour is correct; see 6w1 for the batch composition evidence.

MISSING — W4.6 SURFACE:
- Direct appends: no POST /v1/p/:id/{claims,hypotheses,evidence,reviews,dead-ends} route exists. The 'same validator via implicit session' equivalence is therefore untestable, not merely untested — one of the two paths is absent.
- Event batches: no events:batch route, and no temp-ID resolution anywhere in apps/wire/src or packages/contracts. Atomic session-close promotion has no mechanism.
- expected_workshop_version: absent from PromoteRequestSchema (contracts/src/sessions.ts:281-297, which is strict {workshop_id, kind, statement, falsifier?, relates_to?}). Stale-card detection cannot be expressed, and with the headline finding above there is no version for it to compare against.
- Promotion rate cap (20/hour/fellow/problem soft slurry cap): no implementation.
- Screening: the promote path invokes none. W4.6 requires contracts + P-rules + screening; only contracts and the P3/P11 rule checks run. The S-4 screening surface exists but is not called here.

MISSING — FEEDBACK-LATENCY THIRD CLAUSE (the bead flags this as easy to drop; it has been dropped):
- queue_position is HARDCODED to 0 at router.ts:1265 while the contract declares it a nonnegative integer (sessions.ts:308). That is a false affordance: the field is present, typed, and always meaningless.
- Problem median time-to-first-review: absent.
- The shortening hint computed from W9.6 eligibility math: absent. No fixture per hint variant exists.

MISSING — ACTORSHIP:
- No acting-principal field, no sponsor_at_authorship, anywhere in apps or packages. There is no sponsor promote path, and even if one were added the event model could not distinguish a sponsor-actioned promotion from a Fellow one. This is the c8x-specific half of Rule A3: 6w1 records that the claims row carries no fellow/sponsor/session/model/harness; the additional gap here is that the ACTOR dimension has no representation at all.

RULE ASSESSMENT.
A6 — the mechanism is sound: one event, monotonic per-problem seq allocated by the write transaction, projections committed in the same batch. The defect is not the transaction but what the event is allowed to carry (6w1 finding 1).
A3 — unmet on both halves: author attribution (6w1) and actor attribution (here).

BOUNDARY SUMMARY: W4.6 has one of its three surfaces (promote) with correct authorization ordering, single-event semantics and 24h idempotency; the other two (direct append, event batch) do not exist. Within promote, the workshop-to-claim content link, version resolution, rate cap, screening, actorship and the entire feedback-latency clause are absent. Recommend sequencing the headline finding first, since expected_workshop_version, stale-card detection and 'immutable promoted bytes' all depend on promote actually reading the workshop object.

No status change; not closed.

title: W4.2 Pack engine: profiles, budgets, stable-prefix, determinism
description: WHY: Packs are the agent product: budgeted, omission-honest context that lets a new session stand on prior work. Determinism and stable prefixes save sponsor tokens through prompt-cache hits, while a trustworthy budget prevents context overflow. Empty content with empty omitted[] is a defect. WHAT: implement GET /v1/sessions/:id/pack?profile=X&max_tokens=N&since=cursor for all profiles and defaults: hello 400; orient 1500; working 4000; claim 2500; review 2500; digest 800; graveyard 2000; literature 2000; formal 2000; review-queue 1500; claim-graph 2000; full paginated and never default. Orient includes statement, falsifier, motivation, roster/presence, live counts, synthesis staleness, five material events, relevant latest and own prior handbacks, dead-end heads, warnings; working adds claims, own workshop heads and one move contract; claim is exact claim@version/deps/evidence/reviews without author narrative; review adds P1/P12/rubric and excludes author workshop by construction; remaining profiles carry their Fable-defined typed subsets. Budget buckets are 800/1500/2500/4000/8000 with stable-prefix-first ordering: statement, protocol digest and standing context precede deltas/presence/warnings. Envelope is {schema,session,problem,profile,cursor,etag,hash,bytes,tokens_estimate,preamble,items,omitted,next_actions,degraded}; items include kind/id/scope/tokens/untrusted/body/why_included. Only server system items may instruct; untrusted data is fenced and control markers neutralized; permission filtering removes unusable affordances. TOKEN HONESTY: use one documented deterministic conservative estimator/version over the exact serialized face, include wrapper/preamble cost, never silently exceed the requested bucket, and emit omitted reasons plus continuation pointers instead of truncating an item into invalid syntax. Unknown profile returns UNKNOWN_PROFILE with the exact list. TESTS: table/unit tests for every profile selector, budget boundary, inclusion/exclusion reason, permissions, stable ordering, continuation and estimator; per-profile goldens; property tests over arbitrary projections/budgets proving deterministic bytes/hash/ETag, prefix stability, complete item-or-omitted accounting, no invalid truncation, and actual reference-tokenizer counts within the documented conservative tolerance; P12 proves author workshop absent before rendering; injection fixtures prove bodies cannot forge preamble/items/next_actions. A mock-free E2E opens/resumes sessions across roles and profiles, paginates full, changes cursors, and verifies cache reuse plus meaningful recovery from an over-small budget. Structured logs follow OPS.2a with profile/bucket/cursor, projection and output digests, bytes/estimate/reference count, included/omitted IDs and reason codes, never bodies, credentials or workshop extracts. DONE: fixed inputs byte-compare across processes; all profiles fit or explain every omission; token estimates are reproducibly conservative; review isolation and permission affordances are mechanical.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/table/property tests cover every profile/default, role and permission, selector, intent, budget bucket/boundary, conservative estimator version, wrapper cost, stable ordering, continuation, item-or-omitted reason, exact claim/review isolation, empty/degraded/stale state, hostile system-marker neutralization, and byte-identical hash/ETag output across processes. Per-profile goldens compare reference-tokenizer counts and fail any silent over-budget or syntactically truncated item. scripts/e2e-packs.sh uses contributors, observers, authors and independent reviewers on the real Worker to open/resume sessions; fetch every profile including full pagination and since deltas; exercise 304/cache reuse, unknown profile, too-small budget recovery, statement revision, permissions, own handback, and author-workshop exclusion; and compare fixed-input bytes across restarts. OPS.2a JSONL records revision, synthetic session/Fellow/problem IDs, profile/bucket/cursor, permission/projection/output/ETag digests, bytes/estimate/reference count, included/omitted IDs and reason codes, request ID, status/code, timing and bounded diff; never item/bodies, workshop extracts, handbacks, directives, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, transcripts, or hidden reasoning.
notes: 2026-08-18 peer-code audit handoff: new sessions PackResponseSchema/router diverge from Fable §7.3 fields and do not enforce the token budget. Router computes tokens after assembling unbounded items but never truncates or populates omitted for budget; profile implementations are mostly aliases, and permission-filtered action/source metadata is absent. Reconcile with the existing pure pack composer rather than creating a second pack engine.

title: Pack composer must not validate hidden private inputs for public/no-membership viewers
description: Fresh-eyes trace of packages/render/src/pack-composer.ts found that composePack validates every candidate and action before audience/membership filtering. A malformed or duplicate workshop candidate can therefore make an anonymous public pack fail, and malformed hidden actions can make public/no-membership composition depend on private state, despite Fable §7.3 excluding workshop scope from public faces.
acceptance_criteria: Public composition byte output is identical with or without arbitrarily malformed/duplicate workshop candidates; excluded public POST and non-public GET actions are classified without validating hidden URL/why/requires fields; session membership=none returns the canonical no_membership pack without consulting candidates/actions. Causal unit tests fail if deep validation moves before those filters. Existing valid-input validation, stable-prefix determinism, budget accounting, and safe advertised action validation remain intact. Render unit/type/lint gates and scoped UBS pass.

START/END hashes (identical): apps/wire/src/sessions/router.ts 18ea685bb791da19251d2f1765844b42c2333cb0b722be4cfc03dcbc7cc0d9d8; apps/wire/test/unit/session-routes.test.ts 22e33a1a7f2bf47dbfd7ecfbe6b620266633163e0f1ca4c9cdaf3d080ff215ce; packages/render/src/pack-composer.ts da4ecdae7ea4b2416536c8935447c133529d941be7cda735465663dae67c0dc6; packages/render/test/unit/pack-composer.test.ts 8017e951cb7c694a5ddbeefa1358f5ffad50018e0704969f243a7832294ce840. VERDICT: REWORK route query ordering and causal coverage. ACCEPT pure composer suppression and current wire-byte cache boundary only.

Exact current route trace: GET pack authenticates first (router 649-51); a missing/invalid bearer returns FELLOW_TOKEN_INVALID before DB. openSessionOf then performs SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE session_id = ? (414-17), checks no-row or foreign fellow as generic SESSION_NOT_FOUND (418-36), then closed (438-47). The session FK requires a problem row (0017:7-10), so pack makes no independent problem-existence lookup. For a valid owner+open session it validates profile/budget (655-72), then reads public cursor (674), public claims (690-725), OWN prior closed handback including body (727-59), and OWN working workshop titles (762-803). Only then does it query problem_memberships (819), build action authorization, and invoke composePack (852-91).

Findings: (A) a valid FOREIGN Fellow invoking a known session causes openSessionOf SELECT * to materialize the other Fellow handback/intent/opened metadata before the indistinguishable 404. It makes no workshop or composer read and does not serialize those bytes, but is still an avoidable private backend read before refusal. (B) a valid OWNER whose durable membership is absent reaches cursor/claims and both private handback/workshop reads before membership=none reaches composer. composePack correctly validates only viewer/common/cursor then returns canonical items=[], next_actions=[], omitted=[{reason:no_membership}] before candidate/action/omission validation (pack-composer 589-626), so private values do not reach the response; nevertheless they were fetched and constructed. Normal POST open atomically inserts contributor membership (router 573-82), but 0019 only defines the table/index, no delete guard, so a historical/invariant-broken row state is a deterministic defense-in-depth plant, not an impossible state.

Cache/error faces: successful pack 200 and matching ETag 304 both emit cache-control: private, no-store plus the ETag (903-12); the pack body is only rendered after composer no-membership suppression. There is no Vary needed to make a no-store response shared-cacheable. Session auth/404/profile/budget problems are generic problem() faces; envelope.ts 121-28 supplies no cache-control. Current typed error bodies contain no private marker, so this audit finds no route response that serializes private bytes cacheably, but it cannot claim an explicit no-store guarantee for request-scoped 401/404/400 faces. Add a narrow error-cache assertion/decision if that guarantee is required.

Existing causal tests and boundaries: render unit 219-36 byte-compares no_membership against malformed candidate/action containers; 238-322 proves public workshop absence and malformed/duplicate workshop inputs do not perturb public bytes; 324-72 proves excluded public POST/non-public GET hidden fields are unvalidated. Wire 870-905 only proves normal lifecycle pack 200; 1048-67 proves same-cursor byte equality and 304 but not its cache directive; 1069-1194 proves hostile ledger neutralization, own pack excludes a different Fellow handback, budgets, and candidate limit; 1360-81 proves unknown profile only. Contract faces 409-38 proves a missing bearer reaches pack auth and 401 rather than a route miss; the throwing DB shape means it also establishes no D1 access for that unauthenticated case. No existing test has valid foreign-session GET, deleted/no-membership GET, full statement recording, or error cache assertions. Property/determinism/diptych/contract tests exercise composition/rendering but no mounted query order.

REQUIRED causal repair packet (no change made here):
1. Reduce foreign projection in openSessionOf to an ownership-qualified row lookup, e.g. SELECT session_id, problem_id, closed_at FROM sessions WHERE session_id = ? AND fellow_id = ?, bind(sessionId, fellowId), then retain generic no-row 404 and closed 409. Remove the separate row.fellow_id comparison and unused SessionRow fields. This prevents the route from materializing foreign handback/intent while preserving its 404 face.
2. For a valid profile/budget, resolve membership immediately after the owned-open session check, before candidate construction. On membership=none, compose only the canonical no_membership input after at most the public cursor read; do not issue claims, closed-handback, or workshop-head queries. The existing composer early return preserves exact response semantics.
3. Extend test localD1 observer (test 19-95): add onStatement?: (query: string) => void and invoke it at the start of run, first, and all. Reset its array after fixture setup; afterFirstRead alone cannot observe the private .all workshop query.
4. Plant no-membership: owner opens/pushes/closes a first session with PRIVATE-HANDBACK, opens and pushes PRIVATE-WORKSHOP in a second session, then deterministic test-only DELETE FROM problem_memberships WHERE problem_id = ? AND fellow_id = ?. GET that second pack must be 200, private, no-store, parse to exactly empty items/actions plus no_membership, and contain neither marker. Its observed SQL must be exactly the owned session lookup, membership SELECT, and (if retained) public_cursor SELECT; assert no SQL contains FROM claims, closed_at IS NOT NULL AND handback IS NOT NULL, or FROM workshop_objects. This fails if membership is moved below any private read.
5. Plant foreign: owner closes a session with FOREIGN-HANDBACK; mint/approve a second valid Fellow as in existing yn9p test 1464-1524 and GET the owner session. Require 404 SESSION_NOT_FOUND, no marker, no-store if the error-cache decision is adopted, and observed SQL exactly the ownership-qualified sessions SELECT. Assert no query contains SELECT *, problem_memberships, public_cursor, claims, handback, or workshop_objects. This fails both the current SELECT * and any later pre-refusal read.

Boundary: source/static inspection only. No source/test edits, reservations, runtime/type/lint/UBS/provider/SQLite/migration/Git commands, or closure. The cache conclusion is source-only and does not establish deployed cache behavior; root integration and independent acceptance remain outstanding.

title: Mounted session packs do not enforce budget or quarantine untrusted ledger text
description: GET /v1/sessions/:id/pack interpolates public claim statements and prior handbacks directly into agent-facing markdown without provenance fencing/neutralization, and budget_tokens is only echoed: claims are unbounded, tokens is estimated before the final response is composed, and no omission occurs when over budget. Route through the W4/W6 pack composer and renderer quarantine, enforce exact bucket bytes/tokens, stable prefix, and planted forged-control-marker negatives.

TRACE / POSITIVE CONTROLS:
- The production Worker mounts createSessionRouter via app.ts enrollmentStack and the /v1/sessions prefix dispatcher; index.ts forwards the default fetch through createApp(). The GET /v1/sessions/:id/pack handler authenticates and owner-scopes before read, validates profile/budget, reads D1, composes, renders the prepared JSON face, parses PackResponseSchema, then sends only those rendered bytes with private/no-store and ETag.
- Bounded source selection: claims query is ORDER BY source_seq ASC LIMIT 129 then slices to 128 with candidate_limit; handback is 1; workshop heads are 5. SQL values are parameter-bound. composePack performs deterministic stable ordering, measures the actual prepared JSON projection to a fixed point, selects whole items only, and fails when mandatory envelope cannot fit. The route independently rejects if item token sum or ceil(final rendered UTF-8 bytes / 4) exceeds tokens_estimate. PackResponseSchema further bounds the fixed bucket and item sum.
- Quarantine: ledger/workshop contract scopes require untrusted:true; composer rejects scope/untrusted inversions; renderProjection always goes through prepareProjection; prepare neutralizes every non-system untrusted body. sanitizer neutralizes active asimp control comments and forged next_actions/why_included envelope keys and reports those transformations. Server-owned next_actions are built by the route. The mounted route never serves composePack canonical_json (which intentionally remains raw internal material).

CONCRETE COUNTEREXAMPLES / REJECT CAUSES:
1) Snapshot/cursor mismatch (active blocker asimposiumorg-8spk): handler reads problems.public_seq first, but its claims query does NOT bind source_seq <= cursor. Interleaving: pack reads cursor N; a promotion commits claim C at source_seq N+1 and advances public_seq; claims SELECT then returns C. Response presents cursor N while including C(N+1). Thus its inclusion, omission, budget, ETag, and neutralization report are not causally bound to the declared cursor. This is a deterministic agent-input failure even though the bucket and escaping controls hold.
2) Own-handback selection is ORDER BY closed_at DESC LIMIT 1 with no total tie break. Two closed sessions for the same problem/fellow with equal closed_at (permitted by 0017) can yield different untrusted handback text for the same logical state. That perturbs face/ETag, omission/budget, and neutralization evidence.
3) Existing route test seeds direct claims while fixture public_seq stays 0. After correct source_seq<=cursor repair it will silently lose those candidates. Current C1/C2..C12/C13..C130 assertions need generation-valid setup, not preservation as a false-green post-fix test.

B. In this handler, bind claims as WHERE problem_id=? AND source_seq<=? ORDER BY source_seq ASC LIMIT ? using the already-read cursor and 129 sentinel. Add a bounded/existence disclosure of generation_not_visible for post-cursor rows, if product wants a reason rather than a silent snapshot cutoff. This is the 8spk repair.
C. Make handback ordering total: ORDER BY closed_at DESC, session_id DESC LIMIT 1. No migration needed because session_id is unique.

CAUSAL PLANTS:
- Real-D1 barrier immediately after cursor SELECT: promote C(N+1) before claims SELECT; first response cursor N must exclude C(N+1) (and disclose generation_not_visible if adopted); a later response at N+1 includes it.
- Generation-valid source setup (advance public_seq through promotion, or explicitly match it): roomy 8K includes hostile C1 and C12; 800 is a stable prefix including C1 but omits C12 with budget_exceeded; 129 short visible claims prove C128 included/C129 excluded with candidate_limit, without budget conflation.

- 1,000 emoji and marker-expansion candidate declared as one token must be excluded at 800 with budget_exceeded; actual JSON UTF-8/4 must remain <= estimate. Equal closed_at handbacks must select declared session_id-DESC winner; private nonempty conditional GET must 304 only while selected bytes stay equal and 200/changed ETag after a causal state change.
