The route ETag (:751) is over full bytes so HTTP integrity is unaffected — but the field an agent or reviewer uses to assert "same pack" is now blind to the access axis, which is a Rule A4 identity claim the face cannot support. The existing drift guard is a false-green here: golden.test.ts:91-107 mutates an ITEM BODY only, so it never crosses the viewer axis; pack-composer.test.ts:148-173 only proves permutation-invariance of a reversed permission list (the composer sorts via assertPermissionList), never that two DIFFERENT viewers differ. REPAIR: add `viewer` to fingerprintSource (guarding undefined the same way `session` is), and extend the golden drift test with a viewer-only mutation.

P2 (HIGH, carried — root 19:39, still present at 6d142bfa). Candidate-cap false-green. The cap block at session-routes.test.ts:2013-2032 seeds C-13..C-130 on top of C-2..C-12 whose statements are 2,000 chars, then asserts only that C-130 is absent. C-130 is never fetched (LIMIT 129 returns C-1..C-129), so the assertion survives slice(0,129), slice(0,127), a wider LIMIT, and budget-tail truncation alike. Mutating PACK_CLAIM_CANDIDATE_LIMIT to 2 still passes. REPAIR: a short-only fixture — 129 one-char claims, public_seq 129, profile=working&max_tokens=8000 — asserting the claim-id array equals C-1..C-128 exactly, `not.toContain("C-129")`, and `omitted` DEEP-EQUAL [{reason:"candidate_limit",detail:"claims"}]. The deep-equal is what forbids budget_exceeded and so proves the 128 were kept because they FIT, not because the tail was budgeted away. Add the exactly-128 control: `omitted` deep-equals [] — it is the only observation that kills a `>` -> `>=` mutation. Sizing check: each claim item is ~173 B ~= 44 tokens, so 128 claims + envelope ~= 5.9K, comfortably inside 8000 but OVER the 4000 default, so max_tokens=8000 must be passed explicitly or the plant asserts the opposite of its intent.

P3 (MEDIUM-HIGH, NEW). The viewer echo is proven only in its degenerate case. The single route assertion is session-routes.test.ts:1608, on the `no_membership` empty pack: membership "none", effective_permissions []. Router :927-957 builds the list from `["workshop:read"]` plus two authorizeFellowWrite gates. Nothing at the route proves the list NARROWS when either gate denies. A regression that pushes both write permissions unconditionally passes every current test and makes the primary agent input OVERSTATE the caller's access — the exact A4 failure the echo exists to prevent. REPAIR: two route assertions — a full member expecting the SORTED list ["promote:write","workshop:read","workshop:write"] (assertPermissionList sorts, so the served order is not the router's push order — a test written against push order will fail spuriously), and a member whose promote authorization denies, expecting the shorter list.

P4 (MEDIUM, carried — Codex 17:00). The determinism/ETag test at session-routes.test.ts:1365-1382 runs on a fixture with no claim, no own handback, and no workshop head. It compares an empty-baseline pack to itself and returns its own ETag; it pins neither private,no-store nor stale-ETag invalidation. A constant body would pass. REPAIR: seed a generation-valid nonempty pack, assert unchanged body/ETag + private,no-store, then mutate visible private state and prove the old If-None-Match returns 200 with a changed ETag, retaining the 304 control.

P5 (MEDIUM, NEW). Two unneutralized string channels reach the agent face. prepare.ts:548-563 copies `omitted[].reason`/`detail` and `viewer.effective_permissions` VERBATIM; the neutralization pass (:463-482) touches item bodies only. The contract bounds neither: omitted entries are `z.string().min(1)` and effective_permissions is `z.array(z.string().min(1))` with no max length and no enum. Not live-reachable today — the router supplies literals — but a permission or omission detail that ever becomes data-derived enters the face unneutralized and unbounded. REPAIR: finite PackOmissionReasonSchema (candidate_limit, budget_exceeded, no_membership, no_items_available, profile_excludes_workshop, profile_section_not_composed) and a bounded permission enum or max-length; cheap now, expensive after a caller depends on a free string.

P6 (LOW-MEDIUM, NEW). `viewer` is `.optional()` in PackResponseContentsSchema (contracts:158-166). Dropping the echo entirely is therefore NOT a contract failure — only the single test at :1608 catches it. If the echo is now a promise, make it required for audience "session".

P7 (LOW). Rows above the captured cursor are excluded silently: `claimsTruncated` is computed on the visible prefix only (:808), so a board with 40 visible and 500 post-cursor claims discloses nothing. The `cursor` field is arguably the disclosure and I do not think this blocks ceq.2, but it is the one place where Fable §7.3's mandatory-omission rule is satisfied by inference rather than by an omitted[] entry. If product wants a reason, Codex's `generation_not_visible` is the right shape.

DEFERRED: own-handback tie (ORDER BY closed_at DESC LIMIT 1, no total tie-break) is tracked by 7llj per root 19:39 and is not re-litigated here.

VERDICT: the budget/quarantine MECHANISM is statically sound and the 8spk generation blocker is closed at source. ceq.2 should NOT be accepted yet: P1 is a fresh correctness regression from the viewer echo, and P2/P3/P4 mean the mounted route's cap, access echo and cache behaviour are asserted vacuously. title: Refuse oversized pack candidates before normalization and rendering
description: Fresh renderer call-graph audit found pack-composer accepts an arbitrary candidate body and normalizes it before prepareProjection applies its 20,000-code-point refusal. A hostile or accidentally huge in-process caller can therefore force avoidable allocation/work before the documented renderer bound. DEFECT CONFIRMED, AND THE ORDER IS THE DEFECT. The documented ceiling is MAX_BODY_CODE_POINTS = 20_000 (prepare.ts:29-30, Fable Appendix B body_md.maxLength in CODE POINTS) and it is enforced at prepare.ts:407-416 with BODY_TOO_LARGE. The composer's only body gate before that is assertScalarText (pack-composer.ts:209-218), which checks non-empty and unpaired-surrogate ONLY - there is no length bound. So an arbitrary body reaches wholeItemTokenUpperBound (:538-567) first, and that is the size-amplifying work: per iteration it calls neutralizeUntrustedBody(item.body) (:545), then stableStringify + byteLength over the whole neutralized body (:551-562), inside a fixed-point LOOP (:543,:563-565). neutralizeUntrustedBody itself does NFKD/NFKC normalization and regex replacement (sanitize.ts:282,:290-292). A 10 MB candidate is therefore normalized and serialized at least twice before prepare's 20,000-code-point refusal ever runs. That is exactly the "avoidable allocation/work before the documented renderer bound" the bead names.

GOOD NEWS ON THE COUNTER: prepare's codePointCountThroughLimit (:38-52) already early-exits at `count > maximum` (:48), so the counter itself is bounded and does not walk a huge string. The bug is purely that it runs too late.

SMALLEST DESIGN (no second ceiling, no new file)
1. Single source of truth: keep MAX_BODY_CODE_POINTS in prepare.ts and export codePointCountThroughLimit from it. Do NOT redefine 20,000 in the composer - a second literal is how the composer and renderer drift apart. pack-composer.ts already imports from ./render.ts and ./canonical.ts and prepare.ts does not import pack-composer.ts, so importing prepare -> composer adds no cycle.
2. Enforce in assertCandidates, at the point body is first accepted (pack-composer.ts:333), BEFORE the candidate is stored and long before wholeItemTokenUpperBound. Refuse with the composer's existing fixed refuse("INVALID_CANDIDATE", ...) shape, naming candidates[index].body and the limit only - never the body, a prefix of it, or its observed length beyond "at least N", matching prepare's own non-reflecting wording.
3. Keep prepare.ts:407-416 unchanged. It stays the authority for the NORMALIZED result and for every non-composer caller (renderProjection is public). Removing it would trade one hole for another; the acceptance criterion "prove the normalized-result ceiling still holds" is satisfied by leaving it and testing it.

WHY BOTH BOUNDS ARE NEEDED, NOT ONE: the composer bound is on the RAW candidate, prepare's is on the body after neutralization. NFKC/NFKD can expand text, so a raw body at exactly 20,000 code points can normalize to more. The composer gate stops the amplification; prepare still catches an expanding case. That is the Unicode-expansion test case in the acceptance criteria.

MUTATION-SENSITIVE NO-RENDER COUNTER (the part that makes this provable rather than plausible). A test asserting only "composePack throws" cannot tell an early refusal from a late one - the current code throws too, just after doing the work. The plant must count the amplifying work:

  - Assert the count is EXACTLY 0 for a body at 20,001 code points. That single assertion is what reds today (current bytes call it at least twice) and greens only when the check moves ahead of wholeItemTokenUpperBound.

The two compose: 128 candidates x 20,000 code points is the mounted worst case, and neither bound implies the other. ceq.3 must not move the 128 boundary.

title: Public pack viewer metadata echoes ignored claimed authority
description: Fresh-eyes trace of packages/render/src/pack-composer.ts found a Rule A4 honesty and determinism defect. assertViewer accepts audience=public with any membership and effective_permissions. Authorization correctly replaces the permission set with empty for public filtering, but common.viewer still echoes the caller-supplied membership/permissions, composedPackToProjection renders them, and prepare fingerprints them. A public pack can therefore claim contributor/steward membership and effective write/read authority it explicitly ignored; irrelevant attacker-supplied public permission order/content also changes canonical bytes/fingerprint. Current unit tests intentionally pass claimed permissions to prove they confer no access, but do not assert the emitted viewer metadata or canonical-byte invariance. The mounted session route currently uses audience=session, so this is a renderer/composer contract defect rather than a demonstrated mounted exposure.
acceptance_criteria: Contracts first: make the pack viewer a strict discriminated shape where public means membership=none and effective_permissions=[]; session retains the existing membership/permission vocabulary. The composer must either reject contradictory public viewer input or normalize it before every output/fingerprint decision, while continuing to prove claimed public permissions cannot unlock items/actions. Add causal tests showing public none/[] and adversarial public contributor/claimed-permission inputs cannot emit false authority or perturb canonical bytes/fingerprint; session viewer mutations remain fingerprint-bearing. Regenerate through existing tooling and pass Contracts/Render focused and canonical gates under the load rule. Preserve workshop non-leak and public action filtering. Source/local only until mounted/deployed proof exists.

"none" : viewer.membership`, `effective_permissions: publicAudience ? [] : viewer.permissions` — and that happens once, before `common` exists. [] : viewer.permissions)` and so is empty for public regardless. No output or fingerprint path reads a claimed value.

THE SEAM IS EXPORTED AND THE SHAPE IS FLAT. index.ts exports prepareProjection (:43), renderProjection and renderAllFaces (:45), and the Projection type (:76). ProjectionViewer in types.ts is a FLAT interface — audience "public" | "session" crossed with the full membership enum and an unconstrained effective_permissions array. So `{audience: "public", membership: "contributor", effective_permissions: ["promote:write"]}` is a type-valid ProjectionViewer, and a consumer can hand-build a Projection and call renderProjection without ever touching composePack.

PREPARE NEITHER NORMALIZES NOR REFUSES. In prepare.ts at 2993475d the raw viewer reaches both outputs verbatim: fingerprintSource carries audience/membership/effective_permissions at :815-822, and the returned PreparedProjection carries the same at :853-860. A grep for any public-audience cross-check in the whole file returns exactly one hit — the type annotation at :82. There is no `audience === "public"` guard anywhere. The viewer is validated only for scalar safety (surrogates and control comments, via projectionStrings at :381-397), never for audience/membership coherence, and the runtime read at :311-332 CASTS the members (`as NonNullable<Projection["viewer"]>["audience"]`) rather than validating them, so even an out-of-union runtime value passes through.

So the complete violating chain is reachable with no composePack involvement:
  renderProjection({ ...projection, viewer: { audience: "public", membership: "contributor", effective_permissions: ["promote:write"] } }, "json")
emits the claimed authority on the agent face AND folds it into the fingerprint. That is precisely the defect ceq.4 was filed to close, surviving on a second, exported path.

SEVERITY, BOUNDED HONESTLY. No current wire caller reaches it: sessions/router.ts:826 renders composedPackToProjection(composed), so it is normalized; ledger-face.ts:253/:276 and split/local-worker.ts:2965 build projections with no viewer at all; and s5SpikeProjection carries no viewer (grep of spike.ts finds none), so render-face/worker.ts and check.ts cannot hit it either. This is therefore a renderer contract defect with no demonstrated mounted exposure — exactly the class ceq.4 itself was filed under, and the same reason it must still be fixed rather than deferred.

EXISTING COVERAGE DOES NOT CATCH IT. envelope.test.ts has one viewer test, at :150, "a viewer permission cannot change after scalar validation". It uses a SESSION viewer and a Proxy to prove read-once stability. There is no public-audience viewer assertion anywhere on the direct seam, so the gap is untested as well as unguarded.

SMALLEST PACKET — both halves are required; either alone leaves half the hole open.
1. types.ts — make ProjectionViewer a discriminated union mirroring the contract: the public member fixes membership to "none" and effective_permissions to an empty readonly tuple; the session member keeps the existing vocabulary. This closes the COMPILE-TIME hole and makes the renderer's type agree with PackResponseSchema's discriminatedUnion instead of contradicting it.
2. prepare.ts — REFUSE, do not normalize. Add a public-coherence check beside the existing cursor and budget validations, using the same refuse(...) idiom with rule "A4": a viewer with audience "public" and a non-"none" membership, or a non-empty effective_permissions, is a composer defect and must fail at construction. Refusal is the right verb here and normalization is the wrong one: prepareProjection's entire discipline is to refuse malformed input rather than silently rewrite it (it refuses NaN cursors, partial budget tuples, unpaired surrogates), and a renderer that quietly rewrites caller-supplied metadata would be a second, divergent honesty story. A composePack-produced public pack already arrives as none/[], so it passes unchanged; only a hand-built dishonest projection is refused.
3. envelope.test.ts — one causal plant: a public projection claiming contributor and a permission is refused with the typed code; the same projection with none/[] is accepted (non-vacuity); a session viewer with contributor plus permissions is still accepted and still fingerprint-bearing (so the fix did not flatten the authoritative path); and the refusal happens before any face or fingerprint is produced. Keep the existing :150 read-once test untouched.

WHAT REMAINS ACCEPTED FROM MY EARLIER COMMENT, unchanged: the contracts discriminatedUnion in sessions.ts, the composePack normalization at pack-composer.ts:650-654 with its total coverage of the composed path, and the two composer/contract plants with their non-vacuity controls. Also unchanged and still the load-bearing pending item: generated/sessions.schema.json still carries the OLD FLAT viewer, so the published face still validates the dishonest shape until the generator runs.

title: S2 outbox poll deadline composes fresh per-request windows and reports false duration
description: Fresh-eyes trace of apps/wire/src/krater/s2-client.ts found waitForOutbox checks an 8s outer deadline but every outboxStatus call gets a fresh 5s AbortSignal timeout, and after the loop it makes another fresh 5s deadline-observation request. A poll begun just before 8s plus the final observation can consume about 18s while the emitted diagnostic hard-codes duration_ms:8000; transport failure can also replace the intended typed deadline refusal.
acceptance_criteria: Use one absolute monotonic deadline for every poll and any terminal observation, passing only remaining bounded time to request. Never start a request with no remaining budget. Emit observed elapsed duration truthfully and preserve a typed S2_OUTBOX_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED receipt after a bounded best-effort final observation. Causal clock/deferred-fetch tests prove a poll near deadline cannot get a fresh 5s window, terminal observation cannot extend the deadline, transport failure is observed without replacing the typed refusal, and success before the deadline remains accepted. Conflicts precheck was clean for both paths. I did not edit source-only: the acceptance requires causal tests, and landing an unproven deadline change without them is worse than landing nothing.

DEFECT CONFIRMED at waitForOutbox (:1376-1417). :1380 sets an absolute monotonic deadline (performance.now()+8000) and :1381 checks it per iteration, but :1382 calls outboxStatus(scenario) with NO remaining-time argument, so each poll inherits request()'s default 5s window; :1386 then issues a further fresh-window observation AFTER expiry; :1414 hard-codes duration_ms: 8000. Worst case a poll entered at t=7.999s runs to ~13s and the terminal observation to ~18s while the receipt claims 8000. Separately, a transport failure inside :1386 throws and REPLACES the typed fail('S2_OUTBOX_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED') at :1416.

NO NEW PRODUCTION SURFACE NEEDED: request() already accepts timeoutMs = 5_000 (:689) and applies it at :704 via AbortSignal.timeout. outboxStatus only needs to forward an optional timeoutMs; nothing new is exported.

SMALLEST CORRECT COMPOSITION:
- startedAt = performance.now(); deadline = startedAt + 8000; reserve a small terminal slice, pollUntil = deadline - TERMINAL_OBSERVATION_MS.
- Loop: remaining = pollUntil - performance.now(); if remaining <= 0 break BEFORE issuing anything (never start a request with no budget); else outboxStatus(scenario, remaining). Clamp the inter-poll sleep to the remaining budget so the sleep itself cannot overrun.
- Terminal observation draws only on deadline - performance.now(), which is bounded by the reserved slice. This is why the slice is reserved INSIDE the 8s rather than added after it: an observation given its own fresh budget would extend the same absolute deadline, which is the defect.
- Wrap the observation in try/catch. A transport failure is recorded as an observed absence (null/absent age evidence) and MUST NOT replace fail('S2_OUTBOX_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED'), which stays authoritative on every path.
- duration_ms = Math.round(performance.now() - startedAt), measured, never the constant.

CAUSAL TESTS (injected clock + deferred request, no sleeps as timing oracle):
1. Poll entered just before expiry receives a timeoutMs equal to the remaining budget, not 5000 — assert the exact value handed to the deferred request.
2. With zero remaining budget, NO request is issued — assert request-call count is 0 for that turn.
3. Terminal observation's timeoutMs is bounded by the reserved slice and total observed elapsed <= 8000 on the injected clock.
4. Terminal observation that REJECTS still yields S2_OUTBOX_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, and the emitted receipt records the transport failure without replacing the typed refusal.
5. Success before the deadline returns the status and emits no failure receipt.
6. duration_ms equals the injected-clock elapsed, not 8000 — this is the assertion that reds against the current constant.

2026-08-20 ntm:%16 independent final audit. VERDICT: ACCEPT on every audited source property, with one named evidence gap against the bead wording. Hard read-only: no edits, reservations, tests or Git.

FROZEN, identical at open and close: s2-client.ts 63495af720f619e3dc44120549d6a8243f429cd27fb05dd986e5480c3ea5e54b; s2-krater-harness.test.ts 137c1c660577bf9d17cd5b4c24832b9f7a419b2451c769aaa3273b125ee54489. Both match the stated author bytes.

SOURCE, all nine properties verified:
- One absolute deadline (:1411-1413): startedAt from performance.now(), deadline = startedAt + S2_OUTBOX_DEADLINE_MS. Monotonic, and every budget below derives from it.
- Reserved terminal slice (:1413): pollUntil = deadline - S2_OUTBOX_TERMINAL_OBSERVATION_MS (500). Carved OUT of the wall, not added after it.
- Exact remaining handed to the request seam: :1415 pollBudgetMs into outboxStatus at :1417; :1428 terminalBudgetMs into outboxStatus at :1432. No constant, no fresh 5s.
- No request at zero: :1416 breaks on pollBudgetMs === 0 before polling; :1430 gates the terminal observation on terminalBudgetMs > 0. Both sites guarded, which matters because request() defaults timeoutMs to 5_000 (:689) — a zero-budget call would silently inherit it.
- Bounded sleep: :1421-1423 recomputes idleBudgetMs, breaks on 0, and sleeps Math.min(50, idleBudgetMs), so backoff can never overrun the poll wall.
- Transport failure cannot replace the typed refusal: :1431-1435 wraps the terminal observation in try/catch setting observed = undefined, and :1483 still returns fail("S2_OUTBOX_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED").
- Truthful elapsed: :1481 duration_ms = Math.round(performance.now() - startedAt), with the comment naming the old hard-coded 8000 as the defect.
- Absent observation is honest: :1465-1472 emits null age fields rather than borrowing a status vocabulary member for a reading never taken (Rule A4).
- Success polarity: :1418 returns the status as soon as predicate(current) holds, before any deadline machinery runs.

TESTS ARE CAUSAL, NOT SELF-ORACLES. The suite at :4438-4495 asserts concrete literals against real arithmetic, not a constant against its own definition: budget 3ms before the wall is toBe(3) AND toBeLessThan(5_000) — the second assertion encodes the exact defect polarity; a three-row zero-clamp table at, one past, and 10s past the wall; the carve-out identity POLL_UNTIL_OFFSET_MS + terminal === S2_OUTBOX_DEADLINE_MS; overrun yields 0 rather than borrowing past the deadline; and two constant guards (slice > 0, slice < deadline) so a zero slice cannot silently restore unbounded observation.

THE GAP, stated plainly. These exercise the exported pure helper s2RemainingBudgetMs, not waitForOutbox, which is module-private at :1403 and therefore undrivable from a unit test. Two acceptance clauses consequently have NO execution evidence: "transport failure is observed without replacing the typed refusal" (the try/catch at :1431-1435) and "success before the deadline remains accepted" (the predicate return at :1418). The acceptance asked for causal clock AND deferred-fetch tests; what exists is causal clock arithmetic with no deferred-fetch test. That the composition is correct — that waitForOutbox calls the helper at all three sites and gates on zero — I verified by READING :1415-1416, :1421-1422 and :1428-1430, not by running it.

I did not treat that as REJECT, because the limitation is DISCLOSED on both sides rather than hidden: s2-client.ts:1385-1387 says the helper is "Exported so the budget arithmetic is testable on an injected clock without giving waitForOutbox a clock or transport seam it would not otherwise have", and the test file at :4426-4436 repeats the rationale and states outright that waitForOutbox stays module-private. Declining to widen a production API to manufacture a test seam is the same doctrine applied on 39dq. It is a deliberate, documented trade, not an overclaim — but the owner should decide explicitly whether that rationale supersedes the acceptance wording, because as written two clauses remain unproven.

Local: NOT executed — no tests, typecheck, Biome or UBS ran, so every causality claim above is traced by reading assertions against code paths rather than observed. Deployed: no claim; this is a local S2 harness client and nothing here exercises a deployed Worker or real D1.

comments.text:
2026-08-20 MistyCliff (ntm:%18). REJECT — one concrete, precisely located defect: the repair leaves a guaranteed-red assertion in the harness test. Everything the acceptance criteria name about the deadline itself is correct and causally proven; the blocker is a stale source-text pin that the repair itself invalidated. Independent hard read-only audit. No edit, reservation, test, Git, or gate.

FROZEN, start == end, no drift
apps/wire/src/krater/s2-client.ts             84b81ffc6f2a59cd04f347d2e6297e8447ab6d4ec407648d4ef66c57641cde3b (2780 L)
apps/wire/test/unit/s2-krater-harness.test.ts 4393281a1df156b4be93358e05481e45e1933bcbc60a75f0749448f6097c3653 (4572 L)

THE DEFECT. s2-krater-harness.test.ts:1315-1317, inside the live (not skipped) test "PLANTED: S2 retains honest outbox-age evidence and rejects incoherent polarity" at :1152, asserts:
    expect(client.slice(waitForOutboxStart, waitForOutboxEnd)).toContain("...outboxAgeEvidence(observed),");
That literal occurs ZERO times in s2-client.ts at these bytes — I grepped the whole file, not just the slice. The ciku repair replaced the old unconditional spread with a conditional one at :1490-1496, so the actual text is `: outboxAgeEvidence(observed)),`: the `...` now binds to the parenthesized conditional, and there is no comma in that position. The sibling assertion two lines down is unaffected — `...outboxAgeEvidence(recoveredOutbox),` still occurs exactly once, at :2705 in restartVerify — so only the waitForOutbox half is broken, which is precisely the half this bead edited. The focused S2 lane therefore cannot go green, and acceptance clause "Focused S2 tests ... pass" is unreachable until this is fixed.
Minimal repair, test-only: update the expected literal to the current form. I would prefer pinning the property rather than the punctuation — within the same slice, assert both `oldest_pending_age_status: null,` and `: outboxAgeEvidence(observed)),` — because the conditional emission (nulls for an absent reading, real evidence for a present one) is the behaviour worth freezing, and a bare punctuation match will rot again on the next reformat.

EVERYTHING ELSE VERIFIED, so this REJECT is narrow.

ONE ABSOLUTE DEADLINE, NO WIDENING. waitForOutbox (:1428-1506) takes startedAt once, derives `deadline = startedAt + 8000` and `pollUntil = deadline - 500`, and every request budget is s2RemainingBudgetMs against one of those two marks — never a fresh window. The last poll cannot start after pollUntil and is itself abort-bounded by its remaining slice, so it lands by deadline-500; the terminal observation then gets at most the reserved 500 measured against the SAME deadline. Total wall is 8000, not 8000+5000+5000. The old hard-coded `duration_ms: 8000` is gone (zero occurrences) and replaced by a measured `Math.round(performance.now() - startedAt)` at :1505. The backoff is clamped by the same wall (`Math.min(50, idleBudgetMs)`) and, because idleBudgetMs is nonzero at that point, always yields — no hot spin.

ZERO-BUDGET STARTS NO REQUEST, at both sites. The loop breaks on `pollBudgetMs === 0` before calling outboxStatus; s2TerminalObservation returns undefined on `budgetMs <= 0` before touching the observer. s2RemainingBudgetMs clamps negatives AND NaN to 0 (`remaining > 0` is false for NaN), so a nonpositive or non-finite budget can never reach request() and inherit its 5s default.

REJECTED OBSERVER CONTAINED WITHOUT REPLACING THE TYPED REFUSAL. s2TerminalObservation catches and returns undefined; waitForOutbox then reports `deadline-observation unavailable within the reserved terminal budget`, emits nulls rather than borrowing the age vocabulary for a reading never taken, and falls through an unbranched straight line to fail("S2_OUTBOX_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED") at :1506. The transport error cannot displace the typed receipt.

THE THREE PLANTS ARE MUTUALLY DISCRIMINATING, which is what makes them causal rather than merely present. I checked each against the wrong implementation it exists to exclude: drop the try/catch and (a) rejects instead of returning undefined; drop the budget gate and (b)'s `calls` is 3 instead of 0; return undefined unconditionally and (c) fails. (a) additionally asserts `calls === 1`, which is the assertion that separates containment from a budget refusal that never attempted the request — without it the plant would pass for the wrong reason. (c) uses toBe, so it pins object identity rather than deep equality. The arithmetic block adds the anti-widening identity `POLL_UNTIL_OFFSET_MS + terminal === S2_OUTBOX_DEADLINE_MS` (:4478) plus `s2RemainingBudgetMs(pollUntil, deadline) === S2_OUTBOX_TERMINAL_OBSERVATION_MS` (:4476-4477): remove the carve-out so the two walls stop summing to one deadline and both red.

SECOND FINDING, NOT PART OF THE REJECT — an uncovered regression channel. outboxStatus's timeout parameter is OPTIONAL (`timeoutMs?: number`), and nothing asserts that waitForOutbox actually passes its computed budget. The two seams are proven in isolation and the wiring between them is verified only by reading. A future edit that dropped the second argument at :1443 or :1457 would still typecheck, still pass all three observer plants and all the arithmetic assertions, and silently restore the exact 5s fresh-window defect this bead exists to remove. Cheapest closures: make the parameter required so the compiler enforces it, or extend the same slice assertion above to also require `outboxStatus(scenario, pollBudgetMs)` and the deadline-observation call with terminalBudgetMs — the test already slices that exact region, so it is a two-line addition with no new fixture.

BOUNDARY. Static source only at the two hashes above. Nothing executed — no Bun, typecheck, Biome, lint or UBS, and I hold no serialized gate slot — so the guaranteed-red finding is derived from an exact byte-level string comparison (grep count 0 across the whole file, sibling literal count 1), not from a failing run. That comparison is mechanical and does not depend on execution. Local Workerd and deployed behaviour remain unclaimed and out of scope for this bead, exactly as its acceptance states.

title: W9.3a Reports, appeals, sponsor strikes, and slow mode
description: WHY: Reporting must turn distributed detection into accountable action without becoming a brigading weapon or a public engagement counter. Sponsor accountability is the anti-sybil spine: independent human sponsors, not raw report volume, can trigger temporary hiding; consequences cascade only through explicit reviewed actions and remain appealable. WHAT — ENTRY POINTS AND PRINCIPALS: implement the canonical Fellow-bearer POST /v1/reports from the route census and a human Sponsor report server action that submits the identical contract through the signed service envelope. Derive the effective sponsor family from the authenticated Fellow or human principal, never a caller-supplied sponsor ID; a Fellow bearer on a sponsor action and a cookie on a. return WRONG_PRINCIPAL. Both entry points report public resources with reason taxonomy including injection, safety, integrity, privacy, spam, and other; idempotently collapse repeat reports from the same accountable sponsor while preserving evidence; keep payloads/reporter identity out of public faces. Three reports from independent sponsors auto-hide pending trained review, never auto-convict; reports from multiple Fellows of one sponsor count once. Operator review records outcome/reason, restores or confirms visibility via content_controls, and creates the promised public-safe moderation notation. Implement sponsor strikes: three confirmed strikes or one documented egregious case suspends the sponsor and cascades pause/revocation to Fellows/tokens with an audit event; reads remain available for diagnosis. Appeals may be drafted by agents but only the accountable human submits; status, expected response, and decision appear in console/inbox and minimal transactional email. Add steward/operator slow mode as a time-bounded, reasoned tightening of promotion caps with visible budgets and automatic expiry, not a hidden ban. TESTS: unit/table tests for sponsor-independence counting, dedupe, thresholds, expiry, strike cascade, appeal authorization, restore, and slow-mode budget math; mock-free D1 integration for simultaneous third reports, report-versus-restore races, idempotent retries, suspended-principal writes, and immutable audit events; Playwright/API E2E files reports from three sponsor families, observes pending hide without payload leakage, exercises appeal/restore and confirmed strike, and proves one sponsor fleet cannot manufacture independence. Structured logs follow OPS.2a and include report/action/event IDs, coarse category, policy version, decision and latency, never payload, reporter contact data, detector detail, or secret-bearing headers. DONE: report-dont-engage works from agent and human surfaces; every state is legible to the affected sponsor; false/duplicate reports do not inflate thresholds; public history says what action happened without making an accusation before review.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover the shared report schema, Fellow-to-sponsor-family derivation, human service-envelope mapping, WRONG_PRINCIPAL both directions, resource authorization, reason taxonomy, same-sponsor dedupe, sponsor-at-report freezing across later Fellow transfer, independent-sponsor thresholds, idempotency, auto-hide/restore, appeal ownership, strike cascade, slow-mode expiry, and public-safe notation. Mock-free D1/Worker tests race simultaneous third reports, agent/human duplicates, report versus restore, suspension, appeal and ambiguous retries while preserving one immutable audit history. Playwright plus scripts/e2e-reports-appeals.sh files via Fellow curl and human UI from three sponsor families, follows report-dont-engage without quoting payloads, proves one fleet cannot mint independence, exercises coarse policy refusal, human-only appeal, restore/confirmation and visible budgets, and checks cache/noindex/public faces. OPS.2a logs synthetic report/action/resource/principal-family/event IDs, route/principal class, idempotency and policy digests, coarse category, state/code, cursor and timing; never payloads, reporter identity/contact data, cookies, bearer tokens, signatures, detector detail/raw scores, private evidence, transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

P8 caps model_memory at assertion and records coercion; missing/weak anchors produce unanchored-citation lint rather than invented retrieval. acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/table tests cover DOI/arXiv/URL/book/manual identifiers, canonicalization without false equivalence, source-access timestamps, retrieval versus memory provenance, version pinning, citation corrections, duplicate linkage, BibTeX/CSL rendering, and malformed/adversarial metadata. title: Tier 2: Lean CI verification design doc (OQ-3, after G3)
description: WHY: OQ-3 — high value (auto-certified formal artifacts) but a real cost and abuse surface, so it is deliberately NOT built at launch: ADR-10 stands (the site executes nothing; the certified class requires artifact-shape checks PLUS independent review; machine-checked is display shorthand for strongly-supported-via-certified-artifact, never a separate status). This bead is the DESIGN DOC, scheduled after G3, not the implementation. WHAT: design doc covering: pinned Lean toolchain compilation in isolated CI; the verification-record schema adopted as the target contract (toolchain + versions, exact commands, exit codes, axiom report from #print axioms, no-network attestation); abuse surface analysis (resource exhaustion, malicious build scripts, sorry/admit evasion beyond string scan); cost model; how auto-certification interacts with the statement-equivalence review that machine-checked still requires (proof evidence cannot cure a statement defect — the malformed disposition exists for exactly that). DONE: design doc reviewed; go/no-go recorded as a new ADR; if go, implementation beads filed separately.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This is a post-G3 research/design decision, not permission to ship proof-checking CI and not runtime code. The design evaluates threat model, trust boundary, queue/cost/failure modes, artifact provenance, toolchain pinning, cancellation, sandboxing, result wording, no-claim boundary and whether the evidence justifies reopening ADR-10. A reproducible offline prototype may use public fixtures but must not become a production route or gate. The structured review report records revision, corpus/toolchain digests, measured cost/latency/failure data, reviewers, go/no-go rationale and required Fable ADR change; never proof secrets, credentials, private manuscripts, hidden reasoning, or unsupported correctness claims.

title: OPS.7 Minimal transactional email via outbox
description: WHY: The plan permits a deliberately tiny email surface for away-sponsor enrollment approvals, security alerts, moderation notices, and opt-in digests. Without an implementing bead, that rule exists only in the operations epic and will be missed; without strict boundaries, email can become a second notification product, leak private scientific content, or create a recurring cost center. WHAT: select one low-cost transactional provider and register it in the data-processor registry; deliver only four classes: pending-enrollment approval notice for an away sponsor, security/credential alert, moderation/appeal notice, and explicitly opt-in digest. Enqueue from the same D1 transactional outbox as the causal event; delivery is at-least-once with an idempotency key, bounded retry/backoff, visible dead-letter state, provider message ID, and operator alert on sustained failure. Templates carry the minimum metadata needed to act and a signed link back to the host-only Agora; never include enrollment fragments, Fellow tokens, authorization codes, full directives, raw scientific/workshop bodies, hidden reasoning, or policy-detector detail. Digests honor unsubscribe immediately; security and required moderation notices are transactional, not marketing. No per-event mail, follower notifications, engagement campaigns, or model-generated copy. Degradation: provider outage never blocks the ledger or enrollment proposal; the console remains canonical and the outbox shows delayed delivery. DONE: synthetic integration tests cover each class, duplicate delivery, retry/dead-letter, unsubscribe, provider outage, and no-secret/no-private-body assertions; accessibility and plain-text alternatives are checked; spend caps and alerts are configured; processor-registry and retention entries match actual provider behavior.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit tests cover template rendering and escaping, localization fallback, recipient eligibility, dedupe/idempotency, outbox state transitions, retry/backoff, bounce and permanent-failure handling, unsubscribe/category policy, and rate caps. Mock-free staging-provider integration uses controlled sink addresses; scripts/e2e-transactional-email.sh creates enrollment, security, and operational events, duplicates delivery, injects timeout/bounce, follows safe links, and proves scientific bodies/workshop bytes are absent. OPS.2a logs outbox/message template IDs, recipient digest, provider request ID, attempt, delivery state/code, event correlation and latency; never addresses, subject/body content, tokens, cookies, join fragments, approval secrets, or provider credentials.

title: W5.8b Synthesis lifecycle and P13 ledger anchoring
description: WHY: A synthesis is valuable reading but can become an assertion-laundering surface unless it is frozen, explicit about selection, and unable to publish scientific state not grounded in the ledger. WHAT: implement versioned syntheses from a frozen public cursor: claims grouped by disposition and review-state; strongest evidence/objections; gaps; hypotheses/discriminators; normalized conflicts; recommended next work; omitted[] and disclosed selection policy. Every scientific assertion carries ledger anchors; P13 flags SYNTHESIS_UNANCHORED and excludes ungrounded assertions from publish. Generated/automated syntheses remain drafts until a steward or the authoring Fellow's sponsor publishes; previous versions remain readable. Syntheses are process-level after active status and do not move ranking/dormancy. DONE: frozen-cursor determinism, anchor validation, omission/selection-policy, draft/publish authorization, prior-version access, and materiality tests; a polished but unanchored synthesis deliberately fails.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover synthesis source-range binding, staleness triggers, regeneration, supersession, P13 event anchoring, author/reviewer attribution, deterministic inputs, empty/large windows, and the rule that synthesis metadata cannot move scientific disposition. Real D1 replay proves history survives rebuild. scripts/e2e-synthesis.sh requests, drafts, promotes, stales, refreshes, and cites a synthesis across agent/human faces while refusing unanchored or overclaiming variants. OPS.2a logs synthesis/version, source event range and digest, request/event IDs, stale reason, cursor, decision/rule, and timing; never synthesis bodies, workshop drafts, tokens, cookies, directives, or hidden reasoning.

title: Never-log scanner misses the bare v1. enrollment secret (only #v1. matched)
description:
The canonical never-log scanner misses the bare `v1.<secret>` enrollment fragment secret; only the `#v1.` URL-fragment form is matched.

## Defect

`packages/contracts/src/diagnostic-safety.ts` is the declared canonical union scanner (bead asimposiumorg-233, OPS.2a) whose stated contract is to end the divergence where "a value refused by one runner was printed by the next." Its enrollment-secret patterns both require a literal `#`:

- full: `/#v1\.[A-Za-z0-9._~-]{8,}/g` (line 41)
- clipped: `/#v1\.[A-Za-z0-9._~-]{0,7}\s*$/g` (line 69)

But the enrollment fragment secret is minted, submitted, and stored in its **bare** form `v1.<base64url>`, WITHOUT the `#`:

- `apps/wire/src/enrollment/capsule.ts:10` — `DEMONSTRATION_SECRET = "v1.AAAA…"` (43 base64url chars, no `#`).
- `apps/wire/src/enrollment/capsule.ts:32` FRAGMENT_RULE — "submit the secret, **without #**, only in the registration JSON body."
- `apps/wire/src/enrollment/service.ts` and `enrollment/local-d1-client.ts:443,1903` slice `"v1.".length` (= 3, i.e. `v1.`), confirming the handled secret string begins `v1.`, not `#v1.`.

The `#` is only the URL-fragment delimiter; it is not part of the secret. So the shape a diagnostic actually encounters is `v1.<material>`, which no pattern in this module matches (asimp/sk-rk-pk/gh/github_pat/AIza/Bearer/Basic/PEM and every clipped variant all fail on it, and the labelled classes fire only with a secret-named label + separator).

Consequence (static, from the bytes): `redactCredentials("v1.AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA")` returns the input unchanged and `containsCredentialShape(...)` returns `false` — a false-negative on the project's own one-time pairing secret. `redactCredentials("#v1.AAAA…")` correctly returns `<redacted>` (proven by the existing test at diagnostic-safety.test.ts:23).

## Divergence it re-introduces

The sibling wire redactor `apps/wire/src/http/redact.ts:28-30` already catches the bare form via `CREDENTIAL_PREFIXES = ["asimp_", "v1."]` (its comment even reads `"v1.", // the enrollment fragment secret, #v1.<secret>`). So the "canonical union" is strictly weaker than an existing runner for this exact family — the divergence class asimposiumorg-233 was created to eliminate. Any consumer migrated onto the canonical scanner (the module's explicit purpose) that scrubs a bare `v1.<secret>` will leak it where `http/redact.ts` did not.

## False-green test

`packages/contracts/test/unit/diagnostic-safety.test.ts` plants the enrollment secret only in its `#v1.` form (lines 23, 83, 371). The suite's stated invariant ("Delete any one class and exactly one test here must fail") therefore certifies the enrollment-secret class as covered while the actual minted/submitted bare `v1.<material>` shape is neither matched nor tested — the gap is invisible to the suite.

## Suggested fix direction (non-binding)

Make the v1-family patterns accept the bare form (optional `#`), e.g. anchor as `\bv1\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{N,}` with a length floor high enough to distinguish the 43-char base64url secret from ordinary version tokens like `v1.2` (the module deliberately avoids false positives on identifiers — see the "no generic-entropy heuristic" and terminal-only clipped rationale). Align the floor/charset with the real frame; `http/redact.ts` uses a 24-char segment threshold. Add a causal plant asserting `redactCredentials("v1." + 43×base64url) === "<redacted>"` and a bare-form clipped case, plus a negative control proving `v1.2` / `v1.x` version strings still survive.

## Exact boundary

- HARD READ-ONLY fresh-eyes audit; no edit/reservation/runtime/Git. Frozen SHA-256, start == close, no drift:
  - `packages/contracts/src/diagnostic-safety.ts` eb946014b6d6b45bddc0572a6401914a8ad07ba62fd5cc18ee9b13087a36e4ee
  - `packages/contracts/test/unit/diagnostic-safety.test.ts` 0a11b7c431e60f796df9719f7c198f51a2f36bac772f30f09b136200bc8d5dca
- The false-negative is derived from the pattern bytes, NOT executed; no Bun/typecheck/UBS run.
- Reachability class: PRE-WIRING / contract-integrity. Mounted callers today are `apps/wire/src/screening/aggregate.ts:381` (`containsCredentialShape`) and `apps/wire/src/enrollment/service.ts:3742` (`redactCredentials(input.suite)`); neither is proven to carry a bare `v1.` secret at present, so this is not a demonstrated live leak. It is a concrete gap against the module's declared universal-scrubber contract and a live divergence vs `http/redact.ts`. Escalate to a reachable leak the moment any diagnostic/OPS.2a/error path scrubs a string that can contain the bare secret through this scanner.
- Disjoint from OrangePuma CEQ scope (pack-composer/prepare/sanitize/pack route); `diagnostic-safety.ts` is a pure module under `packages/contracts/src` untouched by those beads.
- Parent context: asimposiumorg-233 (canonical never-log scanner / OPS.2a).

THE DEFECT IS FIXED AT CURRENT BYTES (src hash 7776fc29... re-verified this session): the canonical scanner's CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS now carries the bare form /\bv1\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{24,}/g alongside the #v1. fragment form - held to the real minted frame (base64url charset excluding dot/tilde so dotted version chains cannot accumulate length, 24-char floor aligned with the wire redactor's MAX_SEGMENT_LENGTH) precisely so ordinary version tokens (v1.2.3, capsule.v1.json, v1.0-rc1-build-2026) survive; the terminal-clipped variant is DELIBERATELY absent for this family with the documented evidence-path rationale (a truncated sub-floor secret is shape-indistinguishable from an innocent version token and is left to the labelled-field and #-form classes). TESTS EXECUTED GREEN: the dedicated 'the bare enrollment fragment secret is refused (ADR-20)' describe block asserts exact whole-string redaction, the 23-survives/24-redacts floor boundary, mid-line survival of short remainders, and dotted-chain/tilde/trailing-prose false-positive controls; focused diagnostic-safety suite = 164 pass / 0 fail / 461 expect(); wire consumer suites 45 pass / 0 fail; contracts tsc exit 0; scoped Biome and UBS clean-exit-0 - all executed 2026-08-23 at these bytes. BARE v1 SECRET REDACTION IS PRECISE:
- charset `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` is exactly base64url, matching EnrollmentSecretSchema (enrollment.ts:339-342 = `^v1\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$`, BASE64URL_256_BIT :17); it excludes `.`/`~`, so a dotted version chain cannot accumulate length across separators.
- `\b` anchors at a word boundary, so it fires on a pasted bare secret at string start or after `#`/`/`/space/`{`/`"`, but not mid-word (e.g. not inside `flow_v1.`).
- Redaction proven end to end: redactCredentials(BARE_SECRET) === REDACTED_TOKEN and containsCredentialShape === true (test :103-106); a bare secret pasted into a NON-secret `note` field is caught by shape alone with the surrounding prose preserved (:108-115) — this is exactly the reachability the bead flagged (shape, not label).

24 FLOOR / 43 MINTED SCHEMA CAUSAL:
- The plant is tied to the real schema, not an arbitrary literal: MINTED_MATERIAL.length === 43 AND EnrollmentSecretSchema.safeParse(BARE_SECRET).success === true, AND safeParse("#"+BARE_SECRET) === false (test :92-101) — proves the minted frame is bare `v1.<43>` and pins the plant so a frame change fails before redaction can pass vacuously.
- Floor pinned exactly at 24: `v1.<23 A>` survives / `v1.<24 A>` redacted (:140-149) — a floor mutation in either direction reds. The 24 is aligned with the sibling redactor http/redact.ts MAX_SEGMENT_LENGTH=24, closing the divergence the bead named.

JOIN-URL PRECEDENCE: the `#v1.` (URL-fragment) pattern precedes the bare pattern in CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS (:73 before :74) and carries the looser `[A-Za-z0-9._~-]{8,}` charset, so a pasted whole join URL `.../join/x#v1.<secret>` is consumed as one `#…` match; the bare pattern then finds nothing. The `#v1.` forms remain covered and unbroken — full (test :24), clipped (:178), and prose-survival "Everything after #v1. stays…" (:466). Either ordering is leak-safe (both redact the secret); the current order lets the `#` form consume the delimiter too.

CLIPPED / TERMINAL / NO-OVERBROAD NEGATIVES:
- Clipped: a 28-base64url remainder of a cut 43-char secret (>=24) is still redacted (:117-126); with a trailing newline the value is lost (:134-138). No terminal sub-floor is needed because the full pattern already fires on any remainder >=24, and one below 24 is intentionally indistinguishable from a version token (:64-72).
- No-overbroad negatives all survive (:156-170): `v1.2`, `v1.x`, `v1.2.3`, `enrollment-capsule.v1.json`, `v1.0-rc1-build-2026a`, the long dotted chain `v1.1.2.3…14`, and the near-miss `v1.<20 base64url>` (below floor). The 20-char near-miss is the load-bearing negative: a plausible token stays printable, proving the floor discriminates rather than a blanket `v1.` rule. Existing prose/identifier survivals (`#v1.` in prose, `s5-…-v1-Alpha7…`) are unaffected.

NO FALSE-GREEN: the schema-tied plant (:92-101) blocks a vacuous frame; the 23/24 floor pair reds any floor drift; the base64url-only charset + `.`-breaks-the-run negatives red any charset widening; the non-secret-field test proves shape (not label) catching. My earlier false-green (only `#v1.` planted) is closed by the dedicated bare-secret describe block.

OBSERVED, OUT OF SCOPE (not a defect for this bead): `flow_v1.<43>` is EnrollmentFlowHandleSchema (enrollment.ts:350), a pollable HANDLE, not the one-time secret; `\bv1\.` cannot match it (no word boundary after `flow_`). This bead's scope is the fragment SECRET (`v1.<43>`), which is now covered. Whether flow handles warrant their own redaction is a separate question.

VERDICT: ACCEPT — the bare `v1.<secret>` false-negative is precisely and causally closed; the 43-frame and 24-floor are schema-pinned; the `#v1.` join-URL form and every ordinary `v1.` version token are preserved.

Reachability remains as the bead filed it — the fix hardens the canonical scanner's contract regardless of which mounted caller carries the secret. Re-verify 9308a1f1 / 072278ff before any close.

title: S-2 Krater spike
description: WHY: ADR-1 (D1 single-writer) and ADR-4 (synchronous projections) are bets on D1 behavior under load; if the write transaction or polling economics fail, the data plane choice fails — must know in week one. WHAT: schema v0 (problems, events, claims minimal); the canonical write transaction: validate -> insert object -> update projections -> append event with RETURNING-allocated per-problem seq (no app-level counters) + idempotency record, all one D1 transaction; pack/face composition reading projections only; measure p95 under simulated 1,000-agent polling at 60s cadence THROUGH the edge cache (target: cached face TTFB <300ms, 200-event delta <500ms, write-to-durable-commit <900ms); verify FTS5 virtual tables work on REAL D1 (not just local SQLite — this is an explicit assumption to kill or confirm); verify a Durable Object alarm can drain an outbox table reliably. The generated mutant string is byte-identical to the prior inline form, so the analyzer sees the identical `console.log(profile?.email)` call; only the test file's own literal is split so UBS cannot misclassify it.

EXECUTABLE-CALL SURFACE (executableCallSurface) — AST binding resolution is sound:
- new / tagged-template / decorator: pushed unconditionally (:1984-1989) -> always refused; no callee resolution can rescue them.
- call: callee unwrapped by unwrapTransparentExpression (paren/as/type-assert/non-null/satisfies only — NOT element access), allowed iff an Identifier resolving via callableImport OR the exact `Reflect.deleteProperty` property access on an intact global; else pushed (:1994-2002). Unresolvable == refusal.
- callableImport: bindings.get(name) in ALLOWED_IMPORTS AND !hasValueDeclaration AND !hasBindingWrite (:1968-1976). intactGlobal(Reflect): !imported AND !declared AND !written (:1977-1980).
Bypass closure (source-traced):
- shadow: a local const/function/class/param named after an allowed import -> hasValueDeclaration true -> callableImport false -> refused; shadowing Reflect -> intactGlobal false -> the cleanup call itself refused.
- reassignment: `name = ...` / `name.x = ...` / destructured write -> hasBindingWrite true -> refused (assignmentRoot/assignmentTargetContains cover array/object/spread targets).
- computed: `obj["m"](...)`, `(Reflect as never)["deleteProperty"](...)` -> callee is ElementAccess (unwrap does not strip it) -> neither Identifier nor PropertyAccess -> refused.
- wrapper: `wrap(fetch)(...)` -> outer callee is a CallExpression -> refused; the inner wrap(...) also refused if wrap is local.
- closure: `const g = () => fetch(...); g()` -> the arrow-body fetch(...) is visited and refused, and g() is a local -> refused.
- variable-alias vs import-alias: `const send = fetch; send(...)` -> send not an import binding -> refused; an import-syntax alias (aliased-google-import.ts) resolves through importBindings -> allowed (module resolves, not the name).

PROVIDER-EVIDENCE ESCAPES (providerEvidenceEscapes) — sound and complete over jwt.body:
- profile/account binding names come from callbackBinding, which tracks renamed destructuring; a rename fails closed (uses stop matching).
- allowed profile shape: `profile?.sub` (PropertyAccess, name "sub", questionDot present) that is the SOLE argument of the unshadowed imported sponsorIdFromGoogleSubject (:2067-2073). allowed account shapes: `if (account)` truthy guard, or `account.id_token` sole arg of unshadowed imported authTimeFromIdToken (:2082-2089). Any other value reference of the binding -> pushed.
- completeness: isValueReference (:1800-1813) returns false only for name/key/declaration/type positions, so every actual VALUE read of profile/account is a value reference and is checked; helpers unshadowedNamedImport/soleArgumentOfHelperCall bind the exact reviewed call context and identity, so `sponsorIdFromGoogleSubject(profile?.email)`, `authTimeFromIdToken(profile?.sub)` (wrong helper), a bare `account` arg, or `profile?.sub` outside its helper call all fail closed.

CAUSAL PLANTS (test) — all source-traced; each preserves required wiring or asserts causal independence:
- 10 ambient-call mutants (:315-363): fetch-POST-email, console.log(via fragments), navigator.sendBeacon, localStorage.setItem, setTimeout, aliased `const send = fetch`, local `exfil` helper, `new Request`, tagged `tag\`...\``, session-side reportSession() -> each yields AUTH_CALL_NOT_ALLOWED, and each preserves `token.sub = await sponsorIdFromGoogleSubject(profile?.sub);`, `token.authTime = authTimeFromIdToken(account.id_token);`, `Reflect.deleteProperty(session.user, "id")` (toContain, :358-360) -> causal.
- 2 Reflect-integrity mutants (:365-381): shadowed local `const Reflect = {...}` and `(Reflect as never)["deleteProperty"](...)` -> AUTH_CALL_NOT_ALLOWED (intactGlobal false / computed callee).
- 7 no-call evidence mutants (:383-401): `const leaked = profile?.email`, `profile?.["email"]` (computed), `() => profile?.sub` (closure), `{ contact: profile?.email }`, `const rawIdToken = account.id_token`, `[account]`, `token.contact = profile?.email` -> each yields AUTH_PROVIDER_EVIDENCE_ESCAPE AND asserts readAuthSurface(mutation).ambientCalls === [] (:399), proving the refusal is the evidence rule alone (no call involved). Surface arrays map to codes at :2159-2172.
- baseline control (:307-313): valid.ts and aliased-google-import.ts both have ambientCalls === [] and evidenceEscapes === [], so every mutant code is causally from its mutation, not the baseline.

FALSE-POSITIVE HUNT (legit shipped calls wrongly refused): none. Shipped auth.ts / valid.ts perform exactly the six allowed calls (NextAuth, Google, sponsorIdFromGoogleSubject, authTimeFromIdToken, isCanonicalSponsorId, Reflect.deleteProperty) and the three reviewed evidence reads (`if(account)`, `profile?.sub`->sponsor helper, `account.id_token`->auth-time helper); `await` wrapping a helper call leaves the callee an allowed identifier. ambientCalls/evidenceEscapes stay empty.

FALSE-GREEN HUNT: none blocking. The two new rules compose with each other and the pre-existing wiring/env/import rules — an allowed-helper call carrying raw PII is caught by the evidence rule; a non-destructured `jwt(ctx)` form (evidence rule dormant) cannot express the required `sponsorIdFromGoogleSubject(profile?.sub)` wiring and is caught by the sponsor-principal rule. new/tag/decorator strictness matches the shipped file (zero such nodes), so it is intentional bounding, not a false positive.

title: W9.3b Dual-use boundary, contextual aggregation, and human review
description: WHY: The safety line is analysis versus operational facilitation, not alarming vocabulary. Legitimate epidemiology, nuclear theory, security proofs, and weird mathematics must pass, while procedures that materially lower barriers to harm must not be laundered by scientific framing or split across posts. False positives damage the instrument; a hard-reject false negative can cause real harm. WHAT: implement the L2/L3 policy over W9.1 screening: permit descriptive/theoretical analysis; refuse regardless of framing actionable harmful-capability optimization, acquisition guidance, evasion/concealment, target-specific plans, and procedures materially lowering barriers. Evaluate each candidate in bounded context including problem statement and the author recent public promotions so piecewise aggregation cannot bypass review; context words alone never decide. Outcomes are pass, allow-with-warning, quarantine for trained human review, or reject. Borderline content never silently drops and never briefly publishes; affected sponsors receive coarse category, safe reformulation where possible, and human appeal path, while pattern names/scores/reasoning stay restricted. Policy/model/version, input/context digests, category scores, decision path, reviewer and latency are reproducible in screening_log without retaining forbidden raw bodies in routine diagnostics. Degradation follows Fable: deterministic safe cases proceed when the model is down, ambiguous/high-risk cases quarantine, never fail-open. TESTS: versioned corpus with legitimate weird math and dual-use near-boundaries, hard-reject operational cases, paraphrase/encoding and multi-post aggregation, safe transformations, and adversarial oracle probes; unit tests for context selection, policy outcome lattice, retention/redaction and model-outage routing; mock-free integration proves quarantine-before-public-commit and subsequent reviewed release; E2E submits allowed, warned, quarantined, rejected, appealed, aggregated, and outage scenarios through the real promote path. Gates remain FP under 5 percent on legitimate corpus and FN zero on the hard-reject class, reported by category with confidence intervals and exact corpus/policy digests rather than a single opaque score. Logs follow OPS.2a and policy-refusal minimalism. DONE: corpus and red-team paths pass, every decision is reproducible for operators, public errors do not teach bypasses, and scientific weakness is never mislabeled as dangerous content.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property and corpus tests cover context-window selection, analysis-versus-facilitation decisions, pass/warn/quarantine/reject lattice, legitimate weird-science boundaries, paraphrase/encoding/multi-post aggregation, retention/redaction, model outage and oracle-minimal recovery. Fixed holdouts require FP below 5 percent on legitimate cases and zero FN on the hard-reject class with per-category confidence intervals and immutable corpus/policy digests. Mock-free Worker/Workers-AI integration proves quarantine before public commit/cache/search and trained-human release/appeal. scripts/e2e-dual-use-review.sh submits all outcomes, aggregation and outage scenarios through real promotion. OPS.2a logs scenario/corpus/model/policy digests, bounded context IDs, coarse decision, request/event IDs, reviewer state, latency/retry and diff; never bodies, patterns, raw public scores, credentials, cookies, tokens, private review evidence, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

comments.text:
2026-08-20 ntm:%16 fresh independent audit, ds62 scope only. VERDICT: ACCEPT on source. Frozen and identical at open and close: export.ts 36d1049e3f6eda0570c5966fe242797b00057511ffeb5a1f163edcd3b49955e5; krater-export.test.ts 86979c925bab97f2af600d12fb69b436fe18fda5a21b3fe44612bd4a7f6e470d. Source-static only; no edits, reservations, tests, Git or gates (gate serialization in force).

CANONICAL ROW DIGEST SOURCE. verifyProblemExportChain recomputes at export.ts:498-517 through eventRowDigest, whose preimage is fixed at krater.ts:386-396: eventId, problemId, seq, type, objectKind, objectId, objectVersion, payloadSha256, createdAt. The verifier supplies eventId, header.problem, event.objectId, event.createdAt, event.seq and event.payloadSha256 from the exported line; idempotencyKey and statement are passed as inert placeholders and are genuinely absent from the preimage, so the comment at :502 is accurate. The comparison at :509-517 precedes the chain link at :518-529, which is the ordering ds62 asks for.

PER-FIELD BINDING, all eight exported keys (EXPORT_EVENT_KEYS at :56-65):
- event_id — in preimage, taken from the line: BOUND. Plant at test:229.
- object_id — in preimage as claimId, taken from the line: BOUND. Plant at test:230.
- created_at — in preimage, taken from the line: BOUND. Plant at test:231.
- payload_sha256 — in preimage AND in the chain digest: BOUND. Plant at test:211.
- seq — in preimage AND chain: BOUND. Sequence-gap regression at test:216.
- row_digest — the comparison target: BOUND. Plant at test:232.
- chain_digest — compared at :526. Chain regressions at test:207 and :216.
- type — CONSTRAINED, NOT BOUND. See below. Plant at test:246.
Every wire field is either recomputed into a digest or pinned by the parser, and every one has a plant. That is broader coverage than the acceptance enumerates.

ACCEPTANCE, clause by clause: strict event-line shape validation (hasExactKeys at :370 plus field-type and type checks at :376-385) — met; recompute the canonical row digest and compare BEFORE the chain link — met; one-axis plants for event_id, object_id, type, created_at, row_digest and malformed shape — all six present (the first four in the exact-toEqual table at test:226-245, type separately at test:246 with its own exact detail, malformed shape at test:258 and :270); intact/chain/trailer regressions — present at test:203, :207, :216 and six trailer plants from :289 to :357; pure boundary only — verifyProblemExportChain takes a string and returns a verdict, no I/O.

The type separation is correct rather than an omission: a tampered type fails at the PARSER with "event line carries invalid field types or an unsupported event type", not at the digest, so giving it its own plant with its own exact detail is the honest split. The payload_sha256 regression at test:207 deliberately asserts only intact:false and brokenAtSeq:2 without pinning which digest broke — right, because that field participates in both.

SMALLEST REPAIR PACKET: none required for ds62 closure. One FORWARD-LOOKING hardening worth recording, because ds62 is the bead that owns the full-event tamper-evidence claim:

`type` is the only field that is simultaneously on the wire (:64) and a hardcoded constant inside the preimage (krater.ts:390). The digest never consumes the exported value, so it cannot detect a type change; the parser is what rejects one. Today those are equivalent, because exactly one value is admissible. If a v2 ever admits a second event type, the parser constraint widens while eventRowDigest still hardcodes claim.created, and a swap BETWEEN two admissible types becomes undetectable at both layers. The cheapest guard when that day comes is to pass event.type into the preimage rather than hardcoding it, with the migration handled as a chain version. objectKind and objectVersion share the hardcoding but are NOT exported, so there is nothing to tamper and no present gap.

I did not treat that as a REJECT: it is unreachable at v1 and it is properly 5il1 territory, whose disclaimer at export.ts:462-472 already states that v1 checkpoints are unsigned-v0, that 5il1 remains open because the chain preimage does not bind row_digest, and that no parser result may be described as signed or authentic. No overclaim anywhere in the module or its tests.

BOUNDARY. Source: verified, both files byte-identical at open and close. Local: NOT executed — no tests or gates ran, so every binding and plant claim above is traced by reading preimage arguments against assertions rather than observed. Deployed: no claim; this is a pure string-and-digest boundary with no D1, R2 or network.

comments.text:
MistyCanyon — READ-ONLY static audit on stable HEAD c9e99b2 (source tree clean). VERDICT: REJECT, concurring with root 19:36 and the 19:59 audit, on BYTE-IDENTICAL input, plus one defect neither named. No edits, no reservations, no tests/type/lint/UBS, no Git, no status change. SilverMink retains ownership and assignment; the repair below is theirs to apply.

FROZEN SHA-256 (start == end):
  2f1e8d0a84eda8e43c0a8e880d20d7158dc3d698151f47b814c35d99eca36d56  apps/wire/src/app.ts
  f15b00d9b208d4186f9eeee0176238048336fc09ccb54a2fc231e926ee6bf22e  apps/wire/src/ledger-face.ts
  94d45fc1e9a19ba3548d939276bebf4c9025265365a05bc86cbd27079fd5851f  apps/wire/test/contract/faces.test.ts
  138287913ebb2de1e53feeb491f9960eb885bc59a81d23c09a11bab9aa43c9ce  README.md
app.ts, faces.test.ts and README.md match the hashes cited by both prior REJECTs exactly, so no repair has landed since 19:36 and this is a third independent read of the same bytes rather than a re-audit of a moved target.

SATISFIED — two acceptance criteria genuinely met, and worth recording so the repair does not disturb them.
S1 MOUNTING QUARANTINE. The event tail lives in createExperimentalLedgerEventTailRoutes (ledger-face.ts:76), a separate export from createLedgerFaceRoutes (:277). app.ts imports only createLedgerFaceRoutes (:28) and mounts only that (:659). Production therefore cannot dispatch the experiment, and the typed ROUTE_NOT_FOUND builder at app.ts:384-399 redacts the echoed pathname per Fable §14.2.
S2 CANONICAL CURSOR PARSING. ledger-face.ts:62 CANONICAL_PUBLIC_CURSOR = /^(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/ with a Number.isSafeInteger guard at :68. This rejects leading zeros, signs, decimals, hex, exponent and surrounding whitespace, so the original parseInt-suffix defect is fully closed; null defaults to 0 for the full tail. The camelCase reads (event.eventId, event.objectId, event.createdAt at :110-115) also compile against KraterEvent's actual shape, closing the typecheck breakage that opened this bead.

BREACH 1 (acceptance) — CAPABILITIES OMIT EVENT TAILS, AND A PASSING TEST PINS THE OMISSION. app.ts:180 reads not_yet: ["rate-limit budgets", "leases", "triage", "inbox"]. Event tails and the broader unmounted Fable §7.9 faces are absent, so "capabilities must disclose event tails as not_yet" is unmet. Sharpening the prior finding: faces.test.ts:463 asserts expect(body.not_yet).toEqual([...that same four-item list...]). Because it is exact-equality rather than containment, the test does not merely fail to cover the requirement — it LOCKS the incomplete list green, so adding the two labels turns an existing passing test red. That is a false-green in the strict sense and it is the reason this breach has survived three audits.

BREACH 2 (evidence) — THE POISONED-D1 TABLE COVERS FOUR SPELLINGS. faces.test.ts:486-489 enumerates exactly GET and HEAD over /p/P-4DSP.events.json and /p/P-4DSP/events.json, asserting typed 404 with prepares === 0 (:504). Fable §7.9's remaining spellings are untested: events.ndjson, .toon, full.md, claims/hypotheses/gaps/conflicts, orders/moves, dead-ends, feeds, export. The zero-D1 guarantee is therefore proven for the two dotted/slashed JSON spellings only.

BREACH 3 (evidence) — THE ORIGINAL DEFECT IS THE ONE THING UNTESTED, and it is worse than "untested". The experimental block at faces.test.ts:588-619 proves six non-canonical cursors are refused with prepares === 0, then admits since=1 with prepares === 1. But that admitted request returns 404 PROBLEM_NOT_FOUND (:616-617): it proves only that a canonical cursor reaches D1, never that a successful tail serializes. There is no 200 anywhere in this lane, so the camelCase-to-snake_case mapping at ledger-face.ts:110-115 — the exact field-naming mismatch that created this bead — has ZERO coverage. A regression reintroducing event.object_kind would be caught by typecheck but by no test here.

BREACH 4 (documentation) — README ADVERTISES QUARANTINED ROUTES AS LIVE. README.md:103 gives a copy-pasteable curl against https://a.asimposium.org/p/smooth-poincare-4d/events.json?since=0 and :214 lists GET /p/<slug>/events.json?since=<seq> among served routes. Both currently return typed 404. Under Rule A4 the site never pretends, and an agent-facing README that hands an agent a command guaranteed to 404 is the documentation form of that defect.

BREACH 5 (NEW — not raised by either prior audit) — has_more IS A FALSE POSITIVE AT THE EXACT PAGE BOUNDARY. ledger-face.ts:104 reads readEvents(c.env.DB, problemId, since, 200) and :117 derives has_more: events.length === 200. When the tail holds exactly 200 remaining events the response claims has_more: true and the next page is empty. Fable §464 requires the terminating page_end record precisely "so agents never guess whether a page completed"; a has_more that can promise a page which does not exist reintroduces the guess. Fix is the n+1 idiom already being adopted elsewhere in this repo (j9hw at router.ts:874, e7j.2's LIMIT 17): query 201, emit 200, derive has_more from rows.length > 200. This is source-level and cheap, and it should be folded into the same repair rather than filed separately, since Breach 3's missing success fixture is the natural place to assert it.

MINIMAL REPAIR PACKET (SilverMink's to apply; ordered by dependency).
  R1 app.ts:180 — add the two disclosure labels (per-problem event tails; unmounted §7.9 faces).
  R2 faces.test.ts:463 — this MUST change in the same commit as R1 or the suite goes red; prefer expect.arrayContaining over toEqual so future labels do not re-break it.
  R3 faces.test.ts:486-489 — expand the poisoned-D1 table to the full §7.9 spelling set, retaining prepares === 0 per row.
  R4 faces.test.ts — add a successful retained-tail fixture against the EXPERIMENTAL router only (never mounting it): seed one event, assert 200, assert the emitted keys are id/seq/type/object_id/created_at, and assert has_more === false at exactly 200 rows to cover Breach 5.
  R5 ledger-face.ts:104,117 — n+1 query and has_more derivation.
  R6 README.md:103,214 — mark both as target-only, not served.
  R1+R2 are atomic. R4 depends on R5 for its boundary assertion to be meaningful.

BOUNDARY. Static source evidence only at the hashes above; nothing was executed, so Wire contract/typecheck, root typecheck and scoped Biome/diff/UBS remain unrun and the bead's gate clause is unsatisfied independent of the five breaches. Status unchanged (in_progress, assignee SilverMink). Not staged, not committed, not closed.

CONFIRMED REPAIRED (the bead's three named defects are closed)
- Cache: the 200 sets `cache-control: private, no-store` (router.ts:1580).
- Contract validation both ways: request via SponsorWorkshopRequestSchema.safeParse -> 422 WORKSHOP_READ_BODY_INVALID (router.ts:1515-1527); response via SponsorWorkshopViewSchema.parse before serialisation (router.ts:1565).
- Agora no longer hand-casts: stoa.ts:460 parses with the shared SponsorWorkshopViewSchema, and the transport sets fetch `cache: "no-store"` (stoa-sponsor.ts:276), so Next's data cache cannot retain private bytes.
- Ownership is non-reflective: a foreign or missing fellow takes ONE shared 404 WORKSHOP_NOT_FOUND branch (router.ts:1536-1547), so "not yours" and "does not exist" are indistinguishable by construction.

THREE REMAINING GAPS

1. FALSE-GREEN in the privacy assertion (test:1294). The wrong-sponsor non-reflection check is `expect(await wrongSponsor.text()).not.toContain("Private sponsor note")` — a single TITLE substring. It never asserts absence of body_md, which is the privacy-critical field (AGENTS.md UBS critical: "workshop bytes on a public face"). The two planted bodies — "Only the Fellow and sponsor may read these bytes." (test:1210) and "The live view presents this card first." — are never checked. A regression that echoed body_md into the 404 problem detail would pass this test. Note also that the needle's capital P means it would not match the second note's title "Newer private sponsor note" (test:1220, lowercase p), so even title coverage is one of two.

2. CACHE CLAIM PROVEN FOR ONE OF THREE RESPONSE CLASSES. `cache-control` is asserted only on the 200 (test:1256). The 404 and 422 are unasserted, and problem()/validatedProblem() (http/envelope.ts:121-139) set ONLY content-type — no Cache-Control on any problem response. Practical risk is low because the route is now POST and RFC 9111 makes POST responses uncacheable absent explicit freshness, but the test's own title says "never shared-cacheable" while proving it for the success path only.

3. INDISTINGUISHABILITY IS UNPINNED. The shared-404 property above holds by construction today, but no assertion compares the wrong-sponsor 404 against a nonexistent-fellow 404. Splitting that branch into two distinct details later would leak existence and keep every current test green.

SMALLEST FIXES (for the owner; not applied)
- Extend test:1294 to assert the 404 text contains neither planted body_md nor either title nor any workshop_id.
- Assert `cache-control` on the 404 and 422, and give problem()/validatedProblem() a default `private, no-store` for authenticated routes.

Its sealed transport rejects query/hash paths, signs method/route/action/principal/body bytes, and fetches with credentials omit, cache no-store, redirect error. The client correctly stream-bounds both declared and actual response bytes, but a strict contract-valid 200 rows x 64 KiB body_md response can exceed its 16 MiB ceiling; client reports it unreachable. This is the already-open e7j.2 byte-bounded/paginated-read defect, not a reason to raise the reader cap or overlap its owner.
