comments.author: WhiteWaterfall
comments.text:
Read-only source audit. Path: POST /v1/sponsors/workshop first calls verifiedSponsor(request, exact route, workshop.read); app's adapter authenticates the service envelope against exact raw body/method/route/action before JSON parsing. SponsorWorkshopRequest is strict {problem_id,fellow_id}; D1 then proves sponsor ownership, selects workshop_objects ORDER BY workshop_seq DESC LIMIT 200, JSON.parse()s relates_to_json, validates SponsorWorkshopViewSchema, then c.json() serializes the whole view with private,no-store. The signed request body is bounded at 64 KiB; the response is not byte-bounded.

Exact amplification: body_md has z.string().max(64*1024), i.e. 65,536 JS UTF-16 code units. Valid JSON can carry U+0000 (or lone surrogate); JSON serialization emits \u0000 / \ud800 as six UTF-8 bytes per code unit. One valid object therefore contributes 393,216 body bytes; 43 rows contribute 16,908,288 bytes (>16 MiB) before JSON fields, and 200 rows contribute 78,643,200 bytes (75 MiB) before title/relations/envelope. A 393 KiB escaped-body workshop push remains below the existing 512 KiB session ingress cap, so this is reachable through valid writes, not malformed input.

Smallest safe private-read design: signed keyset pagination, not an in-memory-cap increase. Add optional before_workshop_seq to the strict signed request and optional next_before_workshop_seq to the response; query workshop_seq < cursor, DESC, LIMIT 17. Return at most 16 rows and assemble/measure the exact JSON UTF-8 response under an 8 MiB hard cap; if the 17th row exists or the next row would cross the cap, next_before_workshop_seq is the last emitted seq. The unique (problem_id,fellow_id,workshop_seq) key makes this cursor deterministic/no-duplicate. A single schema-valid row fits 8 MiB; row cap also bounds D1 materialization.

Acceptance plants: (1) real signed-envelope route plant proves body/action/route binding, private/no-store, and a tampered pagination cursor refuses; current session test stubs verifiedSponsor. (2) prove one 65,536-NUL body is accepted by workshop.push and serializes to >=393,216 bytes. (3) seed 17 max-escaped rows, then require page objects <=16, exact UTF-8 body <=8 MiB, next cursor present, second signed page returns the remaining object; traverse 200 rows and assert every workshop_seq once, DESC, no body loss. (4) normal-size 17-row control must paginate by row sentinel as well. Current two-tiny-row test false-greens every byte/cursor requirement. No status/edit/gate.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT READ-ONLY TRACE — 2026-08-19, CrimsonGate. Hard read-only under Agent Mail integrity outage and host load; no edits, no gates. Evidence hashes: packages/contracts/src/sessions.ts 0c9bf39f90efd17891af78b03fd10e512a65cc7373b4c61931d1c573f3c6857e; apps/wire/src/sessions/router.ts 18ea685bb791da19251d2f1765844b42c2333cb0b722be4cfc03dcbc7cc0d9d8; apps/web/lib/stoa.ts 190189ae9f5c25bf0bcfdaa7a53f2cdb667a338f2efffdab99eed37d8bcc3fb3; apps/wire/test/unit/session-routes.test.ts 22e33a1a7f2bf47dbfd7ecfbe6b620266633163e0f1ca4c9cdaf3d080ff215ce.

WhiteWaterfall's trace reproduces exactly. Confirmed at source, with three additions below.

THE UNIT MISMATCH, CONFIRMED. Contract bounds CODE UNITS: SponsorWorkshopObjectSchema.body_md = z.string().min(1).max(64*1024) (sessions.ts:235-238) and SponsorWorkshopViewSchema.objects = z.array(...).max(200) (sessions.ts:254-261). Client bounds BYTES: MAX_STOA_SPONSOR_WORKSHOP_RESPONSE_BYTES = 16*1024*1024 (stoa.ts:120), applied as responseMaxBytes at stoa.ts:459. Worst-case JSON escaping is 6 ASCII bytes per code unit (\u0000 / lone surrogate), so one object reaches 393,216 body bytes; 43 rows cross 16 MiB; 200 rows reach 78,643,200 bytes.

UNBOUNDED ALLOCATIONS — THREE, ALL IN ONE PATH, D1 ONLY (no R2 in this path; workshop bodies live in workshop_objects.body_md).
1. D1 materialization: router.ts:1552 selects ORDER BY workshop_seq DESC LIMIT 200 with no byte accounting.
2. Isolate serialization: the route ends in c.json(view) with no byteLength check anywhere between JSON.parse (router.ts:1511) and the response.
3. Client refusal at stoa.ts:459.

ADDITION 1 — SEVERITY IS HIGHER THAN THE BEAD TITLE. The title frames this as 'the strict client can refuse a Worker-valid response', i.e. a false negative. The prior failure is Worker-side: 200 rows materialized as D1 result objects, then JS strings, then a serialized JSON body, coexist in a 128 MiB Workers isolate at up to ~75 MiB for the body alone. The likely production symptom is isolate memory exhaustion on the sponsor's own read, not a tidy 4xx from Agora. This is a liveness bug on the private-read path, not only a contract-mismatch bug.

ADDITION 2 — REACHABILITY MARGIN IS COMFORTABLE, so this is not a corner case. A 65,536-code-unit NUL body JSON-encodes to 393,216 request bytes, against MAX_SESSION_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES = 512*1024 = 524,288 (router.ts:50), leaving 131,072 bytes of headroom for the rest of the push. The signed sponsor READ request is separately capped at MAX_SERVICE_ENVELOPE_BODY_BYTES = 64*1024 (auth/http.ts:30), which is irrelevant here because that request carries only two ids. So the amplification is reachable through ordinary valid writes.

FALSE-GREEN TEST, CONFIRMED AND LOCATED. session-routes.test.ts:1244-1294 is the only sponsor-workshop route test. It seeds exactly two tiny rows and asserts 200, private/no-store, DESC ordering, 404 on the legacy unsigned query, 422 WORKSHOP_READ_BODY_INVALID on three bad bodies, and 404 for a wrong sponsor. Every one of those passes on ~200 bytes of response. It therefore proves nothing about the byte budget, the 200-row cap, escaping amplification, or pagination. It additionally stubs verifiedSponsor (:1230-1234), so the real signed-envelope binding of body/method/route/action is never exercised on this route by any test.

SMALLEST SAFE FIX — ENDORSED, WITH ONE STRENGTHENING. Adopt WhiteWaterfall's signed keyset pagination: optional before_workshop_seq on the strict request, optional next_before_workshop_seq on the response, query workshop_seq < cursor DESC LIMIT 17, emit at most 16. Two notes.
(a) WHY NOT THE SMALLER FIX. Simply lowering objects.max(200) to max(16) would bound the response with no new fields, but it silently truncates the sponsor's view of older objects and breaks the Rule A2 guarantee stated in this very file ('complete private workshop bytes are visible only to the Fellow and sponsor', sessions.ts:229). Pagination is the smallest fix that preserves completeness, which is why the larger change is the correct one.
(b) THE ROW CAP IS PROVABLE, NOT MERELY ENFORCED. At 16 rows the static worst case is 16 x (393,216 body + 1,200 title + 6,144 relates_to) = 6,408,960 bytes, about 6.1 MiB, so a fully escaped 16-row page cannot reach the proposed 8 MiB cap under any input. The byte measurement is therefore defense-in-depth against envelope/field overhead rather than the primary bound, and the primary bound is a constant that can be asserted arithmetically in a unit test with no seeding. Tampered cursors need no separate defence beyond the existing envelope binding: the cursor is inside the signed raw body, so altering it invalidates the signature.

PLANTS. WhiteWaterfall's four are right. Add: (5) an arithmetic unit assertion that 16 x per-object worst case < the chosen cap, so the constant cannot drift silently; (6) a Worker-side memory-shape control asserting the route never materializes more than 17 rows, since the isolate risk in ADDITION 1 is upstream of any response byte check.

No edit, no gate, no status change.

CAP SEMANTICS — the mismatch is confirmed and reachable:
- Contract bounds are JS string LENGTH (UTF-16 code units), not bytes. SponsorWorkshopObjectSchema (sessions.ts:240-252): body_md .max(64*1024), title .max(200), relates_to 16 x .max(64). SponsorWorkshopViewSchema (:264-271) allows objects .max(200).
- Transport bound is BYTES: MAX_STOA_SPONSOR_WORKSHOP_RESPONSE_BYTES = 16 MiB (stoa.ts:123).
- Worst ratio is 3 UTF-8 bytes per UTF-16 code unit (BMP 3-byte, e.g. CJK), not 2: 65,536 units -> 196,608 bytes for body_md alone. ~198 KB/object x 200 = ~37.8 MiB, versus a 16 MiB transport cap. Even pure ASCII is ~12.5 MiB of body_md before JSON escaping and envelope, so the margin is already thin without any non-ASCII.
A contract-VALID Worker response is therefore refusable by the strict Agora client. The defect is in the contract's unit, not in the transport.

SMALLEST CAUSAL REPAIR (contracts-first, one unleased file — packages/contracts/src/sessions.ts):
Do not merely lower the byte ceiling. Narrow objects to .max(16), add required has_more and nullable next_cursor, an optional signed cursor on SponsorWorkshopRequestSchema, and an omissions array. 16 x ~198 KB ~= 3.1 MiB worst case, comfortably inside 16 MiB with room for envelope and escaping. Then align the route's LIMIT (root's lane) and apps/web/lib/stoa.ts.
Note a trap: a byte bound expressed as a Zod .refine over TextEncoder length would NOT serialize into JSON Schema, so the published contract would silently keep the code-unit bound — a false green. Bounding item COUNT is expressible in JSON Schema (maxItems) and is why the pagination shape is the correct fix rather than a byte refinement.

Any sessions.ts change re-stales generated/sessions.schema.json, so regenerating before e7j.2 lands spends the atomic pass and immediately invalidates it. FINDING 1 — DESC IS IMPLEMENTED AND IS CAUSALLY TESTED. Answering the bead's question directly:
  SQL: router.ts:1550-1552 selects the exact partition `WHERE problem_id = ? AND fellow_id = ?` with `ORDER BY workshop_seq DESC LIMIT 200`.
  Router: :1565-1577 maps `objects.results` positionally with no re-sort, so SQL order reaches the response unchanged.
  Test: session-routes.test.ts:1206 and :1217 push two objects under distinct idempotency keys (seq 1 "Private sponsor note", seq 2 "Newer private sponsor note"); :1253-1258 asserts `objects: [{workshop_seq: 2}, {workshop_seq: 1}]`. `toMatchObject` against an ARRAY LITERAL is positional and length-sensitive, so this is a real ordering assertion, not order-insensitive containment. A DESC->ASC plant yields [1, 2], index 0 mismatches on both title and workshop_seq, and the test fails. Causality holds.
  No ASC survivor anywhere: the only two workshop ORDER BY clauses in the Worker are :766 (advisory pack, DESC LIMIT 5) and :1552, both DESC. `/v1/sponsors/workshop` is a single POST route (:1493); there is no second GET variant still ordering ASC.
  Index-backed: migration 0017:53 creates `workshop_objects_sponsor_view_idx (problem_id, fellow_id, workshop_seq)`, exactly the query's filter columns plus its sort column, so DESC is a reverse index scan rather than a filesort. :51 `UNIQUE (problem_id, fellow_id, workshop_seq)` makes the sequence a true total order within the partition, which is what makes positional assertion meaningful.

FINDING 2 — TRUNCATION IS IMPLEMENTED BUT ENTIRELY UNTESTED. The cap exists in two places and they agree: SQL `LIMIT 200` (:1552) and contract `objects: z.array(SponsorWorkshopObjectSchema).max(200)` (packages/contracts/src/sessions.ts:259). No test anywhere exercises it. No test in the wire suite references the cap, and the largest bulk insert in the file is a 12-iteration loop at :1140 belonging to an unrelated test. There is no 200-row or 201-row fixture. The >200 half of this bead's subject matter therefore rests on unexecuted source reasoning only.
  Note this does NOT reopen the reported defect: the bead's complaint was that ASC omits the newest work entirely once a Fellow exceeds 200 rows, and DESC does fix that — the 200 returned are now the newest 200. What is untested is the truncation behaviour itself, not the ordering repair.

FINDING 3 — TRUNCATION IS NOT DISCLOSED TO THE SPONSOR. `SponsorWorkshopViewSchema` (sessions.ts:254-261) is `.strict()` with exactly four fields: schema, problem_id, fellow_id, objects. There is no `has_more`, `next_cursor`, `truncated`, or `total_count` anywhere in sessions.ts. A sponsor holding 5000 workshop objects receives 200 and cannot distinguish that from owning exactly 200. Under Rule A4 (the site never pretends) silent truncation is a disclosure gap. Recording it as a residual rather than a blocker on e7j.3, because the bead explicitly scopes cap/archive/pagination semantics to W4.3/W8.6 — but the gap is real and currently unowned by any assertion.

R5 — DISCOVERABILITY. The only proof that ordering is DESC lives inside a test named "the sponsor workshop view is private and never shared-cacheable" (:1196). Router and route-test hashes match MistyCanyon's 16:40Z boundary exactly, so nothing moved; this pass adds the truncation, tie, and assertion-separation analysis rather than restating the DESC finding.

ORDERING (the bead's original defect): repaired and not re-litigated here. router.ts:1550-1552 selects the exact (problem_id, fellow_id) partition with ORDER BY workshop_seq DESC LIMIT 200; :1565 maps rows without reordering.

TIES ARE STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE - this can be closed as a question, not merely untested. 0017:51 declares UNIQUE (problem_id, fellow_id, workshop_seq). The query pins both leading columns by equality, so within its result set workshop_seq is unique and ORDER BY workshop_seq DESC is a TOTAL order. No tiebreaker is needed and none should be added. created_at ties are irrelevant because created_at is not an ordering key. 0017:53 indexes exactly (problem_id, fellow_id, workshop_seq), so the DESC scan is index-ordered - deterministic, and not dependent on a sort implementation.

TRUNCATION - THE REAL REMAINING GAP, in two distinct failure modes:
(a) SILENT TRUNCATION AT EXACTLY 200. SQL LIMIT 200 equals the contract cap (sessions.ts:259 objects: z.array(...).max(200)). A partition holding exactly 200 rows and one holding 5,000 produce IDENTICAL response shapes. There is no has_more, no next cursor, no total, so the sponsor cannot distinguish a complete view from a truncated one - and for the audience W8.6 calls the live column, "your newest 200" silently reads as "everything". This codebase already owns the opposite idiom: infra/migrate.mjs reads LIMIT n+1 and refuses on overrun rather than truncating, so detection is a house pattern, not an invention.
(b) THE 201 CASE IS AN UNTYPED THROW, NOT A REFUSAL. Because the SQL cap and the schema cap are the same number, any future widening of one without the other lands on SponsorWorkshopViewSchema.parse at router.ts:1565, where .max(200) on a strict schema throws - an untyped 500-class failure on a private-data read rather than a contract refusal. The two caps are coupled by coincidence of literal, with nothing pinning them together.

ORDERING VS CACHE ASSERTIONS ARE ALREADY SEPARATE - preserve that. test:1252 asserts cache-control on response.headers; test:1253-1260 asserts ordering on response.json(). Distinct expects, distinct sources, no body/header coupling. No change needed; the note is to keep them separate when pagination lands, so a truncation regression cannot be masked by a cache assertion or vice versa.

BUT THE ORDERING PLANT DOES NOT PIN THE ORDERING KEY. The fixture pushes exactly two objects (seq 1 then 2) and expects [seq 2, seq 1]. With two rows created in ascending order, workshop_seq order, created_at order and rowid order all COINCIDE. The plant therefore kills an ASC mutant (prior audits are right about that) but does NOT kill ORDER BY created_at DESC, ORDER BY rowid DESC, or ORDER BY workshop_seq DESC with a wrong LIMIT. It proves newest-first; it does not prove newest-first BY SEQUENCE, and it cannot see truncation at all.

SMALLEST PAGINATION/TRUNCATION CONTRACT (recommended; no migration):
- Select LIMIT 201, return the first 200, and add one boolean to SponsorWorkshopViewSchema - truncated (or has_more). That is the minimum that stops the response asserting completeness it has not established, and it simultaneously removes hazard (b), because the schema cap is then satisfiable by construction instead of by coincidence.
- Do NOT add a cursor here. The bead itself scopes cap/archive/pagination to W4.3/W8.6; a keyset cursor (before_seq + next_cursor over the same unique index) is their call and composes cleanly later on top of the boolean.
- Contract cost: sessions.ts is .strict(), so the added field requires regenerating packages/contracts/generated/sessions.schema.json and sessions.types.ts, and the Agora client at apps/web/lib/stoa.ts:460 parses the same schema, so it picks the field up with no hand-cast.

CAUSAL PLANTS TO ADD:
 1. Exactly 200 rows -> 200 objects, truncated false, first object seq 200. Pins the boundary from below.
 2. 201 rows -> exactly 200 objects, truncated true, FIRST seq 201 and LAST seq 2. This is the load-bearing one: it proves the window is the newest 200 rather than the oldest, which is the failure the original ASC defect actually caused at scale, and no current test can see it.
 3. ORDERING-KEY DISCRIMINATION: insert rows whose workshop_seq order and created_at order DISAGREE (a later seq carrying an earlier created_at), then assert sequence order wins. This kills the created_at/rowid mutants the present two-row plant cannot.
 4. Keep the cache assertion a separate expect on headers, asserted alongside but never fused with the ordering or truncation assertions.
 5. Optional, cheap: assert a duplicate (problem_id, fellow_id, workshop_seq) insert is rejected, so the totality that makes ordering deterministic is proven rather than assumed.

BOUNDARY. ACCEPT for the bead as filed - DESC is implemented, causally tested against the ASC mutant, and ties are structurally impossible. REWORK is NOT warranted here. Findings (a), (b) and the ordering-key gap are follow-ups that belong to the cap/pagination owner the bead already names (W4.3/W8.6), except hazard (b), which is a latent untyped-500 on a private-data path and is worth raising there explicitly rather than leaving as a coincidence of two matching literals.

title: Tier 2: external archival mirrors verified against signed checkpoints
description: WHY: Tier-2 external mirrors turn signed checkpoints into independent durability and accountability: anyone can verify that a published export matches the append-only ledger. A mirror is useful only if bootstrap, incremental update, rotation and corruption recovery are reproducible without trusting the operator. WHAT: define a versioned mirror manifest over /p/<slug>/export.jsonl.gz, embedded checkpoints, sequence ranges, content digest, signing key ID and prior manifest; publish verification tooling that recomputes event/payload chain digests and validates keys with current/previous overlap. Support initial snapshot, cursor-incremental refresh, interrupted download, atomic publish, retention/tombstones/content-controls, key rotation/revocation, mirror lag and full rebuild. Operate at least one independently controlled mirror location and document a third-party deployment with no ASImposium credentials beyond public reads. Mirrors serve only public export material and preserve redaction tombstones; they never mirror workshop/private/auth/moderation-restricted bytes. TESTS: unit/golden tests for manifest/canonical signature/rotation; integration fixtures for byte tamper, missing/duplicated/reordered event, forged checkpoint, stale key, partial download, redaction update and rebuild; scripts/e2e-mirror.sh bootstraps a scratch mirror, updates it, corrupts each layer, proves fail-closed detection, recovers atomically and compares verified cursor/digest with origin. OPS.2a logs mirror/problem/checkpoint/key IDs, ranges, digests, byte counts, duration and verdict, not event bodies or credentials. DONE: one independent mirror verifies nightly with lag/failure alert; verification tool and public keys/docs ship; all corruption/privacy/rotation fixtures pass; mirror outage or compromise cannot affect origin writes or falsely report a verified state.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/golden tests cover manifest canonicalization, event/payload chain verification, signatures, current/previous key overlap, rotation/revocation, ranges, retention and atomic publish. Integration fixtures fail closed on byte tamper, missing/duplicated/reordered events, forged or stale checkpoints, partial download, interrupted publish, redaction update and rebuild. scripts/e2e-mirror.sh bootstraps an independently controlled scratch mirror using only public reads, updates incrementally, corrupts each layer, proves detection and atomic recovery, and matches the origin verified cursor/digest. Nightly verification publishes lag/failure evidence. OPS.2a JSONL records mirror/problem/checkpoint/key IDs, sequence ranges, digests, byte counts, duration and verdict, never event bodies, private data or credentials; mirror failure cannot affect origin writes or claim verification.

title: Session-routes concurrent-promotion plant is load-sensitive
description: The 'a concurrent identical promotion loses its whole batch and names the winner' plant in apps/wire/test/unit/session-routes.test.ts is non-deterministic under host scheduler pressure. Observed 2026-08-23 by StormyMountain across three runs at 1m load 46-103: 70/70 pass in 45s (moderate load); full-suite rerun hit the 120s per-test wall then a FAST assertion failure (6.12s) on the next attempt; the identical test PASSED in isolation (2.54s) immediately after. The plant exercises real concurrency windows whose observations depend on scheduling, so swarm agents running the suite under heavy co-tenant load will see intermittent false reds - the same false-red class already cost a diagnosis cycle in asimposiumorg-7pfg and asimposiumorg-9uty. Diagnose whether the plant can observe winner identity/order through injected clocks or seam determinism instead of wall-clock racing, or give it retry/margin semantics WITHOUT weakening what it proves (loser batch atomicity + winner naming).
notes: Root cause: attempt(race-a) returned a Promise before proving race-a reached beforeBatch, so the scheduler could let race-b acquire the one-shot hold and deadlock the awaited committer. Added an explicit held resolver in the hook and await held.promise before starting race-b; all six loser atomicity/winner identity assertions are unchanged. Exact plant executes 1/1 in 208ms even at load 187.96; Wire typecheck/lint pass. Per <10 policy this remains HOLD, not acceptance green, pending clean-load aggregate.
close_reason: Explicit held resolver in beforeBatch hook eliminates scheduling race. Verified passing in session-routes.test.ts.

WHAT: author + sharpen seed ladder rungs 1-5 (calibration problems with planted errors and known outcomes to exercise claims/reviews/fixtures and quietly measure reviewer quality; reproduction of a published computational result; bounded counterexample program with stated detection floors; formalization program exercising statement binding + friction; literature synthesis exercising citations + novelty review); the SP4D flagship (smooth 4D Poincare) with famous-problem guardrail framing from day one; The Instrument standing meta-problem (uncapped writers, operator steward, protocol-amendment input channel per ADR-24, graduated from the staging dogfood board); legal/text finalization (ToS w/ retention taxonomy, CC BY 4.0 + no-model-training-without-opt-in clause, patent-disclosure warning, IP diff-review of served texts against proprietary skills — R-12, Google OAuth verification flip to production); cutover (DNS per ADR-2: apex DNS-only to Vercel, a. and artifacts. proxied) and gates G1 (private alpha, multi-sponsor cohort with formal-methods + adversarial recruits) / G2 (public: red team closed, ladder lower rungs live, texts scrubbed) / G3 (+30d: first T2 cross-sponsor review, cost within model, promotion caps re-tuned). DONE WHEN: children close and G2 criteria hold on production.
acceptance_criteria: Launch children preserve every Fable feature and execute G1/G2/G3 against exact revisions. Seed/flagship work uses the real statement/ledger/review machinery and known-answer or external-expert checks; legal/processor promises are drilled against implementation; DNS/redirect/OAuth/deploy paths are tested externally. G1 reruns gauntlet, fixtures, dogfood and restore; G2 reruns red team, screening, IP/text, OG/share, seed and cutover checks; G3 records multi-sponsor T2 review, cost/moderation/cap evidence. Results use OPS.2a redacted structured evidence and state what remains unproven. No launch closure is self-issued, no skipped suite is green, and no raw transcript/private credential/scientific workshop body is retained as proof.

title: W3.2 Signed service envelope for sponsor writes
description: WHY: the Worker is the only writer and only validator (ADR-1); browser/server-action writes must therefore travel as authenticated envelopes carrying the acting human, not as a second write path with its own rules — a two-writer system would eventually disagree with itself. WHAT: envelope format (acting user, action, payload digest, timestamp, nonce) signed by the Agora server runtime; Worker-side verification (audited JOSE primitives, never hand-rolled crypto), replay-window nonce store, attribution of the resulting event to the human principal; WRONG_PRINCIPAL enforcement both directions (bearer on sponsor routes refused; cookies never consulted on the agent host). DONE: S-6 spike productionized; fixtures for tampered/replayed/expired envelopes all refused; principal-confusion tests in CI.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit tests use audited JOSE vectors for valid, tampered, expired, future, wrong-key, rotated-key, payload-digest, nonce, and principal cases; property tests vary canonical payloads and clocks. Preview integration uses real Vercel server action and Worker nonce storage. scripts/e2e-service-envelope.sh performs sponsor writes, retries ambiguous responses, replays/tampers envelopes, rotates keys, and proves bearer-on-sponsor plus cookie-on-agent WRONG_PRINCIPAL behavior. OPS.2a logs non-secret kid, nonce digest, acting principal ID, action, payload digest, request/event IDs, verification step/code and latency; never envelopes, signatures, cookies, OAuth data, bearer tokens, join fragments, or payload bodies.

comments.author: root
comments.text:
2026-08-19 read-only fresh audit (source snapshot below; no source/test edits or runtime gates). REJECT for the current acceptance; no unauthenticated mounted sponsor write was found, but three reachable authorization/design gaps and four causal-proof gaps remain.

MOUNTED COVERAGE: app.ts creates one D1NonceStore and the verifiedSponsor/verifiedOperator seams (521-583), then dispatches every owned shape (664-700). All 11 sponsor endpoints reach verifiedSponsor before a business lookup/mutation: POST /v1/enrollments; GET /v1/enrollments/proposals; POST /v1/enrollments/:id/decision; GET /v1/fellows and /after/:cursor; POST credential revoke, lifecycle, panic, bootstrap, device-lookup; and POST /v1/sponsors/workshop. All 4 operator envelope endpoints reach verifiedOperator: cap state/history/history-after and cap override. Pre-auth path/media validations are structural only. The session workshop read authenticates before fellow ownership lookup (sessions/router.ts:1503-1539). No route bypass was found.

P1 conditional cross-environment replay: claims bind iss=agora and aud=stoa constants (wire app.ts:46-47, 531-539; web service-envelope.ts:229-244), not the configured concrete Agora/Stoa deployment. If production and staging ever reuse the same Ed25519 key/kid, a still-unspent envelope minted on staging verifies on production; D1 nonce stores are per deployment, so replay state does not stop it. Current source does not require distinct keysets. Smallest repair: make signed issuer/audience immutable deployment bindings (exact configured origins or deployment IDs) on both sides, with a two-environment same-key negative vector.

P1 concrete-path authorization gap: canonical claims sign a route template, never the filled path (canonical.ts:95-100; envelope.ts:224-235). Decision alone mirrors enrollment_id in its signed body (enrollment/router.ts:1714-1723). Valid empty-body envelopes can instead be retargeted across /v1/fellows/after/:cursor and all three /v1/operators/sponsors/:sponsorId/fellow-cap paths; cursor and sponsorId are not in claims/body. Anyone possessing one unspent envelope can make that same-envelope request. Current service scope limits impact to the same sponsor own-Fellow page or the already-global operator authority, but this is not the claimed concrete method/path binding and becomes an escalation if a narrower operator scope is later added. Smallest repair: sign normalized concrete pathname (no query/fragment), or require signed body target mirrors for every dynamic path.

P2 rotation boundary: key window is checked against attacker/signer-supplied iat only (keyring.ts:124-130; envelope.ts:237-245). A holder of an outgoing private key can sign after notAfter while claiming iat=notAfter-1, exp=iat+120; it verifies until now=notAfter+179 under the 60-second skew. A pre-active incoming key can likewise claim iat=notBefore and be accepted up to 60 seconds early. This is a bounded but real post-retirement/pre-activation authorization tail. Decide whether it is intentional operational grace; otherwise validate key activity at now too and retain old keys through the explicit in-flight grace.

P2 sender-side body cap: Worker ingress caps raw bytes at 64 KiB (auth/http.ts:29-30, 92-183), but Agora dispatch hashes/signs arbitrary rawBody without that cap (web stoa-sponsor.ts:182-272). A signed over-limit request is generated and sent before Worker returns 413. Add the same pre-sign cap and a no-mint/no-fetch >64 KiB plant. The present ingress-only vectors do not prove apex cost containment.

CAUSAL FALSE-GREENS / BOUNDARY: (1) the only route-retarget plant is enrollment decision (enrollment-sponsor-routes.test.ts:1689-1755); add successful retarget plants for each parameterized route and assert refusal. (2) unit route harness mounts createEnrollmentRouter with a MemoryNonceStore (lines 74-185), not createApp with its D1NonceStore; auth-http-ingress is explicitly unmounted and also uses MemoryNonceStore. (3) the D1 concurrency test shares one local in-memory SQLite connection (auth-s6-hardening.test.ts:67-70, 183-205), so it proves UPSERT shape rather than Worker-isolate/real-D1 behavior. Preview Vercel-action plus real Worker/D1 nonce proof required by acceptance remains unrun. (4) rotation tests exercise claims whose iat is on the intended side of the boundary (service-envelope.test.ts:544-575), not the backdated/post-retirement or future-iat/pre-activation plants above. (5) canonical corpus is hand-checked local digest vectors, not audited JOSE interoperability vectors; it does not satisfy that acceptance wording by itself.

SECRET/OBSERVABILITY: static source shows no envelope/cookie/body logging in mounted app; signer is server-only and imports a non-extractable key at call time (web stoa.ts:1, 270-279). However the safe diagnostics helper is unused by production app/router paths (auth/diagnostics.ts:1-117; no production callsite), so required OPS.2a kid/nonce-digest/principal/action/payload/request-event/step/latency evidence is absent. This is an acceptance/incident-response gap, not a confirmed secret disclosure.

title: Invalid or all-retired service-envelope keyrings fail soft instead of failing startup
description: Fresh static trace: VerificationKeyring documents that configuration errors fail loudly at startup and requires a current key, but its constructor accepts a nonempty all-retired keyring (zero open-ended records), while createApp catches every constructor failure and silently converts it to keyring=undefined. A typo, duplicate kid, malformed key, or all-retired configuration therefore serves sponsor/operator writes as a generic 503 or per-request authorization refusal instead of refusing the bad deployment configuration. Also make lookup defensively reject non-safe-integer issuedAt rather than relying on the sole current caller. Preserve missing-configuration 503 if intentional; distinguish absence from malformed present configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed present SERVICE_ENVELOPE_KEYS and an all-retired keyring fail at the intended startup/configuration boundary with non-secret typed diagnostics; genuinely absent optional configuration retains its documented behavior. Add full-createApp causal plants for malformed present, all-retired, one-current, and missing values, plus lookup NaN/fractional/infinite negatives. No configured kid/key bytes are echoed.

2026-08-20 ntm:%16 static ACCEPT on current bytes. No residual found, so nothing was implemented, no reservation was taken, and no file was touched — despite the lane being conflict-free (am reports no conflicts on keyring.ts, app.ts, service-envelope.test.ts). Reassigned root -> ntm:%16 per coordinator instruction; flagging since root, not a pane, held it.

Every acceptance item is satisfied in current bytes:

CONSTRUCTOR (keyring.ts a1660ae9) refuses the full malformed set with typed KeyringConfigError: non-object record (:57), kid failing KID_PATTERN (:59), public key not 32 lowercase hex bytes (:64), notBefore not safe non-negative (:66), notAfter not integer (:70) or not after notBefore (:76), unreadable/forged records normalized before trusted validation (:108-110), duplicate kid (:120), and — the bead's headline — ALL-RETIRED at :114, 'keyring must contain a current verification key'.

LOOKUP defensively rejects non-safe-integer issuedAt at :151-152, returning key_unusable rather than trusting the sole current caller. Negatives exist for NaN, POSITIVE_INFINITY, and MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+1 (service-envelope.test :480-484) plus -1/1.5/MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+1 on skew (:442), so safe-integer is distinguished from integer.

MOUNTED full-createApp plants cover all four required values and prove non-echo on BOTH channels:
- absent: 503 SPONSOR_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE with diagnostics toEqual([]) — quiet, so absence is distinguishable from malformed presence;
- malformed present: same opaque 503, body not.toContain(malformed), diagnostics exactly one [wire] invalid service-envelope keyring / KEYRING_CONFIG_INVALID entry, and JSON.stringify(diagnostics) not.toContain(malformed);
- all-retired: identical shape, not.toContain(retiredKeyring) in body and diagnostics;
- one current key: reaches mounted signature and nonce ingress before the typed post-auth MINT_BODY_INVALID.
No configured kid or key bytes are echoed anywhere.

INTERPRETATION WORTH RECORDING, so a later auditor does not 'fix' it: the acceptance phrase 'fail at the intended startup/configuration boundary' is implemented as a TYPED DIAGNOSTIC, not a throw. app.ts:556-570 catches KeyringConfigError, leaves keyring undefined, and logs once per credential tuple. That is the correct reading, not a residual soft-fail. Throwing inside createApp would 500 every PUBLIC read — /, /cursor, /schemas/*, /capabilities — over a SPONSOR-plane misconfiguration, breaking Rule A5 'reads are free' and A7 'cheap by construction'. And keeping the public refusal identical for absent vs malformed is required by A5's policy-refusal class: a caller-visible difference would turn the sponsor plane into a configuration oracle. The distinction therefore belongs in the operator log channel exactly where it now lives.

Frozen: keyring.ts a1660ae9, app.ts 82cb0e30 (identical at open and close). Note apps/wire/test/unit/service-envelope.test.ts moved during the audit, ea3ca679 -> 13f08112 under concurrent peer activity, so its cited line numbers are a current read, not frozen; the assertions above were verified against the post-move bytes.

BOUNDARY: static current-byte read only. Fresh 1m load 13.38, above the <10 ceiling — no Bun, typecheck, Biome, UBS, or runtime. Nothing was executed, so this is source ACCEPT, not a gate-backed close: canonical Wire gates and deployed startup/runtime behavior remain pending, as every prior comment on this bead has also said. No unrelated paths, no stage, no commit, no close.

title: W1.4 Generation pipeline: JSON Schema, examples, TS types (CI drift-fail)
description: WHY: Published JSON Schema and examples are what curl-first agents and asimp validate use offline; if any generated artifact drifts from Zod, changes nondeterministically, or gives an invalid example, clients learn a lie. WHAT: deterministic generation from packages/contracts to versioned JSON Schema documents for every read/write envelope, at least one minimal and one representative valid example per kind, filled contract-error examples referenced by fix_hints, TypeScript types for Worker/web/render consumers, and machine-readable schema/example indexes. Canonical serialization and stable ordering make output byte-identical across machines; generated files are checked in and CI fails on an uncommitted diff. Additive v1 evolution and semantic new-version naming are encoded in generator metadata; old schemas/examples remain readable. TESTS: unit tests for Zod-to-schema edge cases, conditional requirements, additionalProperties false, unions/discriminators, ID formats, examples and canonical ordering; golden tests regenerate twice in clean processes and compare bytes, then validate every example against its schema and every invalid W1.5 fixture against the expected path/code; compatibility tests classify additive versus semantic changes and deliberately mutate a generated artifact to prove the drift gate fails. Run on supported Bun/OS versions where serialization could vary. DIAGNOSTICS: OPS.2a logs generator/schema/example IDs, source and output digests, tool versions, duration, changed paths, validation code/pointer and bounded diffs—never fixture bodies that may later contain sensitive canaries. DONE: one root command generates the complete index deterministically; CI and local output agree; consumers import only generated types/schemas; every failure identifies the source schema, generated target, digest, pointer and reproduction command.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/golden tests cover each generator, canonical ordering, Unicode/math, examples, type/schema compile, deterministic reruns and deliberate contract changes; independent parsers validate emitted JSON Schema and OpenAPI fragments. scripts/e2e-generated-contracts.sh packages the generated artifact, installs it into clean Worker/render/CLI consumers, runs W1.5 valid/invalid fixtures, and fails on checked-in drift or uncommitted generated output. OPS.2a JSONL records source/generator/output digests, schema/kind/version, consumer/tool version, fixture verdict, missing/extra symbols, duration and bounded diff; never fixture bodies with sensitive canaries, credentials, tokens, cookies, or local machine paths.

WHAT EXISTS AND WORKS. `generate` -> src/generate.ts -> writeGeneratedArtifacts (artifacts.ts:567-573) writes every entry of generatedArtifacts(). `check:drift` -> src/check-drift.ts -> checkGeneratedArtifacts (artifacts.ts:547-565) reads each checked-in file, byte-compares against regenerated content, tolerates ENOENT as drift, and exits 1 on any drift with a typed diagnostic. A typed public registry (public-schemas.ts) imports six of the eight schemas as Wrangler text modules and app.ts:2 serves them at /schemas/<name>. That machinery is real and byte-exact; the findings below are about what is MISSING, not about it being wrong.

BLOCKER 1 - THE DRIFT GATE IS WIRED NOWHERE. THIS IS THE FALSE-GREEN. `check:drift` appears exactly once in the repository as a source/config string: its own definition at packages/contracts/package.json:15. Nothing invokes it - not root package.json, not scripts/suite/cli.ts (whose only lanes are d1-migration-contract, d1-migration-local and g0-spikes), not the contracts package `test` script, and there is no .github/workflows directory at all. CONSEQUENCE: a green root check, a green toolchain:test, and a green contracts `test` all pass WITHOUT ever comparing generated bytes to Zod. The acceptance's "CI fails on an uncommitted diff" is therefore unmet in the strongest sense - there is no CI, and the local dispatcher does not run the gate either. Every prior bead comment reporting "generation/drift pass" (e7j.1 00:29Z, 00:44Z; jgqf history) recorded a MANUAL invocation, not a gate; none of those results is reproducible by any command a reviewer would think to run. Smallest fix: add a contracts drift lane to the suite dispatcher so `bun run check` covers it.

BLOCKER 2 - NO EXAMPLES AND NO INDEX ARE GENERATED. The acceptance requires "at least one minimal and one representative valid example per kind", "filled contract-error examples referenced by fix_hints", and "machine-readable schema/example indexes". packages/contracts/generated contains only .schema.json and .types.ts; a search for example/index/registry artifacts returns nothing. So the acceptance's downstream tests - validate every example against its schema, and validate every invalid W1.5 fixture against its expected path/code - have no inputs to run against. This is the largest single gap to W1 completion and it is upstream of the golden-test work, not parallel to it.

BLOCKER 3 - scripts/e2e-generated-contracts.sh DOES NOT EXIST. The acceptance names this script by exact path and assigns it four jobs: package the generated artifact, install it into clean Worker/render/CLI consumers, run W1.5 valid/invalid fixtures, and fail on checked-in drift or uncommitted generated output. Nothing at that path. Consumer-coherence is therefore asserted by nothing: no test proves consumers import ONLY generated types/schemas rather than reaching into Zod source.

BLOCKER 4 - REGISTRY COVERAGE IS 6 OF 8, SILENTLY. public-schemas.ts imports enrollment, enrollment-capsule, ledger, problem, screening and sessions. NOT served: contracts-scaffold and s2-cost-receipt. Whether either belongs on the public face is a real decision (s2-cost-receipt is plausibly internal), but nothing in the source records that decision, and nothing fails if a NEW generated schema is added and never registered. That is the same class as the manifest schema_heads gap on zdz.2: an additive artifact silently missing from its index. Smallest fix: one assertion that every generated .schema.json is either registered or on an explicit internal allowlist.

NOT BLOCKERS, recorded so they are not re-litigated: byte-exactness of the registry against the generated files is already enforced (exactTextModule with the artifact path). The generator/drift pair is deterministic in shape - artifacts are produced from one list and compared by content, with ENOENT treated as drift rather than as absence.

title: W10: Hardening
description: WHY: Fable promises are real only when mechanically verified by tests capable of failing. W10 is the independent proof layer over W1-W9, not the place features first acquire tests: every implementation bead already lands its unit/integration/E2E coverage through OPS.2a, and W10 composes cross-system adversarial and user-journey evidence. WHAT: Cold-Agent Gauntlet—10 fresh memoryless sessions across at least three harnesses, paste block only, sponsor approval scripted; score name/pair/token/session/pack-following/workshop/falsifiable promotion/injected-422 recovery/handback; pass at least 8 of 10 and median at most 25K tokens. Protocol fixture/state-machine table pins P1-P13, implicit-path equivalence and review isolation. Epistemic controls include subtly false proofs, weaker-statement formal artifacts, scope/citation/leakage/definition traps and valid nulls that must pass. Real auth-race matrix proves exactly one credential outcome. Property tests cover IDs/scopes, sequences, transitions, idempotency, pagination and arbitrary-Unicode rendering. Red team covers injection bare-versus-inoculated, report-dont-engage, dual-use aggregation/FN zero, oracle probing, cap economics, auth and integrity. Load/fault suites validate p95/cost/degradation/backpressure; Playwright proves the human journey, privacy/cache, search/artifacts/moderation and accessibility. Error-copy/slop/ceremony audits complete the user experience. TEST EVIDENCE: OPS.2a structured artifacts tie suite/scenario/seed/revision to request/event IDs, cursors, versions, timings, bounded diffs and safe reproduction commands. Gauntlet/dogfood/browser artifacts never retain credentials, fragments, cookies, raw transcripts, terminal scrollback, private bodies, chain-of-thought or detector internals. Every suite contains a seeded should-fail/fault case; gate/scorer/corpus/threshold changes are separate independently reviewed diffs. Green results state what was not proven; no local/mock proxy is used to claim staging/live evidence. DONE: all children close; gauntlet passes; fixture/corpus/property/auth/user/load suites are green at the exact revision; red-team findings are fixed or explicitly operator-accepted without weakening gates; structured evidence is diagnostic and secret-safe.
acceptance_criteria: Each W10 suite is independently rerunnable at an exact revision, contains a seeded should-fail/fault control, and publishes redacted structured evidence plus a no-claim boundary. title: Renderer accepts NUL text that HTML cannot represent faithfully
description: Fresh-eyes face audit found prepareProjection rejects unpaired UTF-16 surrogates but accepts U+0000 in projection strings. title: S-3 Workshop/ledger split spike
description:
WHY: The workshop/ledger split is the product thesis: continuous private work and a curated public record. If one workshop byte leaks to a public face/cache/search/export, or if any convenience path bypasses validation, the product is broken at birth. WHAT: implement the thinnest vertical slice: session open, working pack, workshop push, sponsor view, promote, and public delta. With two principals active, the sponsor sees the workshop card through the per-(Fellow,problem) workshop cursor while an anonymous browser sees no body, title, extract, count, cache variation, search result, or cursor movement; a second Fellow/sponsor also sees nothing. Promotion moves the object through the one validator and public transaction. Honesty probes send an author-writable disposition/proved field and receive SCHEMA_INVALID with P2/P4 guidance, then promote an NFKC norm-hash duplicate and receive DUPLICATE_CLAIM/P11 with the existing ID and review-or-refine action. TESTS: automate the paired-browser/API privacy matrix, separate public/workshop cursor allocation for two Fellows on one problem, cache/search/export negative probes, valid promotion, both refusals, retry/idempotency, and disconnect around commit. Run against local bindings and preview; at least one seeded should-leak fixture must fail the suite to prove the assertions are live. DIAGNOSTICS: OPS.2a structured steps record principals as synthetic IDs, route template, status/code, public and workshop cursor before/after, request/event IDs, projection digest and timings; never workshop bytes, cookies, credentials, raw bodies, or browser storage. DONE: retained redacted structured evidence proves sponsor visibility and every unauthorized absence, both refusals are permanent CI fixtures, and the mechanical invariant is exact: public seq is per problem; workshop seq is separate per (Fellow,problem); public readers never consult the latter.

PRIVATE-CAS SPIKE CASE: force a workshop body above the spill threshold, capture its content digest from the authorized test state, and probe that digest directly at artifacts.asimposium.org plus every anonymous/cache path. The sponsor view must retrieve through the authenticated Worker path, while the public artifact host remains unable to serve the bytes until an explicit successful promotion/publication step. This retires the shared-CAS-versus-direct-domain privacy ambiguity before W2.7.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: The exact G0 flow opens a session, fetches a `working` pack with mandatory `omitted[]`, pushes workshop work, proves sponsor-only visibility, promotes through the one validator, and observes exactly one public delta. Unit/property tests cover public sequence per problem, workshop sequence per Fellow/problem, access predicates, projection/cache/export/search exclusion and promote copy semantics. Mock-free D1/R2 plus real renderer tests use paired sponsor/Fellow principals. scripts/e2e-s3-split.sh creates identical private/public canaries, proves sponsor workshop visibility and anonymous/cross-sponsor absence across HTML/md/json/search/cache/export/errors, refuses self-certification and near-duplicate promotion with rule citations, then promotes safely and verifies exactly one public event. Structured JSONL records synthetic principal/problem/workshop IDs, route template, pre/post cursors, request/event IDs, decision/code, cache/search/export assertion and timing; never body bytes, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, or private extracts.

The seeded split suite fails if a private spilled body is serviceable by digest from the public artifact hostname, if cross-sponsor responses reveal existence, or if publication exposes bytes before the verified public binding is complete.

title: W8.5 Sponsor console + onboarding dialog
description:
WHY: The sponsor is the accountability spine. The console is where enrollment approval, safe credential control, private-workshop visibility, problem-publication responsibility, and recovery happen; a human must be able to operate it without learning the API or accidentally bypassing the Worker validator. WHAT: /console shows my Fellows with honest live state, last material event, assignments, token profiles/last_used_at/max-three hygiene, pause/revoke/panic and compromised recovery; pending enrollment cards and history; onboarding dialog with problem binding, first directive, scopes, event/artifact budgets, expiry, harness selector, fragment paste block, waiting state and explicit Approve/Reduce/Deny card; directive composer with delivered/acked state; follows and report/appeal status. Add the sponsor problem-proposal queue: Fellow/sponsor proposals remain private-draft, show exact statement/falsifier/motivation/scope/license and sharpening-review state, allow safe edit/directive or publish only through the Worker lifecycle gate, require license/patent-disclosure acknowledgment, and never imply that propose-problems scope grants publication. Surface account data export/deletion request and Fellow transfer/recovery entry points with recent-auth step-up; public ledger retention/tombstone consequences are explained before confirmation. Every mutation is a Next.js server action signed in the service envelope and rendered from the resulting Worker response/event, never optimistic authority. TESTS: component/unit tests for state/action/permission mapping and copy; Playwright/API E2E for honest approval, reduced scopes, denial, expiry, wrong sponsor, double submit, pause/revoke/panic before next write, multiple credential profiles, compromised recovery, directive ack, follow/report state, private problem proposal, failed sharpening/publish, successful publication with acknowledgment, export/deletion and transfer step-up. Structured logs follow OPS.2a with synthetic principal/enrollment/problem/action/event IDs and timing; redact fragments, tokens, cookies, emails, directive/workshop bodies, key fingerprints and proposal text. DONE: all actions have precise confirmation/error/recovery states, no client-side success precedes Worker commit, approval and proposal journeys are accessible/keyboard complete, and the one-sentence human onboarding journey passes against staging.

PROBLEM-INTENT UX BOUNDARY: the sponsor proposal queue first saves a private governance brief and assigns it to one of the sponsor own active Fellows; it does not itself create an attributed scientific Problem. The console shows awaiting-Fellow-adoption versus adopted-private-draft distinctly. Only after the Fellow submits the exact statement/falsifier/motivation through POST /v1/problems may a sponsor/steward publish through the lifecycle gate. The final card shows immutable Fellow/session/model/harness scientific authorship and the sponsor/steward acting publication principal. Seeds use an onboarded Fellow, never a platform-authored scientific shortcut. A sponsor with no active Fellow can save a brief and start onboarding but cannot publish it.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/component and golden tests cover every console state, permission and copy path for Fellows, credentials, enrollments, directives, follows, reports/appeals, private problem-intent briefs, assignment/adoption, adopted private drafts, publication/license acknowledgement, immutable author versus publisher display, compromised recovery, and W3.8 transfer/export/deletion manifests; no action renders success before Worker commit. title: W11.1 asimp scaffold + auth (login PKCE/device, connect, keychain)
description:
WHY: asimp is optional; curl remains first-class. The CLI earns its existence through safe auth, offline resilience and machine-readable ergonomics. Fragment/token handling and the loopback-versus-poll race are security-critical, so diagnostics must be useful without ever echoing secrets. Fresh code may adopt the operator jsm CLI shape, not copy proprietary text. WHAT: Rust/clap static binary. asimp login uses OAuth PKCE S256 with ephemeral loopback callback racing a high-entropy server poll; exactly one result wins and the loser shuts down cleanly; --device follows RFC 8628 pending/slow_down/expired semantics. AUTHORIZATION OWNERSHIP: this bead also owns the additive @asimposium/contracts shapes and Worker/apex transaction endpoints needed by login. Browser Google OAuth authenticates the human sponsor but never becomes direct Fellow authority: an existing-Fellow credential requires the same explicit, recent-auth sponsor approval card, current Fellow/sponsor binding, requested profile/scopes/grants, max-three-token and account-posture checks as Propylon; a first-time --device invocation delegates to W3.5 with the full Fellow proposal and same approval card, never a metadata-free code. Login cannot create or transfer an identity, change the immutable model/harness declaration, exceed existing grants, or mint on page load. The apex sponsor action travels in the signed service envelope; a. never reads the cookie; callback/poll exchange uses a body-only flow handle, returns one credential once, and handles disconnect/replay through an idempotent status result without logging or reissuing the token. asimp connect parses the fragment locally, POSTs the secret only in the registration body, clears buffers where practical, never prints/logs/reposts it and warns about URL handling. Storage ladder is OS keyring, encrypted file with safe permissions, then explicit paste-the-URL fallback; no silent plaintext. Optional PoP remains standards-based DPoP/HTTP Message Signatures with published vectors if later enabled; bearer is default. Every command supports --json, stable exit codes, no ANSI off-TTY and request/event IDs on success. TESTS: unit/property tests for URL/fragment parsing including Unicode/percent/empty/malformed/multiple-fragment cases, PKCE/state/nonce, callback binding, token response decoding, storage selection/permissions/redaction and cancellation cleanup; mock auth-server integration covers callback/poll interleavings, CSRF/state mismatch, port collision, browser failure, device slow_down, expired/denied, ambiguous transport and keyring failure; staging E2E connects/approves/hello using synthetic identity and proves only one credential. OPS.2a/Rust logs record command, auth-flow state, request/event IDs, safe error code/timing and credential profile/key ID, never URL fragments, authorization codes, verifier, state/nonce, tokens, cookies, key material, proposal bodies, raw terminal transcript or hidden reasoning. DONE: auth/connect work end-to-end and recover with precise next steps; never-log canaries absent from stdout/stderr/files/test artifacts/process arguments; race matrix passes; retained evidence is structured outcomes, not a live-session transcript.

CREDENTIAL RECOVERY BOUNDARY: login and connect consume the same W3.4 one-time credential contract. An ambiguous disconnect polls only for the non-secret issuance status; it never replays or remints credential bytes. If the client cannot prove possession by authenticated first use, asimp reports CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN and opens the explicit recent-auth sponsor revoke/rebind path. Unit and staging tests inspect stdout, stderr, process arguments, keychain fallbacks, D1 snapshots, backups and artifacts for secret leakage and prove the loser in the loopback-versus-server-poll race cannot receive a second outcome.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover CLI argument/state machines, PKCE/state/nonce, loopback origin/port binding, browser and poll race cancellation, body-only flow handles, existing-Fellow versus full-proposal device authorization, sponsor binding, recent-auth, scope/grant reduction, token cap, account posture, exactly-one credential, storage ladder, URL/fragment parsing, no-ANSI/JSON output, and stable exit codes. Contract/golden fixtures include valid approval plus page-load, blind-code, wrong sponsor, bearer-on-sponsor, cookie-on-a., stale binding, model-change, over-scope, cap, denied, expired, replay, CSRF/state mismatch, port collision, browser failure, keyring failure and disconnect-before/after-mint cases. Mock-free Worker/Auth.js integration races callback/poll/approval/denial/revocation and proves no path bypasses W3.4/W3.5/W3.7 policy. scripts/e2e-asimp-auth.sh uses synthetic sponsors/Fellows on staging to connect by fragment, login an existing Fellow, run first-time --device, reduce/deny/expire, retry an ambiguous result, revoke, and call hello; exactly one credential survives each approved flow. OPS.2a JSONL records command, auth-flow kind/state, synthetic sponsor/Fellow/proposal IDs, request/event IDs, non-secret key/profile ID, contract/policy digest, status/code, attempt and timing; never URLs or fragments, user/device/authorization codes, flow handles, verifier/state/nonce, tokens or hashes, cookies, OAuth/service signatures, proposal bodies, key material, terminal scrollback, browser storage, raw traces/transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

title: W10.6 Red team: injection A/B, dual-use FN=0, oracle probing, economics, auth
description: WHY: R-3 (cross-agent injection incident) and R-10 (dangerous content evades screening) are the two highest-impact security risks. The red team converts the five-layer defense from claimed to measured — in particular the inoculation A/B, whose value must be a number, not a vibe. Findings become PERMANENT fixtures; post-launch reported real-world payloads feed the same corpus forever. WHAT: one structured pass each, pre-launch (G2 gate): (1) INJECTION — adversarial ledger corpus built from the ACIP taxonomy: authority laundering and role impersonation ("SYSTEM:", "as the Symposiarch"), encoding/steganographic smuggling (base64-shaped runs, character codes), nested-context escape (instructions wrapped in fiction/quotes/hypotheticals), format smuggling (directives in code comments, HTML comments, markdown structure), forged control surfaces (fake system items, fake next_actions JSON, fake pack items, fake handbacks — the sharpest site-specific vector), multi-post aggregation. Run against a live probe agent TWICE, bare then inoculated with /inoculation.md, reporting compliance-rate deltas per category, plus verification that the inoculated probe REPORTS (POST /v1/reports, reason=injection) rather than quotes, follows, or publicly dissects the payload. (2) MODERATION EVASION — violations dressed as science; the dual-use hard-reject class must hold FN = 0 INCLUDING piecewise-aggregation cases (the screen evaluates in context: problem statement + author recent promotions); legitimate weird math holds FP < 5% ("kill the process", "attack model", "viral vector" pass because the fixture corpus says they must). (3) ORACLE PROBING — iterate against POLICY_DENIED responses and verify no trigger phrase, matched pattern, or classifier reasoning leaks (ADR-18: coarse category + appeal path only); the refusal texts themselves become fixtures. (4) ECONOMICS — cap evasion via multi-Fellow sponsors (caps are per Fellow AND per sponsor). (5) AUTH — code replay, token scanning (prefix-identifiable tokens findable by secret scanners), principal confusion. DONE: all five passes executed with written findings; every finding closed or explicitly operator-risk-accepted; corpora and refusal-text fixtures land in CI.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Versioned unit/corpus runners cover ACIP injection classes, system-item mimicry, encoded/paraphrased and multi-post dual-use, legitimate weird science, secret/PII, policy-oracle probes, auth confusion, SSRF and economic abuse; seeds and holdouts are separate. Mock-free staging scripts/e2e-red-team.sh submit cases through actual workshop/promote/search/render/cache/service-envelope/artifact paths, probe transient exposure, model outage and appeal, and assert FP/FN plus cost limits without tuning on the holdout. OPS.2a logs corpus/policy/model digests, scenario/category, request/event IDs, coarse outcome, public-exposure canary result, latency/cost bucket and assertion diff; never bodies, detector patterns/raw scores, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, raw prompts/transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

title: W2.1 D1 migrations: full schema census
description:
WHY: The schema encodes the ontology; append-only enforcement, attribution, membership roles, and separate cursor scopes must be mechanical rather than conventions hidden in handlers. WHAT: numbered, deploy-scripted D1 migrations for users; fellows (immutable model/harness declaration, sponsor, compromised lifecycle); fellow_tokens; sponsorship_transfers (outgoing/receiving sponsor, immutable manifest digest, bounded expiry, cancel/refuse/accept state, step-up evidence references, credential/access handoff cursor); retired identity/byline tombstones and account-lifecycle audit references; enrollments (join/device, secret and flow-handle hashes, mint scopes/budgets/expiry, proposal/approval); sessions (declared model/harness/reasoning_effort/tools_note, observed client/protocol/OS, attestation, protocol version+digest, handback); leases; workshop_objects; areas; problems (PUBLIC seq only, writer cap, admission mode, private-draft/unlisted visibility, current statement); problem_areas/merges/forks; MEMBERSHIPS with observer/contributor/steward roles and founding-steward provenance; statement_versions; claims/claim_versions; claim_deps; version-pinned reviewable claim_relations; hypotheses; proof_gaps; conflicts; evidence; reviews; citations; dead_ends and retry triggers; directives; review_requests; events envelopes carrying immutable actor/effective-principal plus the full scientific attribution snapshot (Fellow, sponsor_at_event, session, model_string_self_declared, harness) and declared/observed labels; event_content; content_controls; outbox; idempotency; rate_buckets; reports; moderation_actions; screening_log; flags; follows; artifacts; and FTS5 over public content only. First-class synthesis/question/retraction/commentary persistence must be explicit in the migration design (dedicated tables or a documented generic versioned-ledger-object table consumed by their W5/W8 projections); they may not exist only as opaque event payloads if their routes require indexed state. CURSORS: problems carry the monotonically allocated public seq; workshop sequence is allocated separately per (fellow, problem), never as one global problem workshop counter and never visible to public faces. APPEND-ONLY: D1 has one application binding, so enforce envelope immutability with DDL triggers that abort UPDATE/DELETE on events (plus storage APIs that expose append only); lawful redaction changes event_content/content_controls while the event envelope, digest, actor, type, and seq remain untouched. DONE: migrations apply on fresh and existing local D1; schema snapshot names every census object and index; membership constraints and role authorization join cleanly; per-(fellow,problem) workshop cursors advance independently; UPDATE/DELETE attempts on event envelopes fail; private/workshop rows are absent from public FTS; migration runner is idempotent and refuses out-of-order application.



RECOVERY/RETENTION SCHEMA ADDITIONS: model immutable workshop revisions and their current-version pointer; distinguish content_author_fellow/session from acting_principal_kind/id on every event that may be performed by a sponsor for a Fellow. Store long-lived credential verifier hashes plus non-secret issuance/delivery receipts and rebind state only; no table may retain replayable plaintext or reversibly encrypted bearer material. Add explicit artifact_bindings/reference state and signed retention/deletion controls sufficient to garbage-collect unreferenced private CAS bytes and to prevent an older backup restore from reviving deleted personal/private data, revoked credentials, cancelled enrollments or superseded access grants.


OQ-10, CAUSALITY, AND EMBEDDING STORAGE: introduce a stable sponsor_accounts principal plus sponsor_account_members, with the launch constraint of one accountable human on an individual account and no organization UI or authority yet; Fellow, quota, report-independence and sponsor-at-event foreign keys target the stable account while approvals also freeze the acting human. Persist caused_by as normalized, deduplicated, canonically ordered qualified event edges with foreign keys plus transaction-time prior-commit/earlier-batch authorization checks suitable for replay; public projections store permission-filtered omission metadata rather than private parent IDs. Add a public-only embeddings store keyed by content digest, model, version, dimension and encoding, with source object/version, lifecycle and build cursor; vectors are never evidence and no workshop/private-draft row can bind. Artifact bindings also record private versus published delivery namespace plus immutable server-derived license-policy/content-class/provenance snapshots, so a row cannot point private-only or rights-ineligible bytes at the public artifacts host or borrow another binding rights state.

PUBLIC REVISION STORAGE: every contract-declared revisable kind has an immutable version table or generic version row, a constrained current-version pointer, unique (object_id, version), original author/governance provenance and compare-and-swap update path. Reviews/relations/citations keep explicit version foreign keys and never join through current head. Kinds corrected only by supersession/retraction have no update path. Migration snapshot and replay can reconstruct heads solely from events and detect a pointer that skips, regresses or references a missing version.

GLOBAL PUBLIC-CHANGE CURSOR STORAGE: add a singleton site-state row for the canonical GET /cursor invalidation revision. It is monotonically advanced only inside a transaction that changes anonymous-visible projection state and is not an event sequence, ranking, count, or replacement for each problem public_seq. The schema and rebuild metadata distinguish it from problem and workshop cursors, prevent decrement/wrap/reuse, and give W7.1 a cheap origin read without scanning events.

GLOBAL EVENT-SCOPE SEQUENCE: the singleton state also owns a distinct monotonically allocated global_event_seq for events whose canonical scope is global (identity lifecycle, site governance/moderation and other contract-declared global commands). Event primary/foreign keys bind both scope_kind and scope_id so the reserved global scope cannot collide with a problem. global_event_seq is canonical ordering within that scope; it is never reused as the site-wide /cursor invalidation revision or exposed as an activity metric.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: SQL lint/table tests verify numbering, checksums, foreign keys, indexes, constraints, monotonic per-scope counters, privacy columns, sponsorship-transfer and account-deletion constraints, no-orphan sponsor invariants, outbox/projection coupling, downgrade prohibition and schema census completeness. Mock-free local D1 applies every migration from empty and supported prior snapshots twice, rejects gaps/drift/out-of-order files, and exercises concurrent writers. scripts/e2e-migrations.sh deploys a disposable staging database, runs smoke, takes export/checkpoint, applies forward migration with injected interruption, resumes safely, and compares schema/data invariants. OPS.2a logs environment/binding ID, revision, migration ID/digest, phase, row/schema/checkpoint digests, status/code, duration and diff; never SQL row contents, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, or production identifiers.

Migration tests cover the individual-sponsor launch constraint without hard-coding human identity into durable attribution, qualified causal-edge integrity/replay, public-only embedding provenance and rebuild, and private-versus-published artifact namespace constraints. Supported-snapshot migration fixtures prove each addition preserves historical sponsor/event meaning.

Migration/concurrency tests race public revisions for every storage pattern, reject skipped/duplicate/missing bases, preserve pinned historical foreign keys, rebuild current heads from events and prove no SQL path can mutate a prior version row.

Migration/invariant tests cover singleton creation and upgrade, monotonic advance across multiple problems and batches, no movement for workshop/private/rejected/rolled-back writes, public content-control/process changes, overflow refusal, restore/rebuild reconciliation and the absence of principal/problem/activity data from the cursor row.

Schema tests allocate interleaved problem, global-event and workshop sequences, prove uniqueness/order within each qualified scope, forbid cross-scope parent ambiguity and counter substitution, and rebuild the global counter from its event envelopes without changing the separate /cursor revision.

title: W11.4 asimp spool, sync (replay-safe), doctor
description:
WHY: Agents work through flaky networks and interrupted sessions; the spool is what makes the CLI resilient without ever lying about what happened. Replay safety is the design center: one-time exchanges are NEVER blindly retried after an ambiguous transport failure. WHAT: durable spool under ~/.asimp/: per-problem cursors, unsent idempotent writes, resumable digest-verified artifact uploads, secret-redacted logs. asimp sync: drains the spool, retrying ONLY operations whose replay semantics are known (idempotency-keyed writes replay safely; enrollment/token exchanges never auto-retry). Spooled writes stamp client_occurred_at so the ledger can honestly display "worked at / posted at" when they diverge materially (provenance only, never trusted for ordering). asimp doctor: connectivity, token validity (and which token of the <= 3 active), cursor sanity vs server, spool health, protocol-version match — idempotent, every finding paired with a suggested remediation. DONE: kill-and-resume e2e (cut the network mid-session; sync recovers exactly-once, no duplicate promotions — verified against the idempotency table); doctor covers every detectable failure with a fix line; spool logs verified secret-free.

REPLAY-WINDOW TRUTH TABLE: exactly-once is claimed only while the server can authoritatively replay or reconcile the operation. A never-attempted spool item may be assigned an idempotency key when first sent even if it was drafted more than 24 hours ago; a definitively rejected item remains rejected until the user changes it into a new logical write. An attempted item with an ambiguous transport outcome keeps its original key and is reconciled by receipt/event/cursor/object digest while the 24-hour server window is live. If that window expires without an authoritative match, sync MUST stop that item in an explicit unknown_commit state, preserve all evidence, show read-only reconciliation commands and require a human/agent choice; it never rotates the key, blindly resubmits, marks success or deletes the item. Clock skew, sleep/wake and offline duration use server timestamps where available. Doctor distinguishes unsent, retryable, committed, rejected and unknown_commit and states which evidence would resolve each.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover spool versions, safe permissions, ordering, draft age versus first-attempt age, server/client clock skew, 24-hour boundaries, exact-key retention, receipt/event/object reconciliation, rejected-item edits, unknown_commit quarantine, partial sync, retry/backoff, corrupt/truncated entries, token rotation and crash recovery. scripts/e2e-asimp-spool.sh queues old-never-sent work, disconnects before/after commits, restarts within and beyond the replay window, reconciles public and private writes, expires credential delivery, and proves exactly-once where authoritative and explicit unknown_commit where not. A seeded implementation that generates a new key after ambiguity must fail. CLI/OPS.2a JSONL records item/operation digests, first-attempt/server times, request/event IDs, cursor/status/code, reconciliation evidence class, recovery action, duration and diff; never bodies, keys, credential material, cookies, fragments, home paths, terminal scrollback, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

title: Session open and close bypass centralized Fellow write policy

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE REVIEW — 2026-08-19, CrimsonGate, hard read-only. Tested the acceptance design against Fable and the current evaluator (apps/wire/src/enrollment/service.ts sha 731275013a699f1975c0e240a49ea915d8cc3bcffd099b6a593c763eb286601b). Root's four corrections all hold; three additional findings below, one of which changes the budget scope.

CONFIRMS ROOT (2): the scope gate is service.ts:669 'if (effect !== "workshop.push" && !credential.grantedScopes.includes(effect))', and FellowWriteEffect = RequestedScope | "workshop.push" (service.ts:518). Adding session.open/close as effects without touching RequestedScope therefore requires widening the unscoped exemption, not the scope vocabulary.

SMALLEST TYPE/SIGNATURE CHANGES (four, all in service.ts, no contract or route type churn):
1. type FellowUnscopedEffect = "workshop.push" | "session.open" | "session.close"; FellowWriteEffect = RequestedScope | FellowUnscopedEffect.
2. Replace the literal comparison at :669 with a type-guard predicate isUnscopedEffect(effect): effect is FellowUnscopedEffect. NOT a bare Set.has() — the current literal comparison is load-bearing for narrowing: after 'effect !== "workshop.push"' TypeScript narrows effect to RequestedScope, which is what makes grantedScopes.includes(effect) typecheck. A Set membership test loses that narrowing and the includes() call stops compiling.
3. Add FellowSessionAdmissionTarget { kind: "session-admission"; problemId: string } to FellowWriteTarget. It must carry NEITHER publication NOR membershipRole: supplying either requires the existence-sensitive lookup this bead forbids, so the type is what enforces the ordering guarantee rather than a comment. The existing else-branch refuses not_a_member at :698, which is exactly why the admission branch cannot reuse it.
4. Quarantine disposition per effect (see FINDING A).

FINDING A — QUARANTINE IS NOT A REFUSAL TODAY, AND THE ACCEPTANCE ASSUMES IT IS. The evaluator returns decision "quarantine" with handling "hold-for-operator-review" (:735-744), not a refusal. That is correct for workshop.push (accept and hold). It is not representable for session.open or session.close: there is no half-open session to hold, and this bead's own plants require a 403 with the session still open. So the quarantine branch needs a per-effect disposition — refuse for the unscoped session effects, hold for workshop.push — and FellowAuthorizationRefusalReason (:558-571) needs a suspicious_review_quarantine member, which today exists only as the operatorReason on the quarantine arm (:599). Deciding this in the route instead would scatter the very policy Fable centralizes.

FINDING B — EVENT BUDGET DOES NOT BELONG IN THIS BEAD. Stronger than root's (4): apps/wire/src/sessions/router.ts contains no event append at all (no appendEvent/recordEvent/INSERT INTO events); all three authorize call sites hardcode {eventsRecorded: 0, artifactBytesRecorded: 0} at :828, :971, :1184. Session open and close therefore CONSUME no event budget, so there is no consumption for this bead to make atomic. What remains is only the CHECK, and the check is free: the eventBudget clause at :716-719 is effect-agnostic, so adding session.open as an effect subjects it automatically with zero new code. RECOMMENDATION: drop the route-level exhausted-event-budget plant from acceptance — with usage fabricated as zero it can only false-green — and keep at most a POLICY-level case that passes a synthetic non-zero usage.eventsRecorded straight to authorizeFellowWrite. That case is honest because it tests the pure function, not the route. The durable grant-wide read, credential attribution and same-transaction guard are wqlf's charter verbatim, and wqlf's own comment already records that a preflight COUNT cannot fix it. Suggest a kgaa -> wqlf dependency for the route-level guarantee; there is no edge between them today.

FINDING C — ADJACENT FABRICATED TARGET, NOT THIS BEAD'S SCOPE BUT NEXT DOOR. The close-path authorize at router.ts:961-975 builds its target with publication: "published" and unlisted: false hardcoded rather than read. It is currently harmless because the private-draft clause (:707-709) only gates promote and review, so the workshop.push outcome is unchanged — but it is a fabricated policy input that becomes wrong the moment the private-draft rule covers another effect. Worth a note on zdz or a fresh bead rather than widening kgaa.

EXACT CAUSAL CASES (policy-level, pure, no route or D1 needed):
- open, wrong binding: effect session.open, grantedResources.problemBinding = P-OTHER, target {kind: session-admission, problemId: P-4DSP} -> refuse problem_binding_mismatch. Must be byte-identical 403 to the next case.
- open, suspicious_review: fellowStatus suspicious_review, binding correct -> refuse (per FINDING A), NOT quarantine-hold.
- open, admission has no membership: same input with no membershipRole anywhere in the target -> allow. This is the non-vacuity control proving the admission branch does not fall through to not_a_member.
- open, expired grant: grantedResources.fellowGrantExpiresAt <= now -> refuse grant_expired, and assert it outranks the admission branch.
- open, budget: usage.eventsRecorded >= eventBudget -> refuse event_budget_exhausted (policy-level only, per FINDING B).
- close, suspicious_review -> refuse, with a separate assertion that the session row is unchanged.
- close, allowed -> allow, and the exact-replay control must still return the original response after a later lifecycle or scope change, proving replay precedes policy.
- ordering guard: a source-level assertion that the route calls authorizeFellowWrite before any problem/session/membership read, in the same shape as the 8xn.3 cold-path guard.

No edits, no runtime, nothing closed.
