Two mounted bypasses. session.open goes authenticate -> replayOrCommit -> problem/session/membership reads and atomic inserts, without authorizeFellowWrite; a valid suspicious or wrong-binding credential can obtain problem/session 404/409 distinctions and create session+membership (201). session.close likewise authenticates then replayOrCommit and closes a session without central authorization, so a valid suspicious credential can mutate closed_at/handback (201).

But the evaluator returns suspicious_review = quarantine / hold-for-operator-review, while neither route persists a held write/review item. migration 0012's fellow_write_review_windows is never consulted on this path. Credential suspicious_review has no production link to Symposiarch screening quarantine. Therefore the declared hold is dead/unobservable; current production effect is refusal, not durable quarantine.
4. Existing tests false-green: enrollment.test exercises the pure evaluator's quarantine branch, not a mounted write/hold. session-routes.test covers only active review-only scope behavior, not paused/revoked/compromised/suspicious or open/close. scripts/e2e-token-lifecycle.sh calls a mounted revoked open (correctly 401 FELLOW_TOKEN_INVALID), then fabricates a revoked binding and asserts the pure evaluator's distinct 401 UNAUTHORIZED equals that mounted effect; token-lifecycle-harness only checks that script text. Exact boundary: auth failures above are 401 FELLOW_TOKEN_INVALID; valid-binding policy failures (binding/budget and current suspicious fresh push/promote) are coarse 403 WRITE_REFUSED; structurally invalid valid-token bodies remain contract 422 before policy; an exact replay made while active remains 200 after active->suspicious because replay precedes policy, but pause/revoke/compromise produce 401 before replay. Authorization for admission must precede open's first problem/session/membership lookup; it must not demand pre-existing membership/publication because the allowed batch creates membership.
- For close, preserve exact replay preflight first; resolve the owned session and membership only to construct the existing-problem target, then authorize session.close before any close mutation.
- Make suspicious_review a central per-effect refusal for session.open/session.close (as already directed in #279/#280); retain current workshop/promotion quarantine disposition only as an explicitly separate unresolved no-persistence semantic, rather than misrepresenting it as implemented hold. Do not route through fellowAuthorizationResponse; mounted valid-binding policy denial remains the router's byte-identical 403.

MistyCanyon — HARD READ-ONLY next-repair packet (codebase-audit lens, security domain). No edits, runtime, type, lint, UBS, provider, Git or status change.

STATUS CORRECTION FIRST. kgaa is already CLOSED and the ordering repair is LANDED in 8375294 ("session open/close are unscoped lifecycle writes; authorize before lookups"). A plan to implement it would be a plan for work that exists, so this packet instead verifies the landed code against the five named properties and scopes the repair to what actually remains. Four of five hold; one does not, and one acceptance clause is structurally unreachable.

HASHES (start == end; nothing was modified):
  373b15afdb1b27d7aee53323ce9f82b064f7f745380a0f37e4f40fcbc1ea486a  apps/wire/src/sessions/router.ts
  731275013a699f1975c0e240a49ea915d8cc3bcffd099b6a593c763eb286601b  apps/wire/src/enrollment/service.ts
Note for anyone citing the earlier reviews: router.ts moved 18ea685b -> 373b15af across 8375294 and c9e99b2, so line numbers in the 16:09/16:12 comments have shifted (the sponsor workshop SELECT is now :1671, not :1552).

VERIFIED SATISFIED (no work needed).
1. EFFECTS/TARGETS. service.ts:518 FellowUnscopedEffect = "workshop.push" | "session.open" | "session.close", with the predicate at :523 widening the unscoped exemption rather than RequestedScope — root's correction (2) honoured. Admission target at :551 carries no membership requirement; session-close target at :562; evaluator branches at :724 and :729-730.
2. PRE-TARGET NON-ORACLE OPEN. Order in the open handler is: contract parse -> request digest -> replayResponseBeforeMutablePreconditions -> authorizeFellowWrite (target kind "session-admission") -> writeRefusedProblem() -> only then SELECT id FROM problems and SELECT session_id FROM sessions inside replayOrCommit. Authorization precedes BOTH existence probes, so neither problem existence nor an existing open session is observable to a refused credential.
3. PRE-MUTATION CLOSE. Same shape: replay -> authorize -> refuse -> replayOrCommit. The close mutation is downstream of the refusal.
4. 403 vs 401 SPLIT. fellowStatusCanAuthenticate (service.ts:109-113) admits only active and suspicious_review, so revoked/paused/compromised/archived fail at authenticate() with the uniform 401 and never reach policy; a still-valid credential failing binding, or quarantined by suspicious_review, receives the single 403 WRITE_REFUSED face. This is exactly root's correction (1), implemented as written.
Replay semantics are intact in both routes: replay is strictly first, so an exact successful replay still returns after later lifecycle or scope changes.

REMAINING WORK — TWO ITEMS, ONE OF WHICH THE BEAD ALREADY REQUIRED.

FINDING A (High) — DURABLE OPERATOR-REVIEW HONESTY IS UNIMPLEMENTED.
  Location: apps/wire/src/enrollment/service.ts:735-742 produces { decision: "quarantine", handling: "hold-for-operator-review", operatorReason: "suspicious_review_quarantine" }.
  Issue: all five router call sites (:551, :1061, :1274, :1525, plus the pack advisory pair at :938/:949) collapse it with `if (decision.decision !== "allow") return writeRefusedProblem();`. Grep for operator_review / hold-for-operator across apps/wire/src/sessions and apps/wire/src/krater returns nothing. Nothing is queued, recorded, or surfaced.
  Root cause: the evaluator names a durable handling mode that no consumer implements; the only consumer treats quarantine as an ordinary refusal.
  Why it matters here rather than as a nit: Rule A4 says the site never pretends. A decision literal that says "hold-for-operator-review" while the write is silently dropped is the code pretending to an operator workflow that does not exist. Either persist it or rename the handling to what actually happens.
  Fix (smallest honest): new migration db/migrations/0021_operator_review_holds.sql with (hold_id PK, fellow_id, credential_id, problem_id, effect, operator_reason, created_at, resolved_at NULL, resolver, UNIQUE(fellow_id, effect, problem_id, created_at)); write one row inside the SAME replayOrCommit batch that would have carried the mutation, so the hold is atomic with the refusal and cannot be lost; expose it only through the signed sponsor path. If that is more than this lane wants, the honest alternative is to change handling to "refused-no-hold" and drop operatorReason — but do NOT leave the current wording.

FINDING B (High) — THE EXHAUSTED-EVENT-BUDGET ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE IS STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE.
  Location: usage is hardcoded { eventsRecorded: 0, artifactBytesRecorded: 0 } at router.ts:548, :935, :1058, :1271, :1522 — all five sites including the two kgaa added.
  Issue: kgaa's acceptance requires open to coarse-refuse an exhausted event budget before any existence-sensitive lookup. With eventsRecorded pinned to 0, service.ts's `usage.eventsRecorded >= eventBudget` can never be true, so event_budget_exhausted is unreachable from every mounted route and a plant for it can only false-green. This bead was closed as "independently accepted" with this clause unsatisfiable.
  Root cause confirmed at schema level: root's correction (4) is exactly right. events (0001_krater_v0.sql:33-44) has no fellow_id or credential_id, and 0004_krater_integrity_v1.sql adds only row_digest/chain_digest. There is no column from which a grant-wide per-Fellow usage count could be derived, so this cannot be fixed in the router alone.
  Fix: either (i) add fellow_id/credential_id attribution to events plus a same-transaction counter read, or (ii) explicitly revise the acceptance to a non-consuming boundary and record that event_budget_exhausted is deliberately unreachable until W3.7 lands attribution. Option (ii) is the smaller honest move and should be a written decision, not silence.

EXACT TEST MATRIX FOR THE REMAINING WORK.
  A1 suspicious-review open refused: 403 WRITE_REFUSED, byte-identical to A2, and exactly one operator_review_holds row written.
  A2 wrong-problem-binding open refused: same 403 bytes as A1 (the oracle test — refusal must not distinguish binding from quarantine), and ZERO hold rows, because binding failure is not an operator-review condition. This pair is the load-bearing one: it proves the hold is written for the right reason and the face still reveals nothing.
  A3 allowed open: 201, non-vacuity control, zero hold rows, contributor membership created atomically.
  A4 hold atomicity: force the batch to fail after the hold insert; assert neither hold nor session exists (same-transaction proof, not two writes).
  A5 replay after quarantine: a successful pre-quarantine open replays exactly after the Fellow enters suspicious_review — proves Finding A did not move replay behind policy.
  A6 suspicious-review close: 403, session still open, one hold row; then allowed close and its exact replay as controls.
  B1 (only if option (i)) budget exhaustion refuses open before the problems SELECT, with a DB stub that throws on contact so reaching the lookup is a hard failure rather than an assertion.
  B2 (if option (ii)) an arithmetic/source assertion that event_budget_exhausted has no reachable route, so the dead reason is pinned as deliberate and cannot be quietly resurrected as a false-green plant.
  Ordering guards: source assertions that in both handlers the authorize call index precedes the first SELECT index, mirroring the existing promote guard.

MINIMAL RESERVATION SET.
  Exclusive: apps/wire/src/sessions/router.ts; apps/wire/src/enrollment/service.ts; apps/wire/test/unit/session-routes.test.ts; db/migrations/0021_operator_review_holds.sql (new file, so reserve the path).
  Not required: packages/contracts/src/sessions.ts — the hold is internal and must not gain a public face; adding one would contradict root's correction (2).
  CONFLICTS. router.ts and session-routes.test.ts are the hottest files in this repo and are currently implicated in e7j.2 (sponsor workshop pagination, same file), p9h1 (pack ownership/membership gates, same file), and the 9p4 lane. 0021 is the next free migration number and nothing else claims it, but a concurrent lane taking 0021 first is the likeliest collision — the implementer should re-check `ls db/migrations | tail` immediately before creating it. Sequencing: land Finding A before any e7j.2 pagination work touches router.ts, because both edit call-site regions and A is the smaller diff.

BOUNDARY. Nothing executed: no runtime, type, lint or UBS gate ran, so every claim above is read from source at the frozen hashes. This is a source-level packet, not deployed evidence. kgaa remains CLOSED — I changed no status, and whether Findings A and B warrant reopening kgaa or a fresh child bead is the coordinator's call, not mine. Not staged, not committed.

title: W2.7 R2 CAS: artifacts pipeline
description:
WHY: Bodies and artifacts are content-addressed so identical bytes dedupe site-wide, caches are immutable and public exports reference verified content without repository bloat. R2 zero-egress economics are load-bearing; unsafe MIME/archive handling or digest confusion would turn the evidence surface into a security defect. OWNERSHIP: this bead builds the Krater storage primitive and R2 binding; W6.9 owns the public Fellow HTTP manifest/resume/status ergonomics over it. WHAT: global CAS at sha256 keys; storage functions for presign, single/multipart upload state, completion, server-observed size/digest verification, dedupe and metadata/scan status; allowed text/source/Lean/log types, 5MB general cap and 20MB tar.gz lake cap; immutable direct artifacts-domain serving; attachment disposition for anything not plain-text-safe; no HTML/SVG execution under a site origin; MIME sniffing, archive traversal and decompression bounds; bodies over 1KB may spill with 280-character D1 extract; external large files stay links with expected hashes; token-shaped/PII hooks run before binding. R2 outage leaves bounded text writes possible and upload state pending/degraded. Workshop bodies share CAS exactly as Fable specifies: access/visibility lives on the owning index row and unlisted hashes are explicitly not secrets, so secret-shaped content is refused. TESTS: unit/property tests for keying, dedupe, ranges/state, limits, MIME/archive decisions and metadata transitions; mock-free local/staging R2 tests for single/multipart, concurrent same-hash writers, resume, interruption, mismatch, corrupt/truncated object, expiry, outage/recovery, inventory orphan/missing, immutable headers and safe disposition; malicious MIME/traversal/bomb and secret/privacy canaries must fail. OPS.2a logs manifest/artifact digests, size/range/state, request IDs and timing—not presigned URLs/query strings, bodies/extracts, credentials or workshop refs. DONE: storage API is idempotent and consumed by W6.9; real-binding tests pass; inventory/reconciliation detects every seeded divergence; no unverified/quarantined object can bind as disposition-moving evidence.

REFERENCE-AWARE PRIVATE RETENTION: CAS deduplication never makes an index-row deletion sufficient. Maintain transactional artifact/body bindings by visibility and retention class. Removing a never-published private/workshop binding triggers a guarded GC eligibility computation: delete the physical object only when no public, licensed, private, backup-restoration, quarantine or legal-hold reference remains; otherwise remove the private association while preserving the shared bytes required by another lawful reference. A hash that is already public is not made private by a duplicate workshop upload, and the deletion response explains that identical public bytes remain public without revealing another private owner. GC is delayed, idempotent, inventory-reconciled and audit logged; orphan detection never blindly deletes. R2 outage queues eligible cleanup without reviving access.

PRIVATE/PUBLIC PUBLICATION BOUNDARY: global CAS means one canonical SHA-256 identity and reference graph, not one anonymously readable bucket. Use separate private and public delivery namespaces or buckets per environment. artifacts.asimposium.org is bound only to the public namespace; private-only and workshop bytes are fetched through an authenticated, non-shared-cache a. Worker path after index authorization. Publication records a pending-publication binding, then an idempotent outbox step copies and re-verifies the digest into the public namespace before any stable artifact URL is returned; faces expose an honest pending/degraded state, and pending or failed publication cannot advance evidence standing. This narrow physical duplication is accepted when one digest crosses visibility classes. An already-public digest remains public, but merely knowing a private digest never bypasses authorization. Dedupe timing, status, metadata and error shapes must not reveal another sponsor private binding. Direct R2 custom-domain serving remains immutable and cheap for published objects only.

RIGHTS-AWARE BINDINGS: each artifact/body binding stores the server-derived immutable license-policy/content-class snapshot and provenance state owned by W1.2/W6.9. Physical CAS identity/deduplication never merges or upgrades legal/visibility bindings: the same digest may have separate lawful private and public associations, and a public-namespace copy occurs only after the target binding rights gate succeeds. Retrieval/export metadata comes from the binding, not object MIME/key or another sponsor association.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover SHA-256 keying/dedupe, state/range transitions, single/multipart resume, observed size/MIME/digest, caps/archive safety, scan/quarantine, visibility bindings, shared public/private hashes, reference/hold accounting, delayed GC eligibility and outage decisions. Mock-free R2/D1 tests race same-hash writers/completers/deleters, interrupt uploads/GC, corrupt/truncate scratch objects, expire presigns, inject scan/R2 failure and reconcile missing/orphan inventory; no bound, held or public object may be deleted and no unverified object may bind. scripts/e2e-cas.sh exercises storage through scratch bindings, including shared public/private body deletion, last-private-reference GC, legal hold, immutable range retrieval, malicious files, authorization, outage/recovery and inventory repair. OPS.2a records synthetic manifest/artifact/binding IDs, declared/observed digests, sizes/ranges/state, reference counts/classes, hold/GC decision code, request ID and timing; never bodies/extracts, presigned queries, private owner refs, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, scanner patterns, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

The E2E matrix must attempt direct artifacts-host access to a private-only digest, authenticated and unauthenticated private retrieval, copy-on-publication interruption/retry, pending-face behavior, failed D1 commit versus public-copy orphan reconciliation, public/private same-digest races, and cross-sponsor existence-oracle probes. No private-only byte or binding metadata is anonymously serviceable; a public URL appears only after verified publication.

CAS tests reuse one digest across differing private/public/license bindings, reject rights-state borrowing and retroactive mutation, preserve historical snapshots through copy/GC/restore, and verify direct public metadata belongs to the authorized published binding without exposing another association.

title: CAS runtime inputs can change after validation
description: casKeyForHash and casUrlForHash let RegExp.test coerce a runtime value and then interpolate that value again, so a stateful Symbol.toPrimitive can pass lowercase-digest validation but emit a different R2 key or URL. decideArtifactAdmission reads the optional body twice, so an accessor can present secret-shaped bytes on the first read and clean bytes on the second. gcEligibility validates remainingClasses in one pass but constructs its Set in a second pass, so an accessor-backed class can validate as public and then change to an unknown value that is filtered into a collectible set. reconcileArtifactInventory likewise validates accessor-backed digest/state properties and then re-reads different values into aggregation. These pure helpers are currently imported only by their unit test, but the boundary is fail-open before W2.7 wiring.
acceptance_criteria: Require an exact primitive lowercase 64-hex digest before key or URL construction. Snapshot optional body, every GC class, and each inventory row digest/state exactly once before validation/use. Add causal stateful-coercion and getter plants proving the emitted key/URL, secret decision, GC preservation, and inventory report use only the validated snapshot. Preserve deterministic reports, exact reference-preserving GC, and nonreflection. Run focused CAS test, Wire typecheck/lint, and scoped UBS only at fresh 1m load below 10. No mounted R2/D1/deployed claim.
close_reason: Runtime input snapshot/coercion defect is causally covered; focused CAS tests, exact Biome/diff and scoped UBS are green. Package-wide reds are unrelated and remain open.

title: W3.4 Proposal, approval card, flow-handle polling, token issuance
description:
WHY: Explicit sponsor approval is the theft defense: a stolen join URL yields a visible attacker-authored proposal the sponsor can deny; visiting a page or knowing a public enrollment/proposal ID never authorizes. Polling uses a separate high-entropy flow handle so the public ID is not an oracle. WHAT: POST /v1/fellows consumes the one-time fragment secret into a pending proposal containing name, declared model/harness/effort, requested scopes/budgets and optional key fingerprint. The sponsor console receives a live approval card with Approve, Reduce scopes/budgets, or Deny as explicit CSRF-protected, account-bound, recent-auth actions. The claim response returns a high-entropy flow handle; RFC-8628-style polling sends it in the POST body and returns authorization_pending, slow_down, expired, denied, or the one credential outcome—never accepts the bare proposal ID and never puts handles in URLs/logs. Proposal expiry is 24 hours independent of the 30-minute start-secret TTL. Approval mints the token once, stores only its hash, returns hello_url/suggested_next, and creates any problem membership plus first directive transactionally. Denial consumes the proposal without leaking sponsor identity or reason beyond safe status. TESTS: unit tables for state transitions, scope reduction, TTLs, polling intervals and response shapes; mock-free D1 race matrix for simultaneous exchange, expiry-versus-approval, approval refresh/double-POST, deny-versus-approve, fast poll, token-response disconnect/retry, and membership/directive rollback; API/Playwright E2E covers honest approval, reduced scopes, denial, stolen URL attacker proposal, wrong sponsor, bare-ID polling, flow-handle replay, CSRF and step-up. Exactly one credential outcome and exactly one approval event may commit; membership and first-directive state add no extra event. DIAGNOSTICS: OPS.2a structured steps use enrollment/proposal/flow digests and request/event IDs, state, status/code, timing and retry only; canary tests prove fragment, flow handle, token, cookie, proposal body, key fingerprint and sponsor email are absent from logs/traces. DONE: all flows are actionable for agent and sponsor, denial is safe, race/negative matrices pass, and approval-card hooks plus correlation IDs are ready for W8.

ONE-CREDENTIAL DELIVERY RECOVERY: approval commits exactly one token and the credential table stores only its hash. The response is shown once; first authenticated use marks possession. If transport becomes ambiguous before possession is established, the same body-only flow returns a non-secret committed-but-delivery-unknown receipt and CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN. It never replays, reconstructs or replaces the bearer automatically. Recovery is an explicit recent-auth sponsor action that revokes the unknown credential and approves a freshly bound credential, respecting max-three-token, scope/grant and account-posture checks. The approval card and agent response explain this rare boundary without showing token material to the sponsor. Backups, exports, observability and test artifacts contain only hashes/non-secret receipts.

ONE LOGICAL APPROVAL EVENT: Approve or Reduce is one accepted logical write. Token issuance, membership and first-directive rows are atomic state/projection effects referenced by exactly one immutable approval event; they do not each append their own event and no approval wrapper is added. Deny and explicit recovery/rebind are separate logical commands and each has exactly one event. The event freezes acting sponsor account plus accountable human and the resulting Fellow attribution without exposing proposal or credential bytes.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/state tests exhaust proposal, Approve/Reduce/Deny, TTL, polling, interval/slow_down, scope and membership/directive outcomes plus hash-only issuance, first-use delivery acknowledgement, ambiguous response and explicit sponsor-approved revoke/rebind. Mock-free D1 races simultaneous exchange, approval/deny/expiry, double POST, token-response disconnect, Worker restart, first use versus revocation/rebind and membership rollback; exactly one credential outcome and exactly one approval event commit; membership and first-directive state add no extra event. scripts/e2e-enrollment-approval.sh covers honest, reduced, denied, stolen-path, wrong-sponsor, bare-ID, replay, CSRF, step-up, disconnect-before/after-mint, successful first use and recovery from delivery-unknown without automatic remint. OPS.2a logs only synthetic IDs/digests, state, status/code, request/event IDs, timing and retry; database/export/backup/log scans prove absence of fragment, flow handle, credential bytes, cookie, proposal body, key fingerprint, sponsor email, transcript and hidden reasoning.

Race and E2E assertions count exactly one event for each approval/deny/rebind command and prove membership/directive side effects do not create extra events or survive without their causal approval event.

title: W5: Ledger objects + validator
description: WHY: The typed object model and computed state machine are the epistemic core: dispositions are OUTPUTS of evidence+review events, never author-writable (ADR-9); labels cannot mint truth. This epic encodes the whole quality stance: falsifiers mandatory, refuter-first display (open-unchallenged until a refutation attempt exists), weakest-link ceilings, versions pinned, negative knowledge preserved. WHAT: problems (private-draft default for fellow-created, sharpening gate via non-proposer statement-clear review, active/dormant/under-result-review/resolved-with-direction, unlisted, famous-problem guardrail requiring external-expert review before any resolution language); governance (transferable stewards, admission modes, merge/fork preserving IDs+cursors; no role moves a disposition by fiat — ADR-22); claims (12 kinds, versioning, NFKC norm-hash duplicate refusal at promote per ADR-15, statement binding + drift flags); disposition machine (open/malformed/disputed/corroborated/strongly-supported/refuted/reduced-to/withdrawn/superseded + review-state and staleness facets; machine-checked is a display BADGE for strongly-supported-via-certified-artifact, never a status — ADR-10); typed reviewable relations + proof gaps + normalized conflicts (ADR-21); hypotheses w/ discriminating_predictions; evidence (5 computed classes assertion<heuristic<citation<computation<certified, P5 detection-floor coercion, P8 cite-or-memory, selection disclosure, exploratory/confirmatory, formalization-friction kind w/ blocker classes + witness seeds); reviews (T0-T3 independence tiers, per-domain rubrics, capable-of-failure field, novelty review); dead ends w/ structured retry_when triggers; syntheses (frozen cursor, P13 ledger anchoring, draft-until-published). DONE WHEN: children close; state-machine fixture table green.
acceptance_criteria: Every ontology/state computation has exhaustive unit/table/property tests for legal and illegal transitions, version pinning/drift, DAG/ceiling, computed tiers/classes/coercions/facets, governance permissions and P1-P13-relevant outcomes. Golden controls include polished-but-wrong and valid-odd cases so validators prove both failure and acceptance. Mock-free D1 integration exercises common write/event/projection/rebuild paths and cross-object triggers. scripts/e2e-ledger.sh builds a problem from private draft through sharpening, claims/hypotheses/evidence/reviews/gaps/conflicts/dead ends/citations/synthesis/question/retraction, verifies exact status panels/agent faces and attempts every prohibited author/steward/operator shortcut. OPS.2a logs object/version/event IDs, rule/error and digests—not scientific/private bodies. No test or metadata may assert a disposition directly.

title: W12.4 Legal, naming, retention, and processor-policy integration
description: WHY: Legal and rights posture is a launch gate but contains four independently owned streams: name clearance, economic posture, contribution/retention terms, and an implementation-grounded processor audit. This bead is the integration and operator-acceptance gate. WHAT: reconcile W12.4a naming decision, W12.4b free/donation decision, W12.4c reviewed ToS/licensing/retention/takedown text, and W12.4d processor/behavior audit with the served policy documents, signup/publication UX, W2 retention/redaction machinery, W3 account lifecycle, W8 human pages, and operator runbooks. Any legal text that cannot be implemented is corrected before launch; any implementation not disclosed is added before launch. The operator—not an agent—accepts residual legal/naming risk. DONE: all four children close; exact versioned documents and registry are live; signup/publish flows require the intended acknowledgment; retention/takedown/account-deletion drills match the public claims; counsel/operator signoff and residual-risk record are dated at the launch revision.
acceptance_criteria: All four child decisions close with dated evidence, applicable counsel/operator review, and no unresolved behavior-versus-policy discrepancy. Static/unit checks map each served policy claim to code/config/processor/retention owner and fail missing version, acknowledgment, license or disclosure. Playwright plus scripts/e2e-legal-policy.sh uses synthetic accounts/content to accept/decline signup and publication terms, export/delete never-published private data, retain immutable public history, submit takedown/appeal, exercise retention and processor canaries, and compare served policy versions across faces. A structured gate report records revision, document/config/registry digests, scenario/result, reviewer/signoff, discrepancies and residual risks; never personal data, credentials, cookies, tokens, privileged counsel communications, private bodies, or unsupported legal conclusions.

title: W7.2 Durable Object rooms: hibernating WebSockets + SSE fallback
description: WHY: Sponsors deserve a live workshop view and problem watchers a live page, but idle connections must be approximately free and liveness can never become a second truth source. WebSocket hibernation provides the preferred path; SSE is a bounded fallback; cursor polling remains the recovery path. WHAT: implement a Durable Object room per active public problem and per watched workshop. The D1 write transaction commits an outbox notification carrying only scope/cursor/event references; a post-commit notifier wakes the room, and the room also reconciles from its durable last-delivered cursor against the event/workshop projection so a crash between commit and notify cannot create a silent gap. Notifications are hints: clients fetch canonical rendered deltas. Use hibernatable WebSockets where supported; SSE fallback has idle timeout and drops to polling; rooms evict on dormancy and reconnect resumes from client cursor. Workshop room authorization is rechecked on connect and privilege/revocation changes; public and workshop channels/cursors cannot cross. Payloads are bounded {seq, kind, summary, refs}, with untrusted bodies omitted. Duplicate notifications are harmless, ordering follows canonical seq, and projection/log disagreement surfaces staleness rather than fabricating activity. TESTS: unit tests for cursor reconciliation, duplicate/out-of-order delivery, eviction and authorization; mock-free DO/D1 integration injects crash before notify, after notify, during reconnect, outbox replay, room restart, revocation, and public/workshop cross-wire attempts; scripts/e2e-herald.sh proves WebSocket, SSE, and polling produce the same ordered event IDs, early reconnect catches every committed event exactly once at the UI, workshop updates remain sponsor-only, and killing all rooms degrades visibly without losing data. Verify hibernation billing behavior and bounded SSE duration. DIAGNOSTICS: OPS.2a logs room/scope synthetic IDs, source/delivered cursor, request/event IDs, transport, reconnect/reconcile reason, lag, duration and retry, never cookies, tokens, directive/workshop bodies, or raw event content. DONE: no phantom or lost canonical event across the fault matrix; hibernation measured; rooms remain disposable because cursor reconciliation always restores truth.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/state-machine tests cover cursor reconciliation, duplicate/out-of-order hints, reconnect, eviction, authorization recheck, payload bounds and transport fallback. Mock-free DO/D1 integration injects crash before notify, after notify and during reconnect; outbox replay; room restart; privilege revocation; projection staleness; and public/workshop cross-wire attempts. scripts/e2e-herald.sh proves WebSocket, SSE and polling converge on the same ordered canonical event IDs, reconnect catches every commit without duplicate UI truth, workshop events remain sponsor-only, and killing all rooms visibly degrades to cursor recovery with no loss. Hibernation and bounded-SSE behavior are measured. OPS.2a JSONL records synthetic room/scope IDs, source/delivered cursors, request/event IDs, transport, reconciliation reason, lag, retry and duration, never cookies, tokens, bodies or raw event content.

title: W8.3a Sponsor commentary lane: contract, Worker write, and fenced projections
description:
WHY: Sponsors are allowed exactly two steering surfaces: private directives to their own Fellows and a public commentary lane. Commentary was previously buried inside the problem-page UI bead, which risks an ad hoc server action, incomplete attribution, weak screening, or accidental interleaving with scientific objects. OWNERSHIP: this bead owns the commentary contract, the Worker-only append path, authorization/screening, persistence/projection, and canonical fenced agent representation; W8.3 owns the human composer and page section. WHAT: add a packages/contracts sponsor-commentary schema with problem, bounded original-text body, optional typed relates_to references, sponsor attribution, timestamp and version/content-control state. Public corrections/supersession and lawful tombstones preserve the immutable event envelope and attribution; no silent edit/delete. Commentary remains a visually and semantically separate lane, never enters scientific Now/materiality/moves/calibration/search ranking or claim counts, and is absent from default agent faces/packs. Default scientific digests, packs, feeds, search, moves, Now and counts omit the commentary body and cannot derive actions from it. The explicit commentary agent face and complete public export include the fenced untrusted body with sponsor provenance and lane=commentary; filtered tails still emit page_end/next_cursor correctly. title: W10.5 Property-based test suite (invariant shapes)
description:
WHY: Fixtures pin known cases; property-based tests pin the invariant SHAPES that enumeration cannot cover. The surfaces chosen are exactly the ones whose failure would corrupt the record silently rather than loudly. WHAT: property suites over: (1) public ID round-trips — short code (C-12), slug, and ULID accepted interchangeably on every public route; problem-local references NEVER accepted by a global endpoint without the enclosing problem; (2) event-sequence monotonicity under concurrency — per-scope seq allocated via UPDATE ... SET public_seq = public_seq + 1 ... RETURNING inside the same transaction as the insert, no application-level counters, no gaps or duplicates in the committed log under concurrent writers (lock-wait instrumented; range allocation is the documented escalation if a hot problem proves it); (3) illegal state-machine transitions rejected — disposition machine (draft/open/malformed/disputed/corroborated/strongly-supported/refuted/reduced-to/withdrawn/superseded + statement-drift flag), hypothesis machine (active/narrowed/killed/deferred/superseded; kill requires killed_by), fellow lifecycle (pending/active/paused/revoked/archived/compromised); (4) idempotency-key semantics — same key + same request digest replays the ORIGINAL result; same key + different digest is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; never a silent second write; 24h retention window honored; (5) pagination stability under concurrent inserts (cursor pages never skip or duplicate events); (6) arbitrary-Unicode markdown safety through the one render pipeline (no XSS, no crash, no raw HTML, control-marker neutralization of forged asimp headers/system-item delimiters holds for adversarial inputs). DONE: suites in CI with logged seeds for reproducible failures; every shrunk counterexample is archived as a permanent named fixture.

IDEMPOTENCY/REVISION BOUNDARY CASES: ordinary writes replay the original nonsecret result for 24 hours; one-time credential exchanges preserve only hash plus nonsecret receipt and surface CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN rather than replay/remint after response loss. A queued write whose outcome cannot be reconciled after the retention window becomes unknown_commit and must not be assigned a new key, retried blindly, reported successful, or discarded. Workshop generators cover create/revise base-version CAS, promote of an immutable revision, edit-versus-promote races, sponsor acting-principal versus Fellow content-author attribution, and the rule that a content edit creates a new logical write/idempotency key while transport retry preserves the old key.

PUBLIC REVISION GENERATORS: generate create/revise target/base_version histories for every eligible public kind, concurrent writers, direct versus promoted commands, sponsor actor versus Fellow author, stale/unauthorized/non-revisable attempts and revisions that newly violate domain invariants. The property is either one new version plus one event with old references stable, or OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT/other refusal with byte-identical pre-state—never last-writer-wins or a historical link that floats to head.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Each invariant has a named generator, shrinker, deterministic seed replay, minimum case count, and regression fixture path; suites run against real D1 transaction semantics where persistence matters. Failures emit OPS.2a-compatible JSONL and JUnit with suite/property/seed, generator version, shrunk input digest, event/cursor range, expected/actual invariant, timing, and assertion diff; never generated bodies that resemble secrets, private content, credentials, cookies, tokens, or raw SQL values. Every discovered counterexample receives a focused unit regression and, when user-observable, a named E2E scenario in the owning journey bead before closure. Idempotency generators include boundary clocks, response loss, one-time hash-only outcomes, first-use/rebind, and greater-than-24h unknown_commit; workshop generators include revision CAS, immutable-version promotion and attribution. Permanent regressions assert no token replay/remint, no blind new-key retry after ambiguity, and no publication of a workshop version different from the one validated.

Shrunk revision counterexamples become owning-domain fixtures; permanent regressions cover no silent overwrite, exact event count, old-version readability, pinned-review stability and direct/promotion parity.

title: W7: Herald liveness
description: WHY: Liveness must be cheap (doctrine A7) and match each audience: agents are request/response creatures (poll with cursors), anonymous lurkers must cost near-zero (a tweeted page brings 10K pollers), sponsors deserve real-time workshop view. The lurker storm lands on a one-integer Worker endpoint, never Vercel, never D1 row reads. WHAT: /cursor endpoint (single integer, edge-cached, sub-50ms at edge); Durable Object rooms per active problem and watched workshop, fed transactionally by the write path — WebSockets with hibernation API where supported (idle approx free), plain SSE fallback with idle timeouts that drop to polling (SSE holds the DO active, so it cannot be the default); optional 25s long-poll on events (wait=25); cache purge by surrogate key on write; rooms evict on dormancy. DONE WHEN: children close; DO spend at simulated load matches cost model; polling fallback proven by killing rooms mid-session.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover cache keys/purge maps, cursor reconciliation, transport state, authorization and rate accounting. Mock-free DO/D1/edge integration injects commit-notify gaps, duplicates, ordering, restart, eviction, revocation and cache staleness. scripts/e2e-herald-integration.sh composes the W7.2 transport proof with public cursor, event tail, long-poll, cache purge and workshop watcher journeys; WebSocket, SSE, long-poll and ordinary polling must converge on the same canonical ordered IDs, and killing rooms must degrade to polling without loss. Viral /cursor load proves D1/Vercel avoidance and sub-50ms edge target; paired principals prove workshop traffic never affects public cursor/cache or crosses sponsors. OPS.2a records transport/cursors/lag/request-event IDs/timing and assertion diffs, never credentials, cookies, tokens, bodies, private refs, transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

title: W8: Agora human UI
description: WHY: The human plane makes the ledger watchable, steerable, shareable — without ever pretending (doctrine A4) or letting humans instruct agents through public content (A2: commentary lane + directives only). Presentation commitments: light-first paper-like scientific-instrument aesthetic, WCAG 2.2 AA, core public content readable without JavaScript, status never color-only, KaTeX trust off. WHAT: app shell + design system; front page (Now strip of material events only, problems-needing-help chips, no engagement ranking), explore/areas, /results honors record (chronological, event-ordered, never actor-aggregated, reviewers credited, DAG context per entry — ADR-19); problem page (tabs, claims board with ceilings+weakest-link, single-team banner, History tab with statement lineage + tombstones + checkpoints); claim page with the two Diptych-honesty panels (Why this status? What remains unverified?); sponsor console (fellows, token hygiene, onboarding dialog with harness-aware paste blocks + live approval card); workshop view (Promote/Keep/Discard where the human can promote FOR a stalled agent through the same validator); director grammar UI (closed verb set assign/focus/forbid/unfocus/pause/resume/revoke/transfer/publish/hide/cap; strongly-supported promotions require the no-undisclosed-directive attestation); OG share images carrying EXACT status (share honesty is hard rule — never resolution language for unresolved work); /reviews global queue; thin admin. DONE WHEN: children close; paired-user cache-leak test green; a11y audit has no blockers.
acceptance_criteria: Component/unit tests cover status/copy/permission/action mappings, metadata, share text, keyboard/focus and render fallbacks. No-JS, axe/WCAG, CSP/XSS and structured-data suites include should-fail fixtures. Mock-free Playwright covers the one-sentence human journey plus proposal publication, token/account recovery, workshop live/fallback/promote, directives, search, follows, reports/appeals/admin, quiet review/honors and honest sharing. Paired-user/cache tests prove workshop/private/unlisted/moderation detail absent from every unauthorized response, cache, metadata, search and artifact. OPS.2a browser artifacts are synthetic, redacted before persistence and contain no credentials/private bodies/raw harness transcripts. HTML never becomes a second semantic source.

title: W10.9 Error-copy audit, refusal voice, ceremony regression metric
description: WHY: Errors are the agent UX at its worst moment. Contract errors must teach maximally; policy refusals must starve the oracle; and R-22 (schema ceremony) warns that required fields and workflows heavy enough that agents abandon or game them is a real failure mode — Rule A10 applies to the contracts themselves. WHAT: audit every code in the ~37-entry error dictionary (PAIRING_INVALID ... NOT_FOUND) for: RFC 7807 shape + code + rule citation + fix_hint + schema URL + filled example + next_actions on every CONTRACT error; colleague-voice copy throughout ("this looks like a claim; claims get the dignity of the ledger — here is the prefilled schema" beats "rejected: wrong type"; refusals read like a colleague upholding shared standards, never a bouncer); POLICY refusals carry ONLY the coarse category + appeal path + (where safe) a reformulation offer — no trigger phrase, no pattern name, no classifier reasoning (ADR-18); recoverable flags accurate per code; 409s carry current version + conflicting event IDs + suggested_action (refetch_and_reapply, review_existing — agents never infer remedies from prose); unknown format/profile returns the allowed list. Slop-scrub pass over all agent-facing strings (Rule A4 applies to the platform's own voice). Ceremony regression: tokens-to-first-valid-post from gauntlet runs tracked as a trend metric; only decision-relevant fields required in schemas; exploratory evidence accepted, labeled, unpromotable. DONE: error-copy review recorded per code; refusal texts snapshot-tested (they are also oracle-probing fixtures); gauntlet token trend wired into CI output.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Golden/table tests cover every error code, contract versus policy class, status/content type, rule, fix_hint, schema/example link, next_actions, colleague voice, localization-safe rendering, and adversarial input non-reflection. Cold-agent scripts/e2e-error-recovery.sh injects representative 400/401/403/404/409/422/429/5xx failures, follows the offered recovery without prior docs, measures recovery turns/tokens, and probes policy-oracle leakage. OPS.2a logs route template, code/class/rule, recovery action ID, harness, attempt/turn/token bucket, outcome, schema/example digest, latency and assertion diff; never rejected bodies, raw prompts/transcripts, policy triggers/scores, credentials, cookies, tokens, or fragments.

title: W8.1 Agora shell + design system
description:
WHY: Presentation commitments are doctrine, not taste: light-first paper-like scientific instrument, real dark mode, WCAG 2.2 AA, status never conveyed by color alone, math as primary content, and all material public content readable without JavaScript. WHAT: Next.js 16 App Router shell and Tailwind tokens; serif science typography and monospaced IDs; KaTeX trust mode off with copyable LaTeX; accessible tabular fallbacks for every graph; reduced motion, semantic landmarks, keyboard navigation; canonical URLs, partitioned sitemaps, robots excluding unlisted/private/auth routes; and structured scholarly metadata only where semantically honest (stable canonical URL, statement version, authorship/provenance, citation/export links—never invented journal credentials or resolved language). RSC renders everything material. SECURITY: strict CSP; Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax host-only cookies rotated on privilege change; CSRF on human POSTs; one markdown pipeline with raw HTML disabled, GFM+math, safe links, and the XSS corpus. DONE: axe/WCAG audit has no blockers; no-JS problem-page smoke test; keyboard and graph-fallback tests; light/dark and reduced-motion snapshots; sitemap/robots/private exclusion tests; structured-data validators prove exact status/version/provenance and reject resolution-shaped metadata for unresolved fixtures; CSP snapshot and a deliberately inline-script fixture fails.

GENERIC DIPTYCH HTML FALLBACK: consume W6.1 public-resource registry and shared HTML-fragment renderer for every public object/version that lacks a specialized Agora page. The generic route preserves the exact canonical status, attribution, version/history, references and agent-face links; specialized problem/claim/Fellow/results pages may enhance presentation but cannot fork semantics. No public resource may exist only as a markdown anchor inside a larger page.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/component and golden tests cover design tokens, light/dark and forced-colors modes, reduced motion, semantic landmarks, keyboard/focus order, status text/icon redundancy, KaTeX trust-off and copyable source, graph/table equivalence, canonical and scholarly metadata, sitemap partitioning, robots exclusions, CSP, CSRF form wiring, cookie attributes/rotation, safe-link protocols, Unicode/math, responsive breakpoints, and the full XSS/forbidden-resolution fixture corpus including deliberately failing controls. scripts/e2e-agora-shell.sh runs Playwright against the real preview with JavaScript enabled and disabled; it traverses anonymous, sponsor and operator shells by keyboard/mobile/desktop, runs axe, validates structured data/sitemaps/robots/CSP, attempts inline-script/raw-HTML/link-protocol injection, toggles themes/reduced motion, and proves private/unlisted/auth routes and cookies do not leak through cache or metadata. OPS.2a browser JSONL records revision, route template, synthetic principal class, viewport/color/motion/JS modes, public projection/render/CSP/metadata digests, accessibility rule/result, status/cache outcome, duration and bounded diff; retained traces/screenshots are synthetic and redacted and never contain cookies, tokens, OAuth data, private bodies, workshop/directive content, browser storage, raw terminal/harness transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

Playwright and no-JS tests iterate the public-resource registry, resolve every human-route key, compare it with canonical agent JSON/GFM, and prove specialized and generic routes preserve stable links across supersession, merge, retraction and tombstone.

comments.text: GAP: the capsule (packages/protocol/assets/capsule.md) tells agents to 'follow only the server-authored next_actions' from hello, but hello's next_actions (apps/wire/src/enrollment/router.ts ~1242) point only to /protocol.md and /skill.md — never to POST /v1/sessions. FIX: add a session-open next_action to the hello response (after the two reads), so the capsule -> hello -> session-open chain is unbroken. BLOCKED ON: the enrollment router is mid-refactor under the zdz.7 P0 (request-body bounding, uncommitted). Land this after that churn settles to avoid collision. comments.author: WildMountain
comments.text: FULLER AUDIT: the gap is not just hello. NO agent-facing document teaches the session-loop API: capsule.md defers to hello's next_actions (which point only to protocol.md + skill.md); skill.md and handbook.md never mention /v1/sessions; protocol.md is the rules (803 words, correctly not an API reference). The ONLY surface listing the session loop is GET /capabilities (agent_writes), and nothing in the onboarding chain points an agent there. So a cold agent following the documented path cannot discover how to open a session. FIX (when the enrollment router settles): hello's next_actions should add the session-open action (or a /capabilities pointer that lists the loop). The gauntlet's cold agents hit exactly this wall. This is the highest-leverage onboarding fix available.

comments.author: WildMountain
comments.text: CORRECTION to the audit: the chain is not broken, only indirect. capsule → hello → next_actions → skill.md, and skill.md line 44 points to /capabilities, which lists the session loop in agent_writes. So a careful cold agent CAN reach the loop: capsule → hello → skill.md → /capabilities → POST /v1/sessions. The gap is DIRECTNESS, not existence — the loop is 3 hops from the capsule, and hello's next_actions (the immediate guidance) stop at the two docs rather than naming the session-open action or the /capabilities index. RECOMMENDATION (unchanged, lower severity): hello's next_actions should name the session-open action directly, so the first guided step after the reads is the loop entry, not a doc that points to a doc. Downgrade from 'broken' to 'indirect'.

title: W7.4 Cache discipline verification
description: WHY: caching bugs here are privacy bugs (workshop bytes on a public face) or honesty bugs (stale status without a warning) — the discipline needs its own verification net, not incidental coverage. WHAT: verify ETag/If-None-Match on every public GET; anonymous GETs edge-cached, authed packs never shared-cached (private semantics); staleness always visibly timestamped when served stale; surrogate-key purge coverage map (which writes purge which faces); the paired-user cache-leak test harness (two users + an unlisted problem + a workshop: private material provably never lands in any shared cache) — this harness is reused by W10. DONE: coverage map documented; leak harness green in CI; stale-with-warning fixture.
acceptance_criteria: The cache coverage map is executable: every public GET/write pair has expected key/Vary/ETag/purge/stale behavior and paired principals. Unit/integration and Playwright tests cover 304, projection-stale warning, unlisted/workshop/auth fragments, logout/revocation and edge error. OPS.2a logs route/cache-key digest, principal class, ETag/projection version, hit/age/purge/stale reason, request/event IDs and timing; never bodies, cookies, identities or private refs. scripts/e2e-cache-discipline.sh runs the full paired-principal matrix against staging edge caches, injects stale projections and seeded leakage/missing-Vary controls, and emits a redacted correlated JSONL report; every seeded control must fail before the bead may close.

title: W9.6 Review matchmaking + queue
description: WHY: reviews are the scarce resource; the queue must rank by scientific consequence and MISSING INDEPENDENCE TYPE (what tier the claim still lacks), and requests must reach eligible reviewers (non-author, tier-advancing) — never reward volume. WHAT: review-request creation (author-initiated + Symposiarch-suggested); eligibility computation (not author; sponsor/model-family diversity vs existing reviews — what tier would this reviewer ADD); queue ranking: consequence (DAG position, dependents), readiness, missing independence type, age, sponsor diversity; declinable requests land in inboxes; review-queue pack profile feeds from here; claim-creation responses report queue position + median time-to-first-review (feedback-latency legibility). Real projection tests replay to identical queues. scripts/e2e-review-matchmaking.sh creates multi-sponsor claims and reviewers, requests review packs, accepts/declines/expires assignments, removes conflicts, and verifies W8.8b plus hello/triage consume the same order. title: W12.7 DNS cutover (ADR-2), apex static copies + 308s, Vercel plan decision
description: WHY: ADR-2 (revised): the apex MUST be DNS-only to Vercel — Auth.js needs to be the terminating platform, and Vercel-behind-orange-cloud breaks in well-documented ways; meanwhile agents are taught exactly ONE origin (a.asimposium.org) by every document that reaches them, so the redirect and static-copy machinery is part of the agent contract, not cosmetics. WHAT: production cutover: asimposium.org DNS-only -> Vercel; a.asimposium.org proxied -> Worker; artifacts.asimposium.org proxied -> R2 custom domain (Cache-Control: immutable, no Worker invocation on the blob path). Apex serves humans plus BUILD-TIME static copies of AGENTS.md / llms.txt / skill.md generated from packages/protocol and the W11.5 canonical /install.sh release asset, with a CI drift-check diffing them against the Worker live copies; apex 308-redirects all .md content paths to a.; /install.sh stays on the apex and is never caught by the markdown redirect. Redirect matrix e2e-tested (every documented path lands where the docs say). vercel.json: disable git auto-deploys once the real app lands (the placeholder phase keeps them on). Decide the Vercel plan (R-9: non-commercial site on Hobby; Pro at $20 is the PRE-DECIDED answer the day ToS friction or traffic warrants it — decide, record, move on). WAF/edge rules follow staging discipline (log in production, inspect, then enforce) and NEVER place a browser challenge in front of a. title: S-1 Capsule + pairing spike
description: WHY: The single biggest product risk is that real harnesses cannot complete onboarding unaided; everything else is moot if the front door fails. This also retires ADR-20 enrollment security as running code without violating Rule A11. WHAT: build the thin G0 Worker slice for minting an enrollment (public ID plus 256-bit one-time secret, SHA-256 at rest, 30-minute TTL, single-use); fragment-secret join URL that never enters request paths/referrers; content-negotiated capsule (markdown default, JSON on Accept, tiny human HTML); POST /v1/fellows burns the secret into a pending proposal; live approval card; RFC-8628-style flow-handle polling with the high-entropy handle in the body, never query string; one-time token mint after explicit sponsor approval. title: W3.8 Sponsor/Fellow lifecycle: bilateral transfer, export, deletion, orphan prevention
description:
WHY: The plan requires that a Fellow always have one living accountable sponsor, cannot transfer itself, and moves only after both humans confirm. Today the transfer UI, token revocation, workshop privacy, retention, and legal promises have no single backend owner, which creates the worst possible seam: an apparently successful handoff that leaves old credentials or private access alive. OWNERSHIP: this bead owns the Worker contracts and transactional state machines for Fellow sponsorship transfer and sponsor account export/deletion. W8.5 and W8.7 own console and director-grammar presentation; W2.8 owns reusable export/retention primitives; W12.4 owns reviewed policy language. WHAT — TRANSFER: an outgoing sponsor initiates a bounded-TTL request through the signed service envelope after recent-auth step-up; the receiving Google-authenticated human separately step-ups and accepts the exact immutable request. The acceptance card shows Fellow identity and immutable model/harness declaration, memberships, moderation/account posture, sponsor-cap effect, which private workshop access moves, which historical directive bodies do not, credential rotation, and the public-attribution rule. Until acceptance, authority and visibility do not change; the outgoing sponsor may cancel; expiry, recipient refusal, capacity failure, suspension, deletion, or any material request change leaves the original binding intact. A Fellow, bearer token, operator shortcut, or mere link visit can never initiate or accept. Atomic activation rebinds exactly once, preserves every historical event and sponsor-at-event attribution, applies the new sponsor only to future writes, removes the former sponsor from live workshop/control access, grants the receiving sponsor the disclosed access, revokes every pre-transfer credential before the next write, pauses the Fellow, and creates a body-only recovery/rebind flow so the new sponsor must approve a fresh credential. Existing directive bodies remain visible to their authoring sponsor and the Fellow but are not disclosed to the recipient; public received-a-directive markers remain. WHAT — EXPORT/DELETION: an authenticated export returns a versioned manifest of the human account, Fellow lifecycle records, entitled private data, public object references, and retention classes without exporting live secrets. Account deletion first presents an exact impact preview and transfer alternative, then requires step-up plus explicit confirmation. Commit cancels pending enrollments/transfers, revokes every Fellow and token atomically, tombstones retired handles and Fellow bylines without recycling them, invokes W2.8 deletion for never-published private drafts and personal data subject to documented legal holds, and preserves licensed public event envelopes/content with stable citations. No Fellow can be orphaned and no public object silently disappears. Contract errors teach; policy/account-suspension refusals remain coarse. DONE: backend ownership is unambiguous, transfer and deletion are replay-safe, every visibility/credential transition is atomic, and UI/legal consumers can rely on one versioned contract.

RESTORE/ERASURE CONSEQUENCES: deletion preview and receipt name the ordinary service-state deletion, encrypted-backup residual window, legal holds, physical-erasure deadline, and shared-CAS case where identical already-public bytes remain while private association is removed. The delete transaction emits the W2.8 signed retention-control record atomically enough to reconcile any crash; no success is shown until durable control exists. A restored snapshot must apply this record before serviceability, so removed sponsors, revoked credentials, cancelled flows, personal data and never-published drafts cannot reappear.

DIRECTIVE-DISCLOSURE HANDOFF: the immutable transfer manifest records which open authored objects/sessions have pre-transfer received-directive markers and their disclosure-attestation state, never directive bodies. The receiving sponsor cannot attest about directives they are forbidden to read. Before transfer, the outgoing sponsor may attest no material undisclosed influence or publish the required scoped disclosure through the W8.7 path; otherwise those pre-transfer objects carry directive_disclosure_unresolved. Transfer and ordinary work still proceed, but strongly-supported or under-result-review gates for affected work fail closed until the prior accountable sponsor resolves the disclosure or a documented operator/legal process records why it cannot be resolved. Work demonstrably begun after the transfer uses only the new sponsor attestation. No one infers harmlessness from silence or transfer.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property state-machine tests cover initiation/manifest/dual-step-up/accept-refuse-cancel-expire, capacity/suspension, sponsor-at-event attribution, workshop/directive visibility, credential rotation/rebind, export classes, deletion preview, signed retention-control creation, backup residual window, legal holds, shared public CAS, tombstones and forbidden self/bearer/operator paths. Mock-free D1/R2/Worker faults race accept with cancel/expiry/revoke/delete/in-flight writes, disconnect around commit, replay keys, and restore a pre-deletion snapshot through W2.8; old credentials/access/private bytes must fail before any post-transfer write or restored service is observable. Playwright plus scripts/e2e-identity-lifecycle.sh uses two sponsors and one Fellow to transfer/reject/expire/recover/export/delete, checks old/new access, directive privacy, public-history immutability, backup/deletion copy, shared-hash behavior and exactly-once audit/control records. OPS.2a logs synthetic IDs/digests, lifecycle/cursor, retention/hold/GC codes, step-up bucket, result/retry/timing; never names/emails, export/workshop/directive/journal bodies, cookies/OAuth, credential material/hashes, fragments, handles, signatures, browser storage, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

State/property and lifecycle E2E cover no prior directives, material/nonmaterial attestation before transfer, unresolved handoff, old-sponsor refusal/unavailability, post-transfer-only work and mixed lineage. The new sponsor never receives old directive bodies or attests for them; unresolved prior influence blocks only the high-status gates and is visibly actionable without rewriting scientific history.

title: W5.6 Hypotheses + evidence engine (classes, coercions, friction)
description: WHY: hypotheses are attack ROUTES (strategy) distinct from claims (content); evidence classes are COMPUTED because authors grade their own homework otherwise; and formalization friction is captured because a stuck proof is high-signal information about the CLAIM, not just the prover. WHAT: hypotheses (route, mechanism, falsifier, expected_evidence, discriminating_predictions consumed by the discriminate move, origin proposed/third-alternative/refinement); evidence engine: 5 computed classes assertion < heuristic < citation < computation < certified — certified requires artifact shape checks (e.g. Lean with pasted axiom report, no sorry on scan) PLUS independent review confirming scan matches (scan alone rates computation; server runs no Lean in v1); P5 coercion (computation without stated domain/detection floor -> heuristic, recorded); P8 (external facts need locator + short copyright-compliant excerpt or source model_memory which caps at assertion); selection disclosure (evidence that selected/tuned a hypothesis is flagged and cannot serve as its independent confirmation); exploratory/confirmatory mode (exploratory accepted, labeled, cannot drive promotion); fails-to-reproduce direction is first-class; FORMALIZATION-FRICTION kind: claim@ver, toolchain, exact stuck point (witness seed), blocker class statement-too-strong / missing-hypothesis / definition-mismatch / counterexample-scent / tactic-only; routing bias stated: under uncertainty friction means the claim might be false — counterexample-scent and statement-too-strong seed the add-refuter-from-friction move; claim CEILING = min over own evidence classes and depends_on chain, weakest link surfaced. DONE: class-computation table tests; every coercion fixture; friction -> move-seed integration test; ceiling DAG computation test. PROSE-PROOF RULE: evidence of kind argument/construction STARTS at class assertion and gains standing through review, not through class — which is exactly the honest description of an unreviewed proof; no amount of prose confidence raises its computed class.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover hypothesis versions/status, falsifiers, evidence classes, bears_on coercions and independence friction, conflicting outcomes, kill/revive rules, third-alternative/discriminate triggers, exact references and the invariant that metadata cannot mint truth. Real D1 concurrency tests race evidence and version changes. scripts/e2e-hypotheses-evidence.sh creates competing hypotheses, uploads/binds each evidence class, attempts invalid coercion/self-certification, fires and disputes falsifiers, records nulls, and verifies packs/moves/claim graph plus md/json/html parity. OPS.2a logs object/version/ref and artifact IDs, evidence class, computed relation/facet digest, request/event IDs, cursor, rule/code and latency; never scientific bodies, workshop data, tokens, cookies, presigned URLs, or hidden reasoning.

title: Device-flow poll contention maps transient pacing races to a lying FLOW_INVALID 400
description: d1-store.ts device polling (:2190-2470 region): the pacing CAS gives each request two read-compute-write attempts; three-plus concurrent polls of one flow handle (e.g. an agent HTTP client retrying on timeout while earlier polls are in flight) can lose both, after which the post-loop check sees token_hash IS NULL and throws FLOW_INVALID -> router maps to 400 telling a legitimate poller its valid handle is bad when the real cause is pacing contention. Self-heals next poll; window is milliseconds wide. SUSPECTED (first-principles trace by EnrollmentAudit scout, no repro run). Fix direction: return a coarse slow_down when the final check finds the row healthy-but-racing instead of FLOW_INVALID.
close_reason: Landed (d42328f): post-loop fallback in D1EnrollmentStore.poll now distinguishes a healthy racing pending row — evidence valid, unexpired, device mapping intact, no sponsor panic — and returns coarse {kind: slow-down, retryAfterSeconds: poll_interval_seconds} instead of FLOW_INVALID 400. Any suspicious field keeps original FLOW_INVALID semantics. Deterministic plant 'nzee: losing both pacing CAS attempts...' simulates the concurrent winner via onStatement sabotage bumping last_poll_at before each pacing UPDATE (armed post-deviceCreate, COALESCE+1 to stay evidence-valid); asserts slow-down decision, >=2 sabotages, row stays pending. File suite 152/152, wire typecheck+lint clean.

title: W12.8 Launch gates G1/G2/G3: alpha cohort, public launch, +30d review
description:
WHY: Launch is a scientific claim about the platform and gets the same honesty the platform demands of its users. The gates are the named ones and ONLY those (build-program honesty, binding on the fleet: proposing a new build artifact requires naming its consumer, the gate it enforces, and the observed defect that justifies it). Closure is never self-issued: a workstream is done when an INDEPENDENT pass re-executes the exit criteria against the exact revision. WHAT: G1 (private alpha): Cold-Agent Gauntlet >= 8/10; fixture table green; dogfood board worked; backup restore drilled. Alpha cohort composition is deliberate: MULTIPLE sponsors per problem (cross-sponsor identity and review independence are the central product hypotheses — an alpha of one sponsor fleet cannot test them), plus recruited formal-methods practitioners, mathematically sophisticated engineers, and at least one adversarial security reviewer, not just enthusiastic generalists. Decide OQ-1 (permissionless at G2 vs invite-allowlist for the first month) from dogfood signal. G2 (public): red team closed; screening corpus holds; texts slop-scrubbed + IP diff-review complete; OG images render; Vercel plan decided; seed-ladder lower rungs live + sharpened SP4D flagship; then post the FIRST PUBLIC JOIN URL on X, attached to the flagship page, with the sandbox ledger already alive behind it. G3 (+30 days): first multi-sponsor problem with a T2 (cross-model-family) review recorded; cost within the model; moderation median response < 24h; promotion cap (20/hr/Fellow/problem) re-tuned on real data; revisit OQ-2 (scheduled vs emergent syntheses) with G3 evidence. DONE: each gate checklist executed and recorded in docs/; every closure independently verified at the exact revision; launch post published.

W11 FINAL-GATE BOUNDARY: the CLI remains optional for participants and never enters the capsule, but the accepted Fable build order completes and verifies W11 before G2. Launch evidence checks signed install artifacts, curl parity, validate/scrub corpus parity, ambiguous-operation recovery and the revision-matched less-than-100ms reference-host warm-start result. A missing CLI proof is not silently reclassified as optional product behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Every G1/G2/G3 criterion is a machine-readable checklist bound to an exact revision, environment, corpus/config digest, independent rerunner, raw artifact references, result, evidence scope, and no-claim boundary. scripts/e2e-launch-gates.sh orchestrates rather than reimplements the named gauntlet, fixture, restore, screening, load, privacy, accessibility, and dogfood suites; it fails closed on missing/stale/partial evidence or single-sponsor substitutes. The redacted launch JSONL and signed summary record gate/scenario IDs, revision, bindings, start/end, retries, result and artifact digests; never credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, workshop/private bodies, raw harness transcripts, or chain-of-thought. Closure requires independent re-execution, not author attestation.

G2 orchestration consumes W11 release/install, curl-parity, corpus-parity, replay-safety and warm-start evidence at the launch revision; missing or stale CLI evidence fails closed while onboarding remains fully curl-first.

title: W2.8 Backups, exports, retention enforcement
description:
WHY: a free public scientific record must be un-losable and exitable: D1 Time Travel covers 30 days, but the JSONL export IS the public dataset, the agent warm-up format, and the exit hatch — and retention promises in the ToS need mechanical teeth. OWNERSHIP: this bead implements and tests the backup, export, verification, restore, inventory, and retention primitives; OPS.6 alone owns deployed schedules, alarms, recurring execution, and filed drill reports. WHAT: provide invocable full SQL dump plus per-problem JSONL event streams and signed checkpoints for a backups bucket with a 90-day lifecycle; restore-to-scratch tooling that counts rows, verifies event-chain and artifact digests, and refuses partial or mismatched restores; artifact-inventory reconciliation of R2 objects against artifacts rows; /p/slug/export.jsonl.gz endpoint under CC BY 4.0; citation export as BibTeX and CSL with stable URL, cite key, statement version, and access date; retention jobs that hard-delete never-published private drafts on an authenticated request and minimize or expire raw IP and security records on schedule without changing public ledger history. TESTS: unit/property tests cover deterministic export ordering, checkpoint chains, compressed round-trip, citation escaping, lifecycle selection, retention eligibility, legal-hold exclusions, idempotency, partial/corrupt inputs, and clock boundaries; mock-free local D1/R2 tests export, destroy only a scratch database, restore it, compare rows/cursors/digests, seed missing/orphan/corrupt artifacts, and prove workshop/private bytes never enter public exports. scripts/e2e-export-restore.sh creates representative public/private state, exports, verifies, restores into an explicitly validated scratch target, exercises interrupted upload/resume and wrong-target refusal, and compares canonical faces. OPS.2a JSONL records run/revision, explicit source and scratch binding IDs, phase, counts, byte/digest summaries, cursors, duration, retry, assertion diffs, and result — never bodies, drafts, IPs, credentials, presigned URLs, or raw security records. DONE: OPS.6 can safely invoke each primitive; export round-trips through the verification tool; restore and retention fault cases pass; the tool refuses any non-scratch restore target. SCALE NOTE (R-7): D1 has a 10GB/database ceiling; the sizing sanity says 10GB of markdown is years of discourse, and the accepted mitigation if success-scale ever threatens it is that problems shard naturally by scope and this export/rebuild machinery is the migration path — no pre-emptive sharding complexity at launch.

DELETION-SAFE RESTORE: backup retention and logical deletion are separate clocks. Every account/private-data deletion, credential revocation, cancelled enrollment/transfer, content control and private-CAS unbind writes a signed, access-restricted retention-control record to a current deletion journal outside the point-in-time dump. Restore always lands in a validated scratch/quarantined target, verifies the snapshot, fetches and verifies the latest journal/checkpoint, reapplies every control newer than the snapshot, reruns reference-aware CAS cleanup, and proves no deleted identity/private draft, revoked credential, old sponsorship access or prohibited content is serviceable before cutover. Backups may retain encrypted deleted bytes until the disclosed 90-day lifecycle or legal-hold expiry, but restore never reactivates them; key destruction may provide earlier cryptographic erasure where used. Missing/stale/unverifiable journal fails closed. Export/deletion receipts state the backup window, legal-hold exception, shared-public-hash consequence and expected physical-erasure deadline without exposing other references.

VISIBILITY-NAMESPACE RESTORE: backup and restore inventories treat private CAS and public delivery as distinct physical namespaces joined by canonical digest and binding receipts. Restore may never attach a private bucket to the public hostname or recreate a public copy solely because a private binding exists. Deletion/redaction drills purge controlled public caches and state the no-clawback boundary for copies downloaded while content was public.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover deterministic exports/checkpoints/compression/citations, lifecycle selection, legal holds, signed deletion-journal canonicalization/ordering, replay/idempotency, shared-CAS reference decisions, backup-window clocks, credential/access revocation, partial/corrupt snapshot or journal and wrong-target refusal. Mock-free D1/R2 tests create public/private/shared state, delete/unbind/revoke after a backup, restore only to scratch, apply the newest journal, compare rows/cursors/digests and prove no deleted personal/private bytes or obsolete authority becomes readable before cutover. scripts/e2e-export-restore.sh exercises export, interrupted resume, snapshot-before-deletion restore, journal loss/tamper/staleness, legal hold/release, shared public hash, CAS inventory and canonical faces. OPS.2a logs run/revision, explicit source/scratch binding IDs, snapshot/journal/checkpoint digests, phase/counts, retention/hold/GC decision codes, cursors, duration, retry and bounded diffs; never bodies, drafts, PII/IPs, credentials/hashes, presigned URLs, journal sensitive contents or security rows. Closure requires a seeded resurrection defect to fail and a report of evidence scope, backup residual window and physical-erasure boundary.

Snapshot-before-publication and snapshot-before-redaction cases prove restore preserves namespace visibility, refuses missing publication receipts, and does not overclaim recovery of previously downloaded or third-party-cached public bytes.

title: Export verifier accepts truncated streams and envelope-only tampering
description: Fresh-eyes audit of verifyProblemExportChain found it treats the last nonempty line as a trailer without validating it, so removing export_end can make the final event disappear from verification and a truncated prefix return intact when checkpoints are absent. It recomputes only payload/previous chain links and ignores row_digest plus event_id/type/object_id/created_at, so envelope-only tampering passes. Header/license/checkpoint/trailer/framing shapes are not strict.
acceptance_criteria: Strictly parse one header, ordered event lines, and one terminal export_end with exact problem/event_count/final_cursor and complete LF framing; reject missing/duplicate/trailing/malformed controls and blank-line ambiguity. Recompute and compare every event row digest and chain digest; validate required checkpoint ordering/shape/root policy rather than allowing checkpoint removal to bypass the final root. Causal tests cover missing trailer, last-event truncation, extra/trailing record, event_id/type/object_id/created_at-only tamper, row digest tamper, checkpoint removal/reorder/corruption, header license/extra-key errors, empty stream, and exact positive round-trip. Focused tests, typecheck, lint, UBS pass.
close_reason: Verified resolved at HEAD — implementation and full causal matrix already landed by peer; executed evidence this session: krater-export.test.ts 30/30 green covering every acceptance case (missing trailer, last-event truncation via chain mismatch, duplicate/extra/trailing terminal records, blank-line + CRLF framing, envelope-field-only tamper via row-digest recompute over event_id/object_id/created_at, checkpoint removal/reorder/corruption/foreign-problem, header extra-key, empty stream, exact positive round-trip). Verifier strictly parses one header, ordered events, one export_end with exact problem/event_count/final_cursor, enforces strict checkpoint sequence + consumption accounting so removal cannot bypass the final root. Residual chain-preimage gap (row_digest unbound) is correctly tracked as 5il1, not this bead.

title: Raw Drizzle query errors can expose SQL and bound values

close_reason: Opaque fixed-operation D1 boundary replaces every sync/async dependency failure with a fresh frozen exact-shape error; SQL/params/cause cannot escape through callback, builder, raw-client, mounted face, or logs.
