comments.author: MistyCliff
comments.text:
2026-08-20 MistyCliff (ntm:%18). ACCEPT on source/static for the filed scope. Independent hard read-only acceptance audit. Root holds the router/test leases; I took no reservation, made no edit, ran no test.

FREEZE (start == end, no drift during this pass)
apps/wire/src/sessions/router.ts        76262da80c2decdc988bb9f36865d6c6895cd7bd7da13e1f12a94eae0ba5fc17 (1960 L)
apps/wire/test/unit/session-routes.test.ts 7f518dd87e8b13d5e75f26c3acc0b7937c075aac7e680a8b3e5bec73fb38a29e (4170 L)
Both files have moved since the 2026-08-19 19:26/19:59 ACCEPTs on router 373b15af... / test 6d142bfa..., so this is a fresh audit of current bytes rather than a re-confirmation of those hashes. Load 10.13-10.96 throughout: no Wire focused/type/Biome/scoped-UBS run. Source-only evidence, not a green gate.

1. OWNERSHIP-QUALIFIED MINIMAL SELECT - ACCEPT. router:522-557 packSessionOf issues exactly `SELECT session_id, problem_id, closed_at FROM sessions WHERE session_id = ? AND fellow_id = ?` - three columns, ownership in the WHERE rather than a post-hoc JS comparison. Absent and foreign converge on one code path, so the 404 body cannot differ between them by construction, not merely by matching literals. Owned-closed returns SESSION_CLOSED 409. Both refusals set `cache-control: private, no-store`. The pack route at :792 is the only caller; I verified openSessionOf's seven call sites (:1127/:1243/:1331/:1559/:1637/:1672/:1743) are all other routes, so no pack path retains the old `SELECT *` shape.

2. MEMBERSHIP BEFORE PRIVATE READS - ACCEPT, and the ordering is structural rather than incidental. membershipRoleOf resolves at :820, readCursor at :821, and the `membership === undefined` early return at :845-869 precedes every private read: claims at :882, prior handback at :917, workshop heads at :953. The two refusals that sit before membership (UNKNOWN_PROFILE 400, budget refusal) are pure parameter checks with no DB access, and both sit after packSessionOf - so a foreign Fellow with a malformed profile still gets the generic 404, never a 400 that would confirm the session exists. The 8spk claims predicate `source_seq <= ? ORDER BY source_seq ASC` survives intact at :884.

3. OBSERVER NONVACUITY - ACCEPT. test:44-82 fires afterRead on all three D1 verbs: run (:47-59, including the SELECT-via-run branch), first (:63-68), and all (:70-74), each after the statement executes, so it records reads that actually happened rather than intentions. prepare() returns `{ bind, ...methods() }`, so an unbound `.first()` is recorded too and cannot slip the roster. LocalRead is exactly `{kind, sql, bindings}` (test:25-29), which is what makes the toEqual rosters below discriminating rather than shape-tolerant.

4. FOREIGN GENERIC 404 PLANT - ACCEPT (test:2390-2531). It seeds all three private lanes first - a closed prior session carrying a handback marker, a workshop object, and a claim row with public_seq advanced - then enrolls a genuinely distinct Fellow through the real enrollment router and asserts `foreignBinding.fellowId !== binding.fellowId`. Arming is scoped by a recordReads flag around the single request. It then asserts the exact roster `toEqual([{kind:"first", sql: packSessionSql, bindings:[targetSession.session_id, foreignBinding.fellowId]}])` - one read, right verb, right bindings - and separately that no marker reaches the body. The strongest line is `expect(await unknown.text()).toBe(foreignBody)`: byte-identity between a foreign-owned real session and a nonexistent id is the actual no-oracle property, and it is proved rather than asserted by matching two literals.

5. OWNER NO_MEMBERSHIP ZERO-PRIVATE-READ PLANT - ACCEPT (test:2533-2637). Membership absence is made deterministic by an explicit `DELETE FROM problem_memberships WHERE problem_id = ? AND fellow_id = ?` rather than by never creating it, so the plant cannot silently pass on a fixture that never had the row. It asserts 200, private no-store, a quoted ETag, all three markers absent, `PackResponseSchema.parse` on the real response bytes, items [], omitted [{reason:"no_membership"}], viewer exactly {audience:"session", membership:"none", effective_permissions:[]}, and the exact three-read roster (owned session, membership, cursor) with `toEqual`. It also proves owned-closed 409 private/no-store on the way through.

NONVACUITY OF THE ROSTERS, CHECKED MECHANICALLY. A hardcoded SQL literal that drifts from source turns these assertions red for the wrong reason, or - worse - a whitespace-tolerant comparison would let a private read hide. I string-compared all three literals against source: packSessionSql matches router:529 exactly, membershipSql matches router:566 exactly, and cursorSql matches krater.ts:1271 exactly, character for character. Each source call uses .first(), matching the asserted `kind`. krater's statement() helper is `db.prepare(sql).bind(...values)` (krater.ts), so the cursor read's bindings are ["P-4DSP"] as asserted rather than []. The router registers no app.use middleware, so nothing outside the traced route can contribute a read.

WHY THE ONE-READ ROSTER IS ACHIEVABLE AT ALL - the question that could have made both plants guaranteed-red. recordReads is armed before the request, so authentication is inside the observed window. authenticate (router:457-478) resolves through options.service.credentialBinding, and fixture() constructs EnrollmentService with `store: new InMemoryEnrollmentStore()` (test:359), so credential resolution performs zero reads through the observed shim. The fellow_tokens liveness read is credentialIsLiveAtCommit (router:446-455), which by name and call site belongs to write commits and is absent from the pack GET path. So one read for foreign, three for no_membership, are both reachable.

RESIDUALS - out of this bead's scope, recorded so this ACCEPT is not read as more than it is:
- packSessionOf's 404 and 409 use the unvalidated `problem()` rather than `validatedProblem()` (envelope.ts:121 vs :131). No schema drift is reachable from these fixed literals today, but this is the class bead `but` tracks, not a p9h1 regression.
- openSessionOf still does `SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE session_id = ?` and compares fellow_id in JS, so the exact private-read-before-ownership pattern p9h1 fixed on the pack route persists on the seven other session routes. p9h1 names the pack route only, so this is correctly outside it - but the class is not closed repo-wide and should not be assumed so.
- The no_membership ETag matcher is `/^"[^"]+"$/`, weaker than the `/^"[0-9a-f]{64}"$/` form used elsewhere in this file; it proves quoting, not that the digest is SHA-256.
- The handback read is `ORDER BY closed_at DESC LIMIT 1`, still tie-nondeterministic - that is dependent bead 7llj, untouched here and correctly so.

BOUNDARY. Local: everything above is proved against real migration SQL on bun:sqlite through the in-test D1 shim, driven by the production createSessionRouter. Static only - I executed nothing, so I claim no colour for the suite; I claim that I found no construct in these two plants that would red for a reason unrelated to the property under test. Workerd: not exercised. The shim emulates prepare/bind/first/all/run and batch-as-transaction; workerd's D1 binding semantics, its statement limits, and its real ETag/304 conditional handling are untested here, so "one read" is a statement about the router's issued statements, not about what a deployed D1 would count. Deployed: no claim whatsoever. Runtime, type, Biome and scoped UBS remain unrun under the load rule, so this ACCEPT is on semantics and bytes - do not close p9h1 on it, and note it is still blocked by 8spk, kgaa and x5wl.

title: Tier 2: DOI/arXiv citation enrichment + retraction watch
description: WHY: Tier 2 citation enrichment makes L-n objects easier to check and retraction watch protects dispositions resting on withdrawn literature. Provider metadata is an aid, not evidence; it must never overwrite contributor provenance, invent a source match, or silently mark a scientific claim false. WHAT: resolve DOI/arXiv identifiers through outbox consumers to versioned provenance-stamped canonical title/authors/year/venue/URL metadata; preserve contributor fields and display discrepancies for review. Watch authoritative retraction/withdrawal/correction signals with provider/source/version/retrieved time and confidence; flag the citation, emit a public event where appropriate, and route dependent evidence/dispositions through existing staleness re-evaluation—never directly change disposition. Support backfill, retry/dead-letter, rate/cost limits, provider replacement and manual correction with history. P8 still requires locator/excerpt for evidence; enrichment neither proves prior art nor contradiction. TESTS: unit tests for identifier normalization, merge precedence, discrepancy, correction/retraction state and staleness routing; mock-free/provider-contract integration with recorded licensed synthetic responses, rate limit, timeout, malformed metadata, DOI reuse/version change, retraction reversal and duplicate outbox delivery; E2E creates/reuses a citation, enriches it, injects a withdrawal, observes staleness/notice and correction without history loss. Logs follow OPS.2a with citation/provider/version/request/event IDs, source response digest, outcome, latency/retry and affected public refs, never full copyrighted metadata payloads, private bodies, API keys or user queries. DONE: new and existing citations process idempotently; one retraction fixture proves end-to-end staleness and one false/withdrawn signal proves reversible review; UI/agent faces label provenance and uncertainty; provider outage leaves core citation writes usable and visibly delayed.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/table tests cover DOI/arXiv normalization, contributor-versus-provider merge precedence, discrepancy/history, correction/retraction states, reversible signals and staleness routing. Provider-contract integration uses licensed synthetic recordings and exercises timeout, malformed metadata, rate limits, duplicate outbox work, identifier/version change, withdrawal and reversal while core writes remain available. scripts/e2e-citation-enrichment.sh creates and reuses a citation, enriches it, injects withdrawal, observes notice plus dependent staleness without direct disposition mutation, then reverses/corrects it without history loss. OPS.2a JSONL records citation/provider/version/request/event IDs, response digest, outcome, retry/latency and public refs, never copyrighted payloads, private bodies, API keys or user queries.

title: W10.2 Protocol fixture table + scientific state-machine table
description: WHY: Quality is mechanical (Rule A9) only if every hard rule is pinned to a recorded refusal — a rule without a fixture will silently regress the first time someone refactors the validator. This table is the permanent, executable form of the P1-P13 contract and of the scientific state machine, and it is what makes "the convenience path cannot bypass the validator" (R-17) a tested fact rather than an intention. WHAT: (A) Protocol fixture table — one recorded refusal per hard rule: self-certification (P2/P4: author-sent disposition/proved/confidence/certificate field is SCHEMA_INVALID with a pointer, never a coerced success); missing falsifier (P3 MISSING_FALSIFIER on conjecture-class kinds); self-review (P1 REVIEWER_IS_AUTHOR); dependency cycle (P10 CYCLE_IN_DEPENDENCIES); near-duplicate (P11 DUPLICATE_CLAIM via norm-hash: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace, tokenize $...$ math spans; response carries the existing ID + "review or refine that one" next action); LOOKS_LIKE_CLAIM with force_note escape (recorded, ranked last, sponsor-visible); statement-drift reset (P9: edit mints @n+1, disposition resets to open, reviews stay version-pinned); review-pack isolation (P12: fixture PROVES author workshop bytes are absent — the review profile is composed by exclusion, not filtering, R-16); implicit-session-equals-promote-validator (the curl one-shot path runs the SAME promote function; fixture proves it cannot bypass any rule); CANNOT_ERASE_NEGATIVE (P6); SYNTHESIS_UNANCHORED (P13). (B) Scientific state-machine table: author cannot self-certify; a verifier pass bound to a different statement digest promotes nothing; invalidated/retracted evidence flags dependent dispositions stale (never cosmetically green); superseded claims reject edits; negative results without scope/detection fields are coerced (P5) and the coercion is recorded; novelty cannot derive from proof review (separate claims, separate reviews); review-state facet and disposition move independently; reduced-to keeps the original open in needs/ranking until the target resolves. Every fixture logs rule id + error code + full RFC 7807 body for snapshot comparison. DONE: all fixtures green in CI; each rule also has a deliberately-should-fail case (a validator that cannot fail is not a validator); fixture changes follow gate-diff discipline.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Every protocol row names preconditions, request fixture, expected transaction/event/projection/cursor changes, response/error and recovery; every scientific row names legal/illegal transitions and disposition facets. Unit validation rejects duplicate, missing, unreachable or contradictory rows and checks coverage against contracts/rules/routes. scripts/e2e-protocol-fixtures.sh executes all eligible rows against real local D1/R2/DO bindings and emits should-pass/should-fail parity across Worker, render and CLI; non-executable scientific controls still replay through the real state machine. OPS.2a logs table/row/version, fixture digest, request/event IDs, cursors, verdict/code/rule, implementation revision, duration and bounded diff; never bodies, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, or private fixture content.

title: W11.3 asimp validate + scrub (byte-parity with the Worker)
description: WHY: Local validation is only trustworthy if it can never be surprised by the server — the byte-parity contract is the whole point. And scrub exists because the server refuses token-shaped strings in bodies (P7) and soft-rejects detected secrets/PII with redacted locations; catching that locally before upload is cheaper for everyone. WHAT: asimp validate <file>: offline validation against the published JSON Schemas from @asimposium/contracts; MUST agree with the Worker validator byte-for-byte on verdicts over the ENTIRE golden corpus — this parity is a CI gate (AGENTS.md: asimp validate and the Worker must agree on the golden corpus). asimp scrub <file>: the same secret/PII scan the server runs at ingest (API-key/private-key/credential patterns, personal addresses), executed locally before anything uploads; reports the REDACTED location and remediation, never echoes the detected value; supports the acknowledged-false-positive path. Both commands: --json, exit code semantics (0 clean, nonzero with structured findings). DONE: corpus verdict diff empty in CI (parity test runs on every contracts change); scrub shares its fixture corpus with the server-side scanner (W9.2) so the two implementations cannot drift.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover every golden object/error, canonical bytes, scrub classes, Unicode/encoding, nested archives, false-positive allow cases, streaming bounds, deterministic output, and fail-closed malformed input. Worker/asimp differential tests share the W1.5 corpus and random seeds byte-for-byte. scripts/e2e-asimp-validate-scrub.sh downloads public schemas, validates valid/invalid files, scrubs secret/PII canaries, compares promote responses, handles offline/stale-schema mode, and proves no input leak through stdout/stderr/log artifacts. Structured CLI JSONL records command/schema/corpus/tool versions, input/output digests, verdict/code/rule/pointer, duration and bounded diff; never file bodies, secrets, PII, tokens, cookies, home paths, terminal scrollback, or raw transcripts.

All four named routes reach the shared seam via jsonBody (:835): /v1/device-code at :1045 (DEVICE_CODE_BODY_INVALID), /v1/fellows at :1108, and /v1/fellows/flow + /v1/device-token both through poll() at :1163 (routes registered :1182-1183).

Canonical reader: readBoundedRequestBody in auth/http.ts:92 — the same seam screening (route.ts:249) and sessions already use.
- maxBytes validated nonnegative safe integer (:96).
- content-encoding other than identity is REFUSED (:99-106) so a compressed-size header cannot stand in for parsed bytes — a decompression-bomb guard beyond what this bead asked for.
- Early declared-length refusal: canonical decimal content-length regex, safe-integer check, then > maxBytes -> too-large (:108-123), each preceded by cancelUnconsumedRequestBody.
- Streamed overrun refusal: running total > maxBytes -> cancel + too-large (:165-169), so an absent or false-low content-length cannot bypass the bound.
- One fixed allocation Uint8Array(maxBytes+1); BYOB reader preferred with documented non-BYOB fallback that copies only accepted bytes and never retains an oversized chunk (:133-150).
- Cancellation on every refusal path; reader.releaseLock() in finally with the error swallowed so a hostile stream cannot replace the typed result (:176-182). Returns bytes.subarray(0,total).

Fatal UTF-8: auth/http.ts:32 TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }) via parseExactJsonBytes (:270), called at router.ts:845 on the raw bytes. Malformed UTF-8 throws instead of replacement-decoding.

Opacity: too-large -> 413 REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE; every other ingress failure -> EnrollmentError(invalidCode) defaulting to PAIRING_INVALID. Both are OPAQUE_PROBLEM_CODES; no body bytes, length, or exception text is reflected. Pre-parse refusals (hasQuery -> BODY_ONLY_REQUIRED, hasJsonContentType -> JSON_CONTENT_TYPE_REQUIRED) also cancel the unconsumed body first.

Two observations, neither a defect:
1. The cap is one shared MAX_ENROLLMENT_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES = 64 KiB (router.ts:70) rather than per-endpoint. It matches MAX_SERVICE_ENVELOPE_BODY_BYTES and is far below screening's 1 MiB, so it is conservative; 'endpoint-appropriate' is satisfied in effect but not expressed per route.
2. The reader eagerly allocates maxBytes+1 per request. At 64 KiB on unauthenticated routes that is a bounded and acceptable small-request-to-allocation ratio; it would deserve review only if this cap were raised toward screening's 1 MiB.

- Compressed ingress is refused outright (:99-106) so a compressed-size header can never stand in for parsed bytes.
- Declared content-length is canonical-decimal, safe-integer and <= maxBytes (:108-123), with cancellation on each refusal. A FALSE-LOW declaration deliberately passes this block, which is exactly why the streaming loop must be authoritative.
- Cap crossing is enforced on the running total BEFORE the copy: total += chunk.byteLength, then if (total > maxBytes) cancel and return too-large (:164-168), with bytes.set only after (:169). No oversized chunk is ever written.
- BYOB is attempted first and the per-read size is min(16 KiB, remaining) over a maxBytes+1 allocation (:136, :159), so at the boundary it requests exactly one more byte — that is how cap+1 is detected rather than inferred.
- Cancellation is best-effort and nested-guarded (:150-157) and releaseLock runs in a finally (:174+), both written so a hostile stream cannot replace the typed result.
The non-BYOB comment is honest: it claims only that OUR code copies accepted bytes and never duplicates an oversized chunk. It does not claim the upstream producer chunk is bounded, which would be false on Bun. No overclaim.

MOUNTED PATH: /v1/device-code reaches the seam through the shared jsonBody helper (router.ts:835-845), which maps too-large to EnrollmentRequestBodyTooLargeError and every other failure to the route invalid code. MAX_ENROLLMENT_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES is 64 KiB (router.ts:70).

THE PLANT (test:874-936) proves all six required properties and is mutation-causal on each:
- Mounted: a real Request to /v1/device-code driven through router.fetch, not a helper shortcut.
- Cap crossing: payload asserted at exactly MAX+1 bytes, split into a first chunk of exactly MAX and a second of one byte, so the boundary is crossed by one byte rather than overshot. content-length is deliberately "1" with a comment naming the intent, so only the stream can enforce the cap.
- Cancellation and release: the stream cancel hook counts exactly 1; incoming.body.locked is false and incoming.bodyUsed is true — a three-part proof that the reader cancelled AND released rather than stranding the lock.
- Zero service effect: service.deviceStart is replaced by a counter that also THROWS if reached, and deviceStartCalls is asserted 0. Double protection.
- Opaque no-reflection: OpaqueProblemSchema.safeParse(refusal).success is true, a schema-level opacity proof rather than a substring check. I confirmed statically that REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE is in OPAQUE_PROBLEM_CODES (problem.ts:98), so that assertion is not resting on an unrun claim. Plus three independent negatives: the join-secret-shaped canary, the agent name, and the whole request JSON are all absent from the raw body. Status 413.
Mutations traced: drop the streaming total check, or trust only the declared length, and deviceStartCalls becomes 1 (and the stub throws); skip cancel and cancellations is 0; skip releaseLock and locked is true; leak the body and the three negatives red; emit a teaching-class problem and the OpaqueProblemSchema assertion reds.

title: W2.3 Envelope/content split + content_controls + lawful redaction
description:
WHY: append-only provenance is a product invariant, but unlawful bytes (CSAM, doxxing, court orders) cannot be retained forever. The resolution is architectural: envelopes remain immutable, content bytes are separately redactable, and the historical fact that an event existed is never falsified. WHAT: event_content table separate from events; content_controls row per target (versioned and attributable, with effective visibility derived here rather than a mutable event flag); a narrowly authorized redaction path that cryptographically erases or replaces content bytes while leaving envelope, digest, public-safe tombstone, reason category, and restricted audit trail; ordinary corrections still use superseding events. D1-compatible constraints/triggers prohibit UPDATE/DELETE of event envelopes from every ordinary write path; the exceptional path touches only separated content/control records and is audit logged. DONE: redacting a fixture leaves the chain verifiable, envelope intact, tombstone visible, and original bytes unavailable from service-controlled origin storage and caches, subject to the explicit downstream-copy boundary; direct UPDATE/DELETE attempts against event envelopes fail in local and real D1 tests; ordinary Worker handlers cannot invoke the exceptional path without the required operator authorization; audit and face fixtures pass.

ERASURE CLAIM BOUNDARY: an authorized redaction purges controlled CDN entries, removes or cryptographically erases origin bytes and blocks every application/index route, but it cannot claw back copies a reader downloaded or a third-party cache retained while the public immutable URL was lawfully live. Tombstone, API response and legal copy state that boundary exactly; tests establish controlled-service unavailability, not universal erasure.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover envelope/content canonicalization, digest binding, key/version references, tombstone and lawful-redaction authority, content_controls ordering, public-versus-private visibility, cache/search/export behavior, corrupt/missing content, and immutable event history. Mock-free D1/R2 tests redact only scratch objects, rotate encryption/signing material where applicable, rebuild projections and verify checkpoint continuity. scripts/e2e-content-redaction.sh publishes representative content, executes authorized and refused redactions, then checks all faces, exports, artifacts, caches, FTS and citations show lawful tombstones without residual bytes or rewritten envelopes. OPS.2a logs object/event/content IDs, content digest, authority/reason code, before/after projection/checkpoint digests, request ID and timing; never redacted/original bodies, legal request details, credentials, cookies, tokens, or private data.

Redaction E2E verifies origin deletion or cryptographic erasure, controlled-CDN purge, direct artifact-host failure and all application/index paths, while the evidence report explicitly excludes previously downloaded or uncontrolled third-party copies from the erasure claim.

title: W6.8 Search v1: exact references + public D1 FTS5
description:
WHY: Search is a documented first-class unauthenticated route and the launch stack explicitly chooses D1 FTS5, yet the prior backlog only mentioned /search inside a renderer census. A cold agent or human must be able to paste an exact cite, find a concept, understand zero results, and trust that private drafts/workshops cannot leak through indexing, snippets, counts, cache keys, or diagnostics. WHAT: implement public search on a.asimposium.org/search?q= with canonical .md and .json agent faces and the matching Agora projection. Resolve exact short codes, slugs, global IDs, problem-scoped refs with enclosing problem, Fellow names, and stable URLs before lexical search. FTS5 indexes only public problem titles/statements, public claim extracts, and Fellow names as allowed by Fable; workshop, private-draft, moderation payload, directive, and unlisted-discovery rows are excluded mechanically. Parameterize every D1 query; normalize Unicode/math queries without inventing semantic equivalence; safely escape FTS operators; reject pathological length/complexity with a teaching contract error. Results carry kind, stable ID/URL, exact status/version, provenance-safe highlighted snippet, score explanation limited to lexical fields, source cursor, omitted[], and next_actions. Ranking is lexical relevance plus exact-reference precedence, never activity, actor/model identity, engagement, or scientific disposition; filters cover kind, area, and current problem status; pagination is cursor-stable under concurrent writes. Empty results distinguish malformed/exact-not-found/valid-no-match and suggest capabilities, cite syntax, or browse surfaces without fabricating related work. ETags and caches derive only from public projection versions. TESTS: table/unit tests for query normalization, exact-ref routing, escaping, filters, snippet sanitization, and stable pagination; mock-free integration tests on real local D1 FTS5 including Unicode/math, adversarial operators, concurrent inserts, and rebuild-from-log parity; scripts/e2e-search.sh proves md/json/html semantic parity, exact-ID precedence, useful zero-result recovery, SQL/FTS injection resistance, ETag/304, and absence of workshop/private/unlisted bytes in results, counts, cache, and structured logs. Logs follow OPS.2a and record query digest rather than raw potentially sensitive text. DONE: documented routes and examples work from curl; public FTS rebuild is deterministic; privacy-negative corpus remains empty; search degradation is explicit while direct ID/URL reads continue to work.

UNLISTED EXACT-REFERENCE LAW: exact-reference precedence applies only to discoverable public resources. /search never confirms, returns or redirects to an unlisted/private-draft object even when q exactly matches its slug, short code, ULID or stable URL; it returns the same non-enumerating valid-no-match shape as an absent ID. A caller already holding an unlisted canonical URL may use the direct read route, whose page labels guessable-not-private. Search next actions may explain that unlisted resources require a direct link without confirming whether this query exists.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover exact reference precedence, Unicode/math normalization, FTS operator escaping, parameterization, query complexity bounds, filters, lexical-only deterministic ranking, safe snippets, stable cursor pagination, empty-state recovery, ETag and degradation. Mock-free local D1 FTS5 tests exercise concurrent inserts, rebuild-from-log parity and adversarial queries. scripts/e2e-search.sh compares md/json/html semantics, exact IDs and lexical results, zero-result next actions, 304/cache behavior, direct-ID continuity during FTS failure and SQL/FTS injection resistance. A privacy corpus proves workshop/private-draft/unlisted/moderation/directive canaries never appear in result, snippet, count, cache, metric or log. OPS.2a records query digest, public filter/result IDs, projection/cursor/ETag digests, status/code and timing; never raw query, bodies, private refs, identity analytics, credentials, cookies, tokens or fragments.

Exact-ref tests pair discoverable, unlisted, private-draft and nonexistent objects with identical-shaped negative responses for the latter three, including status, bytes, timing buckets, counts, cache keys and logs; direct unlisted reads still work and remain absent from suggestions/pagination/snippets.

title: W6.9 Artifact API: manifest, resumable upload, verification, and status
description:
WHY: Artifacts are how computations, formalizations, and reproductions become independently checkable. W2.7 owns CAS storage, but the documented POST /v1/artifacts agent journey needs an explicit ergonomic and failure-safe HTTP contract; otherwise large uploads, ambiguous completion, scan quarantine, and retry behavior will be invented ad hoc by the CLI or first endpoint author. WHAT: implement the Fellow artifact surface over W2.7: POST /v1/artifacts creates a manifest with declared sha256, byte size, allowed media type, filename metadata, intended public object/workshop attachment, and idempotency key; authorize centralized upload-artifacts scope, grants, per-object/day budgets, target visibility, and account posture before returning a 15-minute presigned R2 PUT or multipart/resume instructions. Completion verifies server-observed size, MIME sniff versus declaration, digest, archive traversal/decompression limits, and scan status before the artifact may bind to a ledger object; digest mismatch never aliases the declared hash. GET manifest/status is resumable and returns uploaded ranges, expiry, scan/quarantine state, safe retry action, request/event IDs, and stable artifact URL only when eligible. Ambiguous transport after completion is resolved by idempotent status lookup, never a blind second object. Text writes may commit while R2 is down; upload state becomes explicit pending/degraded and no scientific disposition advances from an unverified or quarantined artifact. Direct artifact serving preserves immutable cache headers and attachment disposition rules; no HTML/SVG executes under a site origin. Workshop CAS references stay visible only in owning workshop indexes even though unlisted hashes are not treated as secrets; token/PII scanning still occurs before binding. TESTS: unit/table tests for state machine, scope/grant/budget policy, MIME decisions, expiry, retry and idempotency; mock-free local/staging R2 integration for single/multipart resume, duplicate digest dedupe, zero-byte/boundary sizes, digest/MIME mismatch, presign expiry, interrupted completion, concurrent completers, R2 outage, scan quarantine, traversal and decompression bombs. scripts/e2e-artifact.sh uploads a small computation, interrupts/resumes a multipart upload, binds it to evidence, verifies immutable retrieval and provenance, proves unauthorized/cross-sponsor binding and quarantined use fail, and checks structured redacted logs. Logs follow OPS.2a, include manifest/request/event IDs and content digests, and never bodies, presigned query strings, credentials, or workshop extracts. DONE: curl-only and asimp-compatible examples work; every error teaches a safe recovery action; real-binding E2E and degradation cases pass; the same manifest cannot create duplicate artifact/event bindings under retry.

DELIVERY NAMESPACE CONTRACT: manifest/status responses distinguish private-uploaded, pending-publication and published. A stable artifacts.asimposium.org URL is returned only for a verified public-namespace object with a live public binding. Owners retrieve private/workshop artifacts through an authenticated a. endpoint with private cache headers; the presigned upload target and status response never make the private namespace publicly addressable. Publication retries reconcile by digest and binding receipt, and a cross-sponsor caller gets no existence, dedupe, scan or ownership oracle for private hashes.

ARTIFACT RIGHTS BINDING: the manifest declares a contract-enumerated content class and source/ownership provenance; public binding derives (rather than trusts) the immutable license snapshot from the target problem rights policy. Private upload/verification may proceed while publication acceptance is unresolved, but copy to the public namespace and evidence eligibility fail closed on missing sponsor terms/patent-warning acceptance, incompatible/unknown licensing, or unlicensed third-party material. Published status/faces/direct responses expose the canonical license link/ID and historical bindings cannot be retroactively relicensed. MIME or filename alone never determines rights.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests exhaust artifact manifest/status states, centralized scope/grant/budget policy, expiry, idempotency, observed-versus-declared size/MIME/digest, multipart ranges, scan/quarantine, target binding, safe retry and outage degradation. Mock-free D1/R2 integration covers boundary sizes, concurrent dedupe/completion/binding, interruption/resume, presign expiry, mismatch, malicious MIME/archive/bomb, scanner/R2 outage and recovery; unverified/quarantined bytes never move disposition. scripts/e2e-artifact.sh uploads, resumes, completes, polls status, binds evidence, retrieves immutably, retries ambiguity and refuses cross-sponsor/unsafe use through curl. OPS.2a logs synthetic manifest/artifact/request/event IDs, content digests, size/ranges/state, attempt, status/code and timing; never bodies, filenames carrying private text, presigned query strings, credentials, cookies, tokens, workshop extracts, scanner patterns, transcripts or hidden reasoning.

Artifact E2E includes authenticated private retrieval, anonymous/direct-host refusal for private-only hashes, delayed copy-on-publication, stable public retrieval after verification, revoked-binding access, cross-sponsor same-digest oracle resistance, and public/private cache separation.

Artifact unit/E2E covers source/text/data/formal/log classes, default and approved override licenses, private upload before acceptance, corrected publication gate, third-party provenance, caller-spoofed/mismatched license, transfer/revision history and immutable direct-response license metadata. Failure preserves private bytes/state for authorized repair, creates no public copy/evidence standing and logs only policy/license/version/provenance digests.

title: W2.2 The write transaction: validate, mutate, project, append — atomically
description:
WHY: Doctrine A6 and synchronous projections live or die here. This is the only state-changing command pipeline—including sponsor envelopes and implicit sessions—so one accepted LOGICAL write must produce exactly one durable event and matching projection state, while every rejected/aborted logical write produces neither. For POST /events:batch, each validated member is one logical write and therefore one event; all member events/projections commit atomically in causal order, with no extra opaque batch-wrapper event and no several-objects-in-one-event shortcut. WHAT: authenticate and authorize the effective principal centrally; validate contracts; run required policy decision or choose quarantine before visibility; freeze total attribution from authenticated state on every scientific logical write and event — (Fellow, sponsor_at_event, session, model_string_self_declared, harness), with declared fields labeled and never later rejoined through mutable current sponsorship; begin D1 transaction; allocate public seq per problem for public ledger writes OR workshop seq per (Fellow,problem) for private pushes using UPDATE...RETURNING, never one shared workshop counter or an application counter; insert/version the domain object; update all affected projections; append the immutable event envelope plus separated content; enqueue outbox work; store idempotency key plus canonical request digest and original result; commit. Same key plus same digest returns the original status/body/event IDs even after an ambiguous client disconnect; same key plus another digest returns IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. client_occurred_at is provenance only and never ordering. No notification, model call, fetch, or R2 dependency holds the D1 transaction open; post-commit effects reconcile through the outbox. TESTS: pure unit tests for command/policy routing and canonical request digest; mock-free local and real-D1 integration for parallel public and per-Fellow workshop allocation, exactly-one-event, all projection/event/outbox/idempotency invariants, validation and injected-failure rollback at every statement, same/different-key replays, connection cancellation before and after commit, lock contention, and stale-context refusal. A property/fault harness restarts the Worker/DB boundary and proves every observed result is rejected-with-no-state or committed-and-replayable—never object without event, event without projection, duplicate commit, or silent gap. DIAGNOSTICS: emit lock-wait, transaction duration, outcome, command kind, scope IDs, request/event/idempotency digests and seq/cursor changes through OPS.2a; never payloads, credentials, workshop content, or idempotency keys themselves. DONE: unit/integration/property suites green, real-D1 behavior matches local, failure logs identify the injected phase and causal IDs, and rebuild-from-log equals incremental projections after the full fault corpus.

ONE-TIME CREDENTIAL IDEMPOTENCY AND ACTORSHIP: ordinary writes persist replayable non-secret original results for 24 hours. A command whose sole successful response contains a one-time credential stores only the credential hash plus a non-secret issuance receipt; it never stores plaintext or reversibly encrypted bearer material and never mints a replacement on retry. First authenticated use records delivery. If the response disconnects before the client can prove possession, polling returns the committed-but-delivery-unknown receipt and CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_UNKNOWN with an explicit recent-auth sponsor revoke/rebind action; it never returns or reconstructs the credential. This is the narrow one-time-exchange exception already required by the CLI doctrine that such exchanges are not blindly retried. Transaction events separately freeze scientific content-author attribution and the acting principal: sponsor-promoting a stalled Fellow object records the sponsor action without changing the original Fellow/session/model/harness authorship or any independence computation.


CAUSAL AND QUARANTINE TRANSACTION LAW: derived writes carry deduplicated, canonically ordered, fully qualified caused_by parents into the immutable envelope. Each parent must be visible and authorized to the acting command and either committed before this transaction or resolved earlier in the same validated batch; same-scope lower seq and batch topological order are enforceable, while independent scopes and the global /cursor are never treated as a total event clock. A public promotion may retain its authorized private workshop cause internally, but permission-filtered public projections replace inaccessible parent refs with caused_by_omitted metadata. A promotion routed to quarantine still commits exactly one logical event, but its public projection/content is only the coarse quarantine notation; restricted candidate bytes remain behind content_controls and never enter object, search, feed, cache or export projections. A later release, rejection or restore is a separate logical write and event caused by the quarantined event. The pipeline never appends both a hidden scientific event and a second wrapper/moderation event for one command.

PUBLIC REVISION ATOMICITY: a revise command validates target/base and replacement against one snapshot, inserts the immutable new version, advances the head by compare-and-swap, applies reset/staleness projections and appends its single event in the same transaction. A lost CAS returns OBJECT_VERSION_CONFLICT after rollback with no version, event, outbox or idempotent success result. Direct, workshop-promoted and batch revisions use this exact command path.

GLOBAL INVALIDATION ATOMICITY: in the same D1 transaction, advance the singleton global public-change cursor exactly when the command changes anonymous-visible projection state. A transaction with several public batch members advances by a documented deterministic delta while committing atomically; a workshop/private-only, rejected, quarantined-with-no-public-notation, or rolled-back command does not advance it. This cursor only tells public clients that something changed; per-problem seq remains the canonical event resume/order contract. The committed cursor value is included in the non-secret result/outbox purge job so W7 can reconcile notification loss without guessing from application memory.

GLOBAL EVENT ALLOCATION: contract-declared global commands allocate global_event_seq with the same UPDATE ... RETURNING discipline and exactly-one-event/projection/idempotency guarantees as problem commands. The event carries a qualified global scope and may cause or be caused by another scope only through validated fully qualified caused_by refs. This canonical global event seq is distinct from the global /cursor public-change revision; a global event advances /cursor only if it changes anonymous-visible state.
acceptance_criteria:
ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover canonical command digests; one-event-per-logical-write; public versus per-Fellow workshop allocation; content-author versus acting-principal attribution; ordinary 24-hour replay; hash-only one-time credential issuance receipts, first-use acknowledgement, ambiguous delivery and explicit revoke/rebind; same-key/different-body conflict; and no replayable secret persistence. Mock-free local and staging D1 fault tests inject failure before and after every statement, disconnect before/after commit and token response, replay across Worker restart, concurrent public/workshop writes, lock contention and stale context. scripts/e2e-write-transaction.sh proves every outcome is rejected with no state, committed and replayable, or explicitly unknown/recovery-required; it verifies exactly one event/credential, matching projections/outbox, sponsor-promotion authorship, rebuild equality and no secret in D1 dumps, backups, exports, logs or artifacts. OPS.2a records command/scope/request/event/receipt digests, actor and author principal classes, cursors, phase, lock/transaction timing, result/code and bounded diff; never idempotency keys, credential material, flow handles, payloads, workshop bodies, cookies, signatures or private data.

Fault/property tests include causal DAG validation and replay plus pass, quarantine, release, reject and restore paths. They assert one event per logical command, visible coarse notation where promised, no hidden sequence gap, no restricted-byte exposure, and no duplicate wrapper event.

Fault injection stops before/after public-version insert, head CAS, projection and event; concurrent revisions prove exactly one winner and byte-identical loser pre-state, with direct/promote/batch parity and rebuild-derived head equality.

Fault/property tests correlate global cursor changes with projection visibility across multi-problem concurrency, mixed public/private batches, commentary/content-control/moderation notation, rollback and ambiguous disconnect. They prove monotonicity, deterministic batch delta, no false movement, no missed public-visible commit, replay returns the original cursor result, and outbox reconciliation converges after purge loss without changing event order.

Concurrency/fault cases interleave global identity/moderation/governance commands, problem writes and workshops; assert gap-free committed ordering per scope, rollback without sequence/event/projection residue, qualified cross-scope causality, replay equality and independent global_event_seq versus public-change-cursor behavior.

Causality fault cases cover canonical deduplication, same-scope prior seq, already-committed cross-scope parents, earlier versus later temp IDs, actor authorization, private workshop-to-public promotion, permission-filtered omission metadata and attempted use of /cursor or timestamps as event order. Replay retains the complete internal DAG while anonymous projections leak no private parent identity.
notes: 2026-08-18 peer-code audit handoff: session replay wrapper runs the write, seals the response, and inserts replay state as separate operations. Seal/insert failure can leave a committed write without its replay receipt; concurrent same-key calls can both run before one replay insert wins. Promote additionally updates global public_cursor outside Krater writeClaim. A single atomic write path must own mutation, projection, event, cursor, and idempotency receipt.

title: bun:sqlite bulk run silently skips mid-file failing statements (migration data-loss hazard)
description:
bun:sqlite's bulk Database.run(sqlFile) executes a multi-statement script but SILENTLY SKIPS any statement that fails mid-file: observed on 2026-08-22 while proving asimposiumorg-yxmo — applying db/migrations/0021_problem_scoped_claim_identity.sql over a contaminated legacy database let the FK-violating INSERT..SELECT be skipped without any error, silently dropping the projection row and leaving a half-applied migration that then COMMITTED cleanly. Constraint errors DO propagate for short single-line statement blobs; the skip reproduces with real multi-statement migration files.

This is a latent data-loss footgun for every harness or test that (a) seeds rows into a legacy-shaped database and (b) applies forward migrations via bulk run — exactly the pattern the S-2/S-3 legacy fixtures use elsewhere through wrangler/D1 routes (safe there) but not necessarily in future bun-side harnesses. krater-backup.test.ts freshDb() bulk-applies only onto empty databases today, which is why it has not misbehaved.

Fix direction: apply migration files statement-by-statement inside one transaction per file (D1 semantics), using a sqlite3_complete()-style splitter that handles trigger bodies (nested CASE..END;, single-line triggers) — working reference implementation lives in apps/wire/test/unit/krater-problem-scoped-identity.test.ts splitSqlStatements(). Alternatively node:sqlite exec propagates correctly but is unavailable under Bun 1.3.14.

Acceptance: a focused regression test proves bulk-run skip vs statement-wise refusal on the 0021 contamination scenario; any repo harness applying SQL files through bun:sqlite bulk run is migrated to the statement-wise seam or annotated; no behavior change for D1/wrangler paths.
close_reason: Executable hazard proof landed in krater-problem-scoped-identity.test.ts: bulk exec silently skips the refused mid-file statement (later statements still apply -> half-migrated + committed), and the silent drop disarms the statement-wise seam on re-run. Harnesses already migrated off bulk runs by the batch()-shim refactor (exec=0 across wire); no D1/wrangler behavior touched. Seed helpers converted to array-form bindings to satisfy installed bun-types.

title: OPS.2 CI pipeline (stage order = doctrine) + gate-diff discipline
description: WHY: CI stage order is doctrine: contracts gate faces, faces and pack determinism gate smoke, smoke gates deploy. Green must mean required proof ran, not that a provider skipped it; gate changes must be isolated and independently reviewed. OPS.2a owns the shared runner/secret-safe diagnostic contract consumed here. WHAT: create one provider-neutral root gate, runnable locally and on an actually available hosted runner: format/typecheck/lint; comprehensive unit suites; contract golden corpus; face snapshots and sanitization; pack determinism/budget/isolation; mock-free D1/R2/DO integration; security/property tests; smoke-agent.sh and smoke-gallery.sh against preview; then deploy Worker before web and verify compatibility/capabilities. Slow scheduled suites remain explicit: Playwright, gauntlet, load/fault, restore and release tests run at the Fable-prescribed gates/cadence, with required status visible in the launch revision. A stage whose subject exists cannot be skipped, marked neutral, or hidden behind continue-on-error; timeouts/cancellations fail and clean resources. Protected paths—gauntlet/scorer, fixture corpora, smoke scripts, goldens, redaction rules and thresholds—require a separate gate diff and independent reviewer; weakened-gate-inside-feature-change is refused. Integration uses real local bindings/staging, never D1/R2 mocks. DIAGNOSTICS/ARTIFACTS: collect OPS.2a JUnit, redacted JSONL, coverage as a diagnostic, property seeds/shrunk cases, bounded diffs, deployment IDs/timestamps and exact revision. A failed stage links its safe reproduction command and causal request/event IDs; success says which scheduled/live proofs were not run. CURRENT CONSTRAINT: ops/console-notes.md records GitHub Actions unavailable due usage limits. First land the local gate, then select/document a runner that is actually available. Vercel native Git and Cloudflare Workers Builds remain intended deploy paths, but independent native deploys do not prove ordering; orchestration must make Worker schema/capabilities ready before Agora and roll forward/fail closed on incompatibility. DONE: local gate passes; hosted gate runs on every reviewable change; test runner redaction self-tests pass; protected-path review is enforced; missing/failed stages are unmistakable; Worker-before-web is proven with revision/deployment evidence. This blocks G0 exit so smoke proof cannot be declared without a live gate path.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: The provider-neutral root gate runs format/typecheck/lint, complete unit/contract/render/determinism, mock-free bindings integration, security/property, smoke and deploy-compatibility stages in doctrine order, with explicit scheduled Playwright/gauntlet/load/restore/release status. Unit tests cover stage DAG, fail/timeout/cancel propagation, cleanup, retry, artifact/redaction and Worker-before-web compatibility/roll-forward. A hosted runner actually available to this repository executes every reviewable change; no subject-bearing stage is neutral, continue-on-error or silently skipped. Protected gate/corpus/scorer/golden/redaction changes are isolated and independently reviewed. scripts/e2e-ci-pipeline.sh seeds failures at every stage and proves status/diagnostics. OPS.2a artifacts bind exact revision/deployments, JUnit, redacted JSONL, seeds and safe reproduction; never secrets, private bodies, raw traces/transcripts or hidden reasoning, and green states all unrun proof.

title: [Security] Reject extra fields in runtime service-envelope keyring
description: Reachable mounted path: app.ts parses SERVICE_ENVELOPE_KEYS and casts the array, then constructs VerificationKeyring. keyring.ts validates only kid/publicKeyHex/notBefore/notAfter and copies every enumerable property, so a syntactically valid record with an extra privateKey or secret field is accepted and its public key verifies envelopes. That can place signing material on the Worker, defeating the public-key-only compromise boundary. infra/resolve-wrangler-deploy.mjs rejects extra fields, but the runtime parser does not, and the mounted runtime tests do not plant this case. Fix runtime structural validation to allow only the four public fields and add mounted secret-canary rejection/no-reflection coverage.
acceptance_criteria: A mounted app rejects a key record with any extra field, including privateKey or secret, without echoing its value; legitimate rotation records still work.
close_reason: Accepted at dac1c9cf/98ad42f2: mounted app rejects privateKey and secret extras before retention/import with fixed nonreflecting error and zero D1; legitimate two-key rotation reaches signature/nonce ingress; focused 127/127, Wire typecheck, scoped Biome and positional UBS pass; independent frozen-byte audit ACCEPT. No deployed claim.

  apps/wire/test/unit/service-envelope.test.ts 98ad42f2006004e7e9bdd1259a7a2026cfe99dec365fe346e02d4fbc797c53fa

EXACT OWN ENUMERABLE KEY SET BEFORE RETENTION/IMPORT: constructor snapshots each record via Object.freeze({...record}) (keyring.ts:106) BEFORE validation; validateRecord runs on the sealed snapshot and rejects any Object.keys(sealed) member outside the frozen whitelist {kid,publicKeyHex,notBefore,notAfter} (VERIFICATION_KEY_RECORD_FIELDS :39, check :60-62) with the fixed message "key record contains an unsupported field" — no field name or value reflected. Order is whitelist (:121) -> retention #records.set (:131) -> lazy crypto.subtle.importKey only at lookup (:168). So an extra field is refused before the record is retained and long before any key import. An accessor-backed field is materialized by the spread and thus caught as a data key; a getter that throws is caught at :102-115 into the fixed "keyring records could not be read", not reflected.

SYMBOL/PROTOTYPE/NON-ENUMERABLE BOUNDARY — HONEST: the mounted input is JSON.parse(SERVICE_ENVELOPE_KEYS) (app.ts:440), which yields only own-enumerable string keys, so the string-key whitelist closes the actual reachable threat completely. Object.keys is string-only by design; non-enumerable own props are not copied by spread (dropped, unretained); prototype props are neither copied nor Object.keys-visible and a prototype-injected kid reads back undefined and is rejected. Tests do not overclaim: :790 rejects a symbol *value* for publicKeyHex, :782/:786 reject non-object/non-string, :796/:825 normalize throwing/ trap-forged inputs without reflecting a canary. Residue (non-blocking, outside the JSON threat model and not claimed covered): a symbol-*keyed* extra on a non-JSON caller's record is spread-copied into the frozen snapshot and retained, but is never read, imported, or reflected — inert, and unreachable from the mounted config path.

MOUNTED REJECTS privateKey AND secret, NO REFLECTION, NO D1: test.each ["privateKey"/MOUNTED_PRIVATE_KEY_CANARY, "secret"/MOUNTED_SECRET_CANARY] (:1064-1108) builds the record via JSON.stringify (real mounted shape), drives createApp().fetch at the mint URL, and asserts failure instanceof KeyringConfigError, message === "key record contains an unsupported field", JSON.stringify(diagnostics) excludes the canary, and preparedSql === []. The nonceClaimingD1 spy (:889-903) records every prepare(); [] proves zero SQL. app.ts parseKeyringRecords (:436-448) emits only fixed "valid JSON"/"nonempty array" messages and casts; the construction throw at enrollmentStack (:529-531) precedes all nonce ingress.

LEGITIMATE TWO-KEY ROTATION STILL VERIFIES: overlap keyring (mounted-previous notAfter=now+3600, mounted-current notBefore=now-3600 open-ended) passes the "exactly the newest current key is open-ended" invariant (:134-140); both kids reach mounted signature+nonce ingress and land the expected 422 MINT_BODY_INVALID, with preparedSql length 4 = 2 DELETE + 2 INSERT auth_envelope_nonces (:1151-1211). Unit overlap at :575-614 and single-key ingress at :1111-1148 (2 SQL) corroborate.

TESTS CAUSAL / NO OVERBROAD REJECTION: the preparedSql empty-vs-populated pair is the causal oracle — the ONLY difference between the rejected canary keyring ([]) and the accepted valid keyrings (2 / 4 SQL) is the extra field, so acceptance of the extra field would flip [] to 2 and red the canary tests. notAfter stays optional (:73) so a current-only record ({kid,publicKeyHex,notBefore}) and valid rotation are accepted (:694,:732-746) — no overbroad rejection. Startup errors never echo the invalid kid (:720-730).

title: W12.1 Seed-problem ladder rungs 1-5 (ADR-25): calibration through literature
description:
WHY: ADR-25 — launch does not seed only famous unsolved problems; each ladder rung exercises a specific subsystem against a KNOWN answer before open-ended frontier work depends on it. Day-one visitors must see a ledger that demonstrably works, and R-1 (nobody comes) is mitigated because the site works at N=1 as a public lab notebook with the calibration rung proving the loop on day one. WHAT: author, sharpen (through the real statement gate: claims board locked until a non-proposer review lands statement-clear), and WORK each rung end-to-end on staging, then seed production: RUNG 1 calibration problems — known theorems with PLANTED ERRORS and known outcomes; exercise claims, reviews, and the epistemic fixtures against ground truth, and quietly measure reviewer quality. RUNG 2 reproduction problem — reproduce a published computational result with open code/data; exercises artifacts, environments, reruns, and honest fails-to-reproduce findings. RUNG 3 counterexample program — bounded conjecture family where finite searches yield real results with stated detection floors; exercises hypotheses, kills, and dead ends. RUNG 4 formalization program — translate known informal theorems into Lean; exercises statement binding, formalization-friction reports with blocker classes and witness seeds, and the certified review path (artifact scan rates computation; certified requires independent review confirming artifact-matches-scan). RUNG 5 literature synthesis — map a narrow question with exact anchors; exercises L-n citations, unanchored-citation flags, and novelty review. G2 minimum: one calibration problem worked end-to-end with known outcome + one reproduction + one counterexample program live. All statements pass the real sharpening gate; every rung leaves its known-answer checks recorded ON the ledger as the proof it works. DONE: rungs 1-5 live with at least one worked example each; subsystem checks recorded; G2 minimum met. SCHEDULING NOTE: statement/reference DRAFTING for every rung may begin immediately in docs/seed/ (nothing gates prose); this bead is blocked only on WORKING the rungs through the live sharpening gate and ledger.

AUTHORSHIP PATH: seed dossiers are input material, not self-publishing platform content. Each live seed problem is adopted and promoted by an explicitly onboarded Fellow in a recorded session under a named sponsor, then passes non-proposer sharpening review and sponsor/steward publication; the platform/operator may prepare and assign the private governance brief but never posts the scientific object as a Fellow.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/schema/golden checks bind every rung dossier to its exact public statement version, falsifier, source/artifact hashes, known-answer oracle, expected object/refusal sequence, license, subsystem assertion and no-claim boundary; planted controls include both must-fail and valid-negative cases so a polished transcript cannot pass by appearance. scripts/e2e-seed-ladder.sh runs all five rungs through real staging enrollment, sharpening, sessions/packs, workshop promotion, artifacts, reviews, citations, formalization friction, novelty and closing handbacks, then compares ledger events/faces/exports with the frozen expected outcomes; it deliberately injects a wrong proof, weaker formal statement, leaking computation, missing detection floor, fabricated/misquoted citation and unanchored synthesis and requires the exact mechanical refusal or coercion. A separate production-seed mode is explicit, idempotent, revision-bound and refuses to run against an unexpected environment or changed dossier digest. OPS.2a launch JSONL records rung/scenario, revision/environment, dossier/source/artifact/statement/event/output digests, synthetic Fellow/sponsor/session IDs, cursors, rule/code, reviewer tier, expected/actual outcome, timing and bounded diff; never hidden oracle answers before evaluation, scientific/workshop bodies, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, private directives, raw harness transcripts, or hidden reasoning. Closure requires an independent rerun and states which scientific conclusions remain unproven.

title: OPS.4a Compute research-write and product readiness from revision-bound capability evidence
description: WHY: Plane health and endpoint reachability are not evidence that the research product exists. Agora must never turn a healthy canary or reachable Worker into a false ready claim. WHAT: define one versioned, closed readiness contract produced by Stoa and consumed by Agora. Compute research-write and overall product readiness only from same-revision mock-free evidence for enrollment, sessions, packs, workshop, promotion, public ledger delta, cursor, and visible budgets. Replace the current hardcoded not-ready row only when that complete evidence is fresh and coherent; otherwise fail closed with a precise unavailable/not-ready state.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: A generated contract enumerates the exact required capability and proof IDs, revision, environment, observation time, evidence digests, and expiry. Agora accepts only schema-valid, same-origin, same-environment, same-revision, fresh, complete evidence and never exposes secrets or private bytes. A mock-free staging run completes enrollment then session to pack to workshop push to promotion to public Diptych delta, and separately proves cursor movement and visible budgets. Missing, stale, malformed, duplicate, unknown, mixed-revision, empty, canary-only, enrollment-only, or endpoint-only evidence leaves research_write and product_readiness not ready. Contract, Worker, Agora, and retained launch evidence agree byte-for-byte; closure requires an independent exact-revision rerun.

No production file, no new file, nothing deleted. The start hash equals the byte set both prior audits (SnowySnow 03:34, jemanuel 04:13) froze and ACCEPTed, so this builds on the audited bytes rather than racing a peer edit.

PRESERVED VERBATIM: the exact four-field template assertion at faces.test.ts:664-666 is untouched, including its backtick-escaped id and the em-dash label sequence.

DEFECT REPLACED. The old loop was 'for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(entry)) expect(markdown, field).toContain(String(value))'. It searched the WHOLE document for a bare value, so a future field false-greens whenever its value collides with something already printed: a future 'revision: 73' rides on 'seq 73', and any future instant equal to updated_at rides on the timestamp beside it. Neither field would need to be rendered at all.

REPLACEMENT, distinct-position binding. Locate this entry's own line and the omitted[] line, then for each contracted key that is NOT named in omitted[], record indexOf(String(value)) within that line, require it to be >= 0, and finally require the set of recorded positions to have the same size as the number of recorded fields. Two fields can therefore never be proven by one substring: a colliding value resolves to the SAME index and collapses the set, failing the size assertion. Disclosure in omitted[] remains the explicit escape the acceptance allows. No renderer label or template is restated here, so the test cannot drift into asserting a private copy of the face it is checking.

WHY NOT MUTATION. I first designed a per-field sentinel re-render, which is the strongest form, and rejected it: ledger-face.ts loadIndex calls ProblemsIndexResponseSchema.parse, so every sentinel must be type- and format-valid per field, which cannot be derived generically for an unknown FUTURE field without duplicating the schema's domains into the test. Distinct-position binding stays general.

KNOWN RESIDUAL, disclosed rather than hidden: indexOf returns the FIRST occurrence, so if a future fixture chose an id or value that textually contains another field's value earlier in the same line, a genuinely rendered field could map to the wrong position and fail. That is a false RED, never a false green, and it fails with the field name in the assertion message. The current fixture (P-DIPTYCH-PARITY / 73 / two distinct instants) has no such overlap.

STATIC CHECKS: git diff --check clean; every line I added is within Biome lineWidth 100 (one 113-char assertion was wrapped by hand before it could trip the formatter).   3fe0a06b2b6796d827fd3aaa  apps/wire/test/contract/faces.test.ts
  46bd1ff61183270b37a00899  apps/wire/src/ledger-face.ts
  39ef39fd22a4ce7190e18269  apps/wire/src/app.ts
  51eb8833986ac4ee5235daa5  packages/contracts/src/ledger.ts

VERIFIED — the plant at faces.test.ts:716 does what it claims, through the MOUNTED entrypoint.
- Genuinely one-axis: `after = { ...before, updated_at: … }`, so id/public_seq/created_at are byte-identical and only the mutated field can move an ETag.
- Mounted, not a bare router: it drives `wireEntrypoint.fetch(request, env, context)` with a real execution context, so the assertions cover the dispatch path rather than a handler in isolation.
- Both faces change: JSON is parsed through ProblemsIndexResponseSchema and compared with `toEqual([expected])`; Markdown is asserted to contain the exact rendered line including `updated ${expected.updated_at}`. A mutation that reached one face but not the other fails.
- Per-face ETags move across the mutation: `second.jsonEtag !== first.jsonEtag` and `second.markdownEtag !== first.markdownEtag`, asserted separately.
- Cache headers preserved on BOTH the 200s and the 304s: exact `public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300`, plus `markdown === json` cross-check. Asserting the literal rather than importing the shared constant is the right call — an imported constant would move with the source and could not detect a weakening.
- Exact If-None-Match yields an EMPTY 304: status 304, the same ETag echoed, cache-control preserved, and `expect(await conditional.text()).toBe("")`. The empty-body assertion is explicit, not implied by the status.

NO FALSE-GREEN FIXTURE REUSE. The DB stub closes over a mutable `current` reassigned between the two reads, so one env serves both passes and the mutation is the only delta; `after` is a fresh spread, so there is no aliasing back into `before`. The stub re-asserts the exact SELECT text on every call. The sibling parity test at :671 uses a DISTINCT fixture (P-DIPTYCH-PARITY / seq 73) from this one (P-DIPTYCH-ETAG / seq 74), so neither test can green the other or contaminate it.

THE ONE UNASSERTED PROPERTY — cross-face ETag distinctness. Every `.not.toBe` in the plant is TEMPORAL (before vs after, per face). Nothing asserts that at a single instant `jsonEtag !== markdownEtag`, and a repo-wide search for that comparison in the suite returns zero. If the two faces ever emitted the SAME ETag, every assertion here would still pass — while a client that cached /problems.json under an ETag and revalidated /problems.md with it would receive a wrongful 304 carrying the other face's semantics.
The property does hold in production, and deliberately so: ledger-face.ts:35 computes `strongEtag(face, body)` as SHA-256 over `${face}\n${body}`, i.e. the face label is a DOMAIN SEPARATOR prefixed to the body. That separator exists precisely to make the two faces' ETags distinct even if their bytes ever coincided — and no test pins it. Deleting the `${face}\n` prefix would leave this plant, and the whole suite, green.
SMALLEST ADDITION (one line, no new fixture): inside `readFaces`, `expect(jsonEtag).not.toBe(markdownEtag);`. That converts the domain separator from an undocumented implementation detail into a pinned contract, and it costs nothing because both values are already in scope.

BOUNDARY. Static source only at the hashes above. Nothing executed — no tests, typecheck, Biome, UBS, Git or Beads writes beyond this comment — so the plant's redness under mutation is reasoned from its assertion structure and the ETag derivation, not observed. Local unverified; deployed unclaimed.

FROZEN, start == end, no drift

THE PREMISE IS CONFIRMED, AND THE STATED JUSTIFICATION IS STALE. local-d1-worker.ts:60-65 justifies the bypass because "createApp() builds its own enrollment stack from bindings this harness does not supply, and routing enrollment through it would silently discard the clock offsets the TTL proofs depend on." Both halves are now false: app.ts:67-69 declares createEnrollmentStore and enrollmentClock on CreateAppOptions, enrollmentStack threads them at :534-535, and :521-522 keys the cached stack on their identities. The harness's clock is `{ now: () => Date.now() + localClockOffsetMs }` - a stable object whose closure reads the live module variable - so passing it once keeps the cache hot AND keeps every later offset mutation visible. The bypass has no remaining technical reason.

EXACT CURRENT PATH: request -> local-d1-worker fetch -> two public-text paths short-circuit to a separate `createApp()` instance (:245-250) -> resolveService (its own EnrollmentService over `new D1EnrollmentStore(env.DB)`, agoraOrigin hardcoded "https://asimposium.org", clock Date.now()+offset) -> ten `/__s1/*` setup and observation routes -> everything else falls through to `createEnrollmentRouter({ service }).fetch(request)` at :490.
PRODUCTION PATH: request -> createApp -> ledger faces, screening, /p guards -> session middleware -> `isEnrollmentPath(pathname)` gate -> enrollmentStack(env, options) -> router.fetch -> ROUTER_MISS_HEADER translated to canonical routeNotFound -> app.notFound / app.onError.

FIVE BEHAVIOURAL DELTAS, which is exactly the drift the bead names:
1. Unknown-path 404. Production translates the router miss into the canonical RFC7807 routeNotFound (app.ts:754-757) and strips x-asimp-internal-router-miss. The harness's router never gets a notFound - app.ts installs that at :641 on the router IT builds, not inside createEnrollmentRouter - so today an unknown path returns Hono's default plain-text 404 AND leaks the internal header to the client.
2. Dispatch breadth. Production routes only isEnrollmentPath(pathname); the harness sends everything not matched earlier to the enrollment router.
3. Unhandled errors. Production app.onError emits a typed INTERNAL_ERROR 500 problem; the harness has no onError, so a throw escapes as a raw workerd 500.
4. Surface. Session/cursor, ledger faces, /p guards and the screening route do not exist in the harness at all.
5. Origin policy. The harness hardcodes agoraOrigin; production requires a trusted AGORA_ORIGIN binding or refuses the whole plane with 503.

THREE RISKS I RETIRED BEFORE PROPOSING THE MIGRATION, each from the frozen bytes:
- Required bindings. env.ts declares REQUIRED_BINDINGS = DB, ARTIFACTS, PUBLIC_ARTIFACTS, KRATER_OUTBOX with structural probes, so the obvious fear is that createApp fails closed under the harness's narrow LocalEnrollmentEnv. It does not: app.ts references missingBindings/bindingStates/REQUIRED_BINDINGS NOWHERE. Nothing on the enrollment path consults them. And the harness already shares infra/wrangler.toml, which declares all four, so at runtime they are present regardless - the narrow interface is a type, not the binding set.
- Dual EnrollmentService. Keeping resolveService for the `/__s1/*` routes while createApp builds its own service means two instances over one database. That is safe here because EnrollmentService's six fields are ALL readonly (#store #clock #random #replayProtector #stoaOrigin #agoraOrigin) - it holds no instance-scoped mutable state, so with the same D1 store, the same key-derived protector and the same clock the two are observationally equivalent.
- Case stability. The migration narrows dispatch, so any case reaching a non-enrollment path would change. I enumerated every non-`__s1` path the client requests: /v1/device-code, /v1/device-token, /v1/fellows, /v1/fellows/flow, /v1/hello, /join/<enrollment_id>, /protocol.md, /skill.md. The first five are in EXACT_ENROLLMENT_PATHS (app.ts:85-98), /join/<id> matches the two-segment join branch at :376, and the two texts are served by createApp's own public-text table. The client asserts NO 404 and NO router-miss anywhere. So all 33 existing cases stay byte-stable, and delta 1 above is a strict improvement with no case depending on the old shape.

ONE HARD NEW REQUIREMENT. enrollmentStack refuses unless isTrustedAgoraOrigin(env.AGORA_ORIGIN) (app.ts:503-504), and that predicate accepts ONLY https://asimposium.org or https://staging.asimposium.org (contracts/enrollment.ts:140-148). The harness supplies no AGORA_ORIGIN today. Without it every enrollment request becomes 503 and all 33 cases fail - so this is the one change that cannot be skipped.

--- PATCH 1: apps/wire/src/enrollment/local-d1-worker.ts

1a. Add `AGORA_ORIGIN?: string;` to LocalEnrollmentEnv beside STOA_ORIGIN, with the same
    comment discipline: absent or untrusted must reach the same fail-closed 503 as a
    malformed one.

1b. Delete the two public-text specials - PUBLIC_TEXT_PROOF_PATHS (:66), cachedPublicTextApp
    (:73) and the short-circuit block at :243-250 - and replace them with one cached
    production app that carries the overrides:

/**
 * One production app for this isolate, built with the harness's own store and
 * clock. It serves the public texts, the enrollment plane, and every other
 * mounted production surface through the exact middleware, dispatch, error and
 * 404 path a deployed Worker uses. The overrides exist precisely so this
 * harness no longer has to bypass it: `enrollmentClock` is a stable object
 * whose closure reads the live offset, so advancing the offset stays visible
 * without rebuilding the cached stack.
 */
let cachedProductionApp:
  | { readonly db: D1Database; readonly app: ReturnType<typeof createApp> }
  | undefined;

function productionApp(env: LocalEnrollmentEnv): ReturnType<typeof createApp> {
  if (cachedProductionApp !== undefined && cachedProductionApp.db === env.DB) {
    return cachedProductionApp.app;
  }
  const app = createApp({
    createEnrollmentStore: () => new D1EnrollmentStore(env.DB),
    enrollmentClock: { now: () => Date.now() + localClockOffsetMs },
  });
  cachedProductionApp = { db: env.DB, app };
  return app;
}

1c. Replace the fall-through at :490

      return createEnrollmentRouter({ service }).fetch(request);

    with

      return productionApp(env).fetch(request, env as never, _ctx);

    and rename `_ctx` to `ctx` in the fetch signature. Drop the now-unused
    `createEnrollmentRouter` import (:10). Keep resolveService, localFailure,
    unavailable, sha256Hex and all ten `/__s1/*` routes exactly as they are -
    they are the local-only setup/observation surface the bead requires retained,
    and they must keep running BEFORE the fall-through so production dispatch
    never sees them.

--- PATCH 2: scripts/e2e-s1-cold-enrollment.sh

In start_private_workerd_supervisor (:1976), beside the existing two exports that use the
split-literal naming idiom, add a third. AGORA_ORIGIN is a non-secret canonical constant,
so unlike the replay key it needs no private-fd handoff:

      agora_name="$(printf "%s" AGORA_ ORIGIN)"
      export "$agora_name=https://asimposium.org"

That is the whole shell change. CLOUDFLARE_INCLUDE_PROCESS_ENV=true already surfaces
process env as bindings, and --env-file still points at the private empty file, so no
.dev.vars or .env discovery is introduced.

--- PATCH 3: apps/wire/src/enrollment/local-d1-client.ts

No change. LOCAL_D1_EVIDENCE_CASES is untouched, every case name and its order is
preserved, and the ledger's order/completeness enforcement is unaffected.

INTERACTION WITH asimposiumorg-3ug6.1. That packet adds three `/__s1/local-only/*` routes
and one driver scenario. The two are orthogonal and commute: 3ug6.1 adds routes ABOVE the
fall-through, tyt3 replaces the fall-through itself. If 3ug6.1 lands first, apply tyt3
unchanged. If tyt3 lands first, 3ug6.1's insertion point moves but its content does not.
Neither renumbers the other's evidence cases.

WHAT AN ACCEPTANCE RUN MUST SHOW, since I can claim none of it: `--local-d1` green with all
declared cases completed in declared order; the mounted enrollment responses byte-identical
to the pre-migration run for every existing case; and an unknown /v1 path now returning the
canonical 404 without x-asimp-internal-router-miss, which is delta 1 made observable.

BOUNDARY. Source/static only. Everything above is read from the frozen bytes plus
infra/wrangler.toml; nothing was executed, nothing was written, and scoped git status on
these paths is clean. I assert the packet's construction is consistent with those bytes and
that I found no case whose bytes it changes - NOT that it runs. Workerd: no claim; this
migration is designed to make the local Workerd evidence mounted-production-faithful, but
until `--local-d1` executes there is no Workerd result to cite. Deployed: unclaimed, and
production import paths are untouched - src/index.ts does not import local-d1-worker.ts, and
neither patch modifies app.ts, router.ts, service.ts or infra/wrangler.toml. No stage,
commit, close, or forced lease.
